safi-cedvel:29-29.t:
* I'rab:
(قاتلوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). (الذين) a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (لا) negative. (يؤمنون) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); the wāw is the fāʿil. (بالله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (لا يؤمنون). (الواو) conjunction. (لا) redundant (zāʾida) to emphasise the negation. (باليوم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (لا يؤمنون) — conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the first prepositional phrase. (الآخر) a naʿt (adjective) of اليوم, genitive (majrūr). (الواو) conjunction. (لا يحرّمون) like لا يؤمنون. (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi. (حرّم) a past verb. (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative. (الواو) conjunction. (رسول) conjoined to the Name of Majesty, nominative, and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (الواو) conjunction. (لا يدينون) like لا يؤمنون. (دين) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb) [Note: Or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), since it is a maṣdar (verbal noun).], (الحقّ) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive [Note: This is if (الحقّ) is one of the names of Allah, or on the assumption of an omitted muḍāf, i.e. the religion of the people of truth.], (من) a preposition. (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive; [the phrase is] attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of يدينون. (أوتوا) a past verb, passive; the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (الكتاب) mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (حتّى) a particle of limit and a preposition. (يعطوا) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied (muḍmara) أن after حتّى, the sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil. (الجزية) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and the second object is omitted. (عن يد) a preposition and its genitive noun, a ḥāl of the fāʿil of يعطوا, i.e. submitting.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يعطوا ...) is in the position of genitive by (حتّى), attached to (قاتلوا).
(الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya). (هم) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). (صاغرون) khabar (predicate), nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw.
The clause «قاتلوا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «لا يؤمنون ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «لا يحرّمون ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «حرّم الله» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «لا يدينون ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause لا يؤمنون.
The clause «أوتوا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second relative (الذين).
The clause «يعطوا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the implied verbal relative particle (أن).
The clause «هم صاغرون» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.

* Morphology:
(الجزية): a noun for what is taken from the dhimmī, equivalent to the kharāj taken from the Muslim. It is derived from al-mujāzāh (requital) or from al-jazāʾ in the sense of settling [a debt]. Its pattern is فِعْلة, with kasra then sukūn. The plural is جِزًى, with kasra on the jīm and the short final alif, and جِزْي, keeping the yāʾ with sukūn on the zāy, and جِزاء.

* Rhetoric:
Kināya (metonymy): in His saying the Exalted عَنْ يَدٍ is a metonymy for submission, i.e. from a compliant hand, not a refusing one, because whoever refuses and resists does not give his hand, unlike the obedient, submissive one. Hence they said:
«أعطى بيده» (he gave with his hand) when someone submits. Do you not see their saying «نزع يده عن الطاعة» (he withdrew his hand from obedience), just as it is said:
«خلع ربقة الطاعة عن عنقه» (he threw off the noose of obedience from his neck)?

safi-cedvel:30-30.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive. (قالت) a past verb ... and (التاء) is for the feminine. (اليهود) fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ). (عزيز) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative [Note: عزيز comes with tanwīn because (ابن) is its khabar, and the alif is retained in it.] [Translator's note: the source writes عزيز here and in the note; the Quranic word is عزير.] (ابن) khabar (predicate), nominative. (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr). (الواو) conjunction. (قالت النصارى ... الله) like its counterpart before it. (ذلك) a demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ; (اللام) is for distance and (الكاف) for address. (قول) khabar, nominative, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (بأفواه) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of قول, whose governing agent is the demonstrative; and (هم) like the last. (يضاهئون) an imperfect verb, nominative ... the wāw is the fāʿil. (قول) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb). (الذين) a relative noun, muḍāf ilayhi, in the position of genitive. (كفروا) a past verb and its fāʿil. (من) a preposition. (قبل) a noun indeclinable on ḍamma, in the position of genitive, attached to (كفروا). (قاتل) a past verb, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative. (أنّى) an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as a ḥāl [Note: Or it is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to an omitted ḥāl.], (يؤفكون) an imperfect verb, nominative, passive; the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
The clause «قالت اليهود ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «عزير ابن الله» is in the position of accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «قالت النصارى ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause قالت اليهود.
The clause «المسيح ابن الله» is in the position of accusative as the maqūl al-qawl of the second verb of saying.
The clause «ذلك قولهم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يضاهئون ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the pronoun in قولهم or of القول, the referring pronoun (ʿāʾid) being omitted, i.e. يضاهئون به [Note: The clause may be resumptive.].
The clause «كفروا» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «قاتلهم الله ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يؤفكون» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the object of قاتلهم الله.

* Morphology:
(عزير): some prevent it from taking tanwīn because it is foreign; others hold that it is Arabic, and Ḥafṣ's reading is accordingly so, since it carries tanwīn. It is thus on the diminutive pattern فُعَيْل, with ḍamma on the fāʾ and fatḥa on the ʿayn.
(يضاهئون): the reading of Ḥafṣ keeps the hamza after the hāʾ, while the majority drop it (يضاهون). It contains iʿlāl (phonetic weakening) by dropping the yāʾ, its original form being يضاهيون. Retaining the hamza follows the dialect of Thaqīf. In al-Miṣbāḥ: ضاهأه مضاهأة, with hamza, means he matched and rivalled him; lightening [the hamza] is permitted, so one says ضاهيته مضاهاة, which is the resemblance of one thing to another.

* Rhetoric:
His saying the Exalted ذلِكَ قَوْلُهُمْ بِأَفْواهِهِمْ gives the impression [that it is redundant], since speech can only be with the mouth; so what is the point of mentioning their mouths?
I say there are two aspects to it. The first: what is meant is that it is a statement supported by no proof; it is nothing but a word they utter with their mouths, empty of any meaning beneath it, like meaningless words that are mere ringing and tones signifying no meanings. The second: what is meant by «قول» is doctrine, as in their saying «the qawl of Abū Ḥanīfa», meaning his doctrine and what he holds. It is as though it were said: that is their doctrine and their religion, with their mouths, not with their hearts.

* Benefits:
In this verse His saying the Exalted مِنْ قَبْلُ occurs, and in its i'rab it is said: a noun indeclinable on ḍamma, in the position of genitive by من.
We will now clarify the ruling on the two words قبل and بعد regarding indeclinability (bināʾ) and declension (iʿrāb):
1- If they are cut off from iḍāfa in wording but not in meaning, they are indeclinable on ḍamma, in the position of accusative as adverbs, as in our saying «جئت قبلُ وذهبت بعدُ» (I came before and went after), or in the position of genitive by a preposition, as in His saying the Exalted: لله الأمر من قبل ومن بعد. The meaning of being cut off from iḍāfa in wording is that no muḍāf ilayhi comes after them; the meaning of not being cut off in meaning is that a muḍāf ilayhi is implied after them, the implied form being: لله الأمر من قبل ذلك ومن بعد ذلك.
2- If they are cut off from iḍāfa in both wording and meaning (i.e. no muḍāf ilayhi comes after them and none can be implied after them), they are declinable, as in the poet's saying:
وساغ لي الشراب وكنت قبلا ... أكاد أغصّ بالماء الفرات
(Drink became easy for me to swallow, whereas before I would almost choke on fresh water.)
The evidence (shāhid) in it is قبلا, an adverb of time, accusative with fatḥa, because it is cut off from iḍāfa in both wording and meaning.

safi-cedvel:31-31.t:
* I'rab:
(اتّخذوا) a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). (أحبار) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (الواو) conjunction. (رهبان) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to أحبار, accusative, and (هم) like the first. (أربابا) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (من دون) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of (أربابا), (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr). (الواو) conjunction. (المسيح) conjoined to أحبار, accusative [Note: Or it is the mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb (اتّخذوا), the second object being omitted, its implied form being ربّا.], (ابن) a naʿt of المسيح, accusative. (مريم) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa, as it is a diptote. (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya). (أمروا) a past verb, passive, indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma; the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (إلّا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). (اللام) of cause (taʿlīl). (يعبدوا) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām; the wāw is the fāʿil. (إلها) mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (واحدا) a naʿt of (إلها), accusative. (لا) the lā of generic negation. (إله) the noun of lā, indeclinable on fatḥa, in the position of accusative. (إلّا) a particle of exception. (هو) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as a badal (substitute) of the pronoun concealed in the omitted khabar, its implied form being موجود [Note: Or a badal of the position of (لا and its noun), so it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ.]
, (سبحان) a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being سبّح, and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (عن) a preposition, and (ما) a maṣdar particle. (يشركون) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); the wāw is the fāʿil.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما يشركون) is in the position of genitive, attached to the maṣdar سبحان.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يعبدوا) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to (أمروا).
The clause «اتّخذوا ...» has no grammatical position, being in effect an explanation (taʿlīl) of what preceded.
The clause «ما أمروا ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).
The clause «يعبدوا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the implied verbal relative particle (أن).
The clause «لا إله إلّا هو» has no grammatical position: a resumption affirming tawḥīd [Note: Or in the position of accusative as a second naʿt of (إلها).
(2, 3) in the previous verse (31).] [Translator's note: the source merges two footnotes here; the second fragment, "(2, 3) in the previous verse (31)", belongs to the cross-references in the next entry.].
The clause «(سبّح) سبحانه ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يشركون» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the verbal relative particle (ما).

safi-cedvel:32-32.t:
* I'rab:
(يريدون) like يشركون «2», (أن) a maṣdar and subjunctive particle. (يطفئوا) like يعبدوا «3», (نور) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb). (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr). (بأفواههم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يطفئوا) ...
and (هم) muḍāf ilayhi. (الواو) conjunction. (يأبى) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif. (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil (agent), nominative. (إلّا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr) [Note: What permitted the "emptied" exception (al-istithnāʾ al-mufarragh) from an affirmative statement is that (يأبى) carries the meaning of negation, i.e.:
لا يريد (He does not want).] (أن) like the first. (يتمّ) an imperfect verb, accusative; its fāʿil is "huwa" (He). (نور) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يتمّ ...) is in the position of accusative as the mafʿūl bihi of the verb يأبى.
(الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya). (لو) a non-jussive conditional particle. (كره) a past verb. (الكافرون) a verb [Translator's note: so in the source, «فعل»; read «فاعل», fāʿil (agent)], nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw.
The clause «يريدون ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يطفئوا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the verbal relative particle (أن).
The clause «يأبى الله ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «يتمّ ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second verbal relative particle (أن).
The clause «لو كره الكافرون» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); the apodosis (jawāb) of (لو) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. «فالله متمّ نوره» (then Allah will complete His light).

* Rhetoric:
Istiʿāra (metaphor): in His saying the Exalted يُرِيدُونَ أَنْ يُطْفِؤُا نُورَ اللَّهِ بِأَفْواهِهِمْ, «light» is a primary, explicit metaphor (istiʿāra aṣliyya taṣrīḥiyya), and its annexation to Allah the Exalted is the contextual indicator (qarīna). What is meant by extinguishing is rejection and denial, i.e. the people of the two Books want to reject what indicates the oneness of Allah the Exalted and His transcendence above what they attributed to Him, glory be to Him, (بأفواههم), i.e. with their false sayings. It is also possible that the speech contains an allegorical metaphor (istiʿāra tamthīliyya), in that their state in trying to nullify his prophethood ﷺ by denial is likened to the state of someone who wants to blow out a great light spread across the horizons. His saying the Exalted وَيَأْبَى اللَّهُ إِلَّا أَنْ يُتِمَّ نُورَهُ would then be a tarshīḥ (reinforcement) of the metaphor, because completing the light is an increase in its brightness and the spreading of its radiance, so it is a derivation from the thing likened to (al-mushabbah bihi).

* Benefits:
His saying the Exalted: ذلِكَ قَوْلُهُمْ بِأَفْواهِهِمْ gives the impression [of redundancy], since speech can only be with the mouth; so what is the point of mentioning their mouths?
But the secret lies in the mouths: what they lament [Translator's note: so in the source, «تندبه»; perhaps «يدّعونه», what they claim] is nothing but a mere statement, paid no heed, supported by no proof and upheld by no argument. It is nothing but an empty word and nonsense with no substance beneath it, like meaningless words that are mere ringing and tones containing no meanings; and what has no meaning goes no further than the lips.

safi-cedvel:33-33.t:
* I'rab:
(هو) a detached pronoun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). (الذي) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate). (أرسل) a past verb; its fāʿil (agent) is "huwa" (He). (رسول) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (بالهدى) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أرسل) [Note: Or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of رسول, i.e. furnished with guidance.] (الواو) conjunction. (دين) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to الهدى, genitive (majrūr) like it. (الحقّ) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (اللام) of cause (taʿlīliyya). (يظهر) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām; its fāʿil is "huwa", and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (على الدين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يظهر), (كلّ) tawkīd (emphasis) of الدين, genitive like it, and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi. (ولو كره المشركون) like كره الكافرون [Note: In the previous verse (32).].
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يظهره ...) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to (أرسل).
The clause «هو الذي ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «أرسل ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذي).
The clause «يظهره ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the implied verbal relative particle (أن).
The clause «لو كره المشركون» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl ... and the apodosis (jawāb) of لو is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e.: «فسيظهر دين الحقّ على الدين كلّه» (then He will make the religion of truth prevail over all religion) [Note: Many grammarians tie the meaning of (لو) to the future in this verse; therefore the clause cannot be a ḥāl, and it is resumptive.].

safi-cedvel:1-1.t:
* I'rab:
(براءة) khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "هذه" [Note: Or it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is (إلى الذين عاهدتم), i.e. "a disavowal … reaching those who…"; this is the choice of Abū Ḥayyān in al-Baḥr al-Muḥīṭ. The more apparent view is that it is on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "ذات براءة".], (من الله) a preposition and its genitive noun, a naʿt (adjective) of براءة; (الواو) conjunction; (رسول) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the Name of Majesty, genitive (majrūr); (إلى) preposition; (الذين) relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of a genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (براءة); (عاهدتم) past verb, indeclinable on sukūn … and (تم) a pronoun, fāʿil (agent); (من المشركين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the omitted resumptive pronoun, i.e. "عاهدتموهم".
The clause «(هذه) براءة …» is a clause with no grammatical position, initial (ibtidāʾiyya).
The clause «عاهدتم …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).

* Morphology:
(براءة): an aural (samāʿī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the verb برأ يبرأ, of the فرح pattern, meaning to sever protection so that no tie or connection remains, or meaning to keep far apart; its wazn is فعالة with fatḥa on the fāʾ.

* Benefits:
The statements differ about the reason the basmala is not mentioned at the beginning of this sūra. Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥanafiyya said: I said to my father, meaning ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib: Why did you not write «بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم» in Barāʾa? He said: My son, Barāʾa was revealed with the sword (i.e. with mention of fighting and its rulings and threatening the polytheists with the sword if they did not return to the right path, which is Islam), and «بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم» is security.
Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna [Translator's note: the source prints "عينية"] was asked about this and said: Because the basmala is mercy, and mercy is security, and this sūra was revealed concerning the hypocrites. It was also said: The Companions differed over al-Anfāl and Barāʾa, whether they are two sūras or one sūra; so they left a gap between them, as an indication for whoever says they are two sūras, and they did not mention the basmala, as an indication for whoever says they are one sūra.

safi-cedvel:2-2.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) conjunction, to link the cause with the effect; (سيحوا) imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn … and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (في الأرض) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (سيحوا); (أربعة) adverb of time, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (سيحوا); (أشهر) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (الواو) conjunction; (اعلموا) like سيحوا; (أنّ) a particle resembling the verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) — and (كم) a pronoun in the position of an accusative, the noun of أنّ; (غير) khabar (predicate) of أنّ, nominative (marfūʿ); (معجزي) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ, and the nūn was dropped because of the iḍāfa; (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّكم غير …) is in the position of an accusative, standing in place of the two objects of اعلموا.
(الواو) conjunction; (أنّ الله مخزي الكافرين) like أنّكم غير …, and the sign of the genitive in (الكافرين) is the yāʾ.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ الله مخزي) is in the position of an accusative, maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the first interpreted maṣdar.
The clause «سيحوا …» is a clause with no grammatical position, conjoined to the initial clause [Note: It may be the speech (maqūl al-qawl) of an omitted verb of saying, i.e. "So say to them: travel freely in the land."].
The clause «اعلموا …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause سيحوا.

* Morphology:
(مخزي): active participle from the quadriliteral أخزى; its wazn is مفعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn. [Translator's note: the source prints the wazn as "مفعول"; with "ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn" the pattern described is مُفْعِل.]

* Rhetoric:
Explicit mention (al-iẓhār): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ مُخْزِي الْكافِرِينَ», where He mentioned the Majestic Name explicitly [Translator's note: i.e. instead of a pronoun] to instil awe and to magnify the matter of al-ikhzāʾ, which is humiliation that carries disgrace and shame.

safi-cedvel:3-3.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction; (أذان) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ) [Note: Or it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هذا أذان …" or "هذه الآيات أذان", and (من الله، إن الناس) [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably (من الله، إلى الناس)] are both attached to أذان.] (من الله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of (أذان); (الواو) conjunction; (رسول) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the Name of Majesty, genitive (majrūr), and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (إلى الناس) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; (يوم) adverb of time, accusative (manṣūb), attached to the omitted khabar; (الحجّ) muḍāf ilayhi; (الأكبر) naʿt of الحجّ, genitive; (أنّ) a particle resembling the verb — an abrogator (nāsikh); (الله) the Name of Majesty, the noun of أنّ, accusative; (بريء) khabar, nominative; (من المشركين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (بريء); (الواو) conjunction; (رسول) mubtadaʾ, nominative, and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi.. and the khabar is omitted, its implied form being "بريء" [Note: (رسول) may be maʿṭūf to the latent pronoun in (بريء), which is in the position of a nominative because it is the fāʿil (agent) of the adjective بريء; what licenses this conjoining is that it has been separated by His saying من المشركين.]. The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ الله بريء) is in the position of a genitive by an omitted preposition, namely the bāʾ, attached to a naʿt of (أذان) [Note: The interpreted maṣdar may be the khabar of أذان, with (إلى الناس) attached to أذان.]; (الفاء) resumptive; (إن) a jussive conditional particle; (تبتم) past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, in the position of a jussive, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) … and (تم) a pronoun, fāʿil; (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (هو) detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of a nominative, mubtadaʾ, i.e. the repentance; (خير) khabar, nominative; (اللام) preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (خير); (الواو) conjunction; (إن تولّيتم) like إن تبتم; (الفاء) linking the apodosis; (اعلموا أنّكم غير معجزي الله) its i'rab has already passed [Note: In the previous verse.]; (الواو) resumptive; (بشّر) imperative verb, and the fāʿil is "أنت"; (الذين) اسم الذين آمنوا و (نصروا) معطوف على (آووا) ويعربان مثل كفروا (أولئك) موصول مبنيّ في محلّ نصب مفعول به [Translator's note: this passage is garbled in the source, apparently mixing in material from the i'rab of another verse (cf. 8:72–74, «الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا … وَالَّذِينَ آوَوْا وَنَصَرُوا أُولئِكَ»); it is left in Arabic as printed. Literally: "(الذين) the noun of الذين آمنوا, and (نصروا) is conjoined to (آووا), and both are parsed like كفروا; (أولئك) a relative, indeclinable, in the position of an accusative, mafʿūl bihi (direct object)". The intended sense here is evidently: (الذين) relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of an accusative, mafʿūl bihi.]; (كفروا) past verb, indeclinable on ḍamma.. and the wāw is the fāʿil; (بعذاب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (بشّر) [Note: The verb was used by way of mockery of them.]; (أليم) naʿt of عذاب, genitive like it.
The clause «أذان من الله …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the initial clause.
The clause «رسوله (بريء)» is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the khabar بريء.
The clause «إن تبتم …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «هو خير لكم» is in the position of a jussive, the apodosis of the second condition [Translator's note: so in the source; it is in fact the apodosis of the first condition, إن تبتم], joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «إن تولّيتم» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause تبتم.
The clause «اعلموا …» is in the position of a jussive, the apodosis of the second condition, joined with the fāʾ.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّكم غير معجزي الله) is in the position of an accusative, standing in place of the two objects of اعلموا.
The clause «بشّر …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «كفروا» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).

* Morphology:
(أذان): an aural (samāʿī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the verb أذن يأذن, of the فرح pattern; its wazn is فعال with fatḥa on the fāʾ. There are other aural maṣdars: إذن with kasra on the hamza and sukūn on the dhāl, أذن with fatḥa on the hamza and sukūn on the dhāl, and أذانة with fatḥa on the hamza.. Or it is a noun of maṣdar (ism maṣdar) from the quadriliteral آذن فلانا الأمر وبالأمر, meaning he informed him of it.

* Benefits:
1- His saying, the Exalted: أَنَّ اللَّهَ بَرِيءٌ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ وَرَسُولُهُ — the grammarians' statements on the i'rab of the word رسوله diverge into several views. Abū al-Baqāʾ al-ʿUkbarī [Translator's note: the source prints "البكري"] mentioned them in his book Iʿrāb al-Qurʾān, saying: It is read with the nominative, and there are three views on it:
1- It is maʿṭūf to the pronoun in بريء, and what lies between them functions like a tawkīd (emphasis); hence the conjoining is permissible.
2- It is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "ورسوله بريء".
3- It is conjoined to the position of the mubtadaʾ, and according to the verifying scholars this is not permissible, because (أنّ with fatḥa) has a position other than that of the mubtadaʾ, unlike the one with kasra. It is also read with the accusative, conjoined to the noun of أنّ.
2- The reason for the founding of the science of grammar:
A man was brought to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, who was reading «أَنَّ اللَّهَ بَرِيءٌ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ وَرَسُولُهُ» with the genitive [Translator's note: i.e. ورسولِه]. He questioned him, and he said: This is how I read it in Medina. ʿUmar said: It is not so; it is only ورسولُه with ḍamma on the lām, for Allah does not disavow His Messenger. Then he ordered that none should recite the Qur'an except one knowledgeable in Arabic, and he summoned Abū al-Aswad al-Duʾalī and ordered him to lay down grammar.

safi-cedvel:4-4.t:
* I'rab:
(إلّا) particle of exception; (الذين) a relative in the position of an accusative by way of connected exception [Note: The one from which the exception is made is His saying (الذين عاهدتم من المشركين) in the first verse — according to the view of al-Zajjāj. Some make the one from which the exception is made omitted, the implied form being: "Kill the polytheists who have a treaty, except those with whom you made a treaty …". According to Abū Ḥayyān it is a disconnected exception because of the remoteness of the one from which the exception is made, with (إلّا) meaning "but" (لكن), and the relative is in the position of a nominative, a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is the clause أتمّوا.], (عاهدتم من المشركين) its i'rab has already passed [Note: In verse (1).]; (ثمّ) conjunction; (لم) particle of negation, jussive and conversion (qalb); (ينقصوا) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn … the wāw is the fāʿil (agent) and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (شيئا) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb) [Note: Or it is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar.]; (الواو) conjunction; (لم يظاهروا) like لم ينقصوا; (على) preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يظاهروا); (أحدا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition; (أتمّوا) imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn … and the wāw is the fāʿil; (إلى) preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to the verb (أتمّوا); (عهد) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (إلى مدّة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of عهدهم [Note: Or attached to (أتمّوا), the preposition إلى having the meaning of the end-limit (intihāʾ al-ghāya).], and (هم) like the previous; (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb — an abrogator (nāsikh); (الله) the Name of Majesty, the noun of إنّ, accusative; (يحبّ) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the fāʿil is "هو"; (المتقين) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ.
The clause «عاهدتم …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «لم ينقصوكم …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «لم يظاهروا …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «أتمّوا …» is in the position of a jussive, the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e. "if they have done that, then fulfil …".
The clause «إنّ الله يحبّ …» has no grammatical position, causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «يحبّ المتّقين» is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of إنّ.

safi-cedvel:34-34.t:
* I'rab:
(يأيّها الذين آمنوا) its i'rab has already been given [Note: In verse (23).], (انّ) a particle resembling the verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) — (كثيرا) the noun of inna, accusative (manṣūb). (من الأحبار) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of (كثيرا). (الواو) conjunction. (الرهبان) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to الأحبار, genitive (majrūr). (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis. (يأكلون) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) ... and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). (أموال) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative. (الناس) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive. (بالباطل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of يأكلون or of its object, i.e. being involved (in the plural or the singular) in falsehood. (الواو) conjunction. (يصدّون) like يأكلون. (عن سبيل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يصدّون). (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. the path of the religion of Allah. (الواو) conjunction. (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). (يكنزون) like يأكلون. (الذهب) mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (الفضّة) conjoined by the wāw to الذهب, accusative like it. (الواو) conjunction. (لا) negative. (ينفقون) like يأكلون, and (ها) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi [Note: The pronoun refers back to the treasures implied in His words (يكنزونها) [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has يكنزون], or to the kinds of gold and silver, or to silver as a symbol of wealth.. etc.]. (في سبيل الله) like عن سبيل الله, attached to (ينفقون). (الفاء) redundant (zāʾida), because the relative resembles the conditional. (بشّر) an imperative verb, its fāʿil being "you", and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (بعذاب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (بشّر). (أليم) a naʿt of عذاب, genitive.
The clause «يأيّها الذين ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «إنّ كثيرا ... ليأكلون» has no grammatical position: the response to the vocative.
The clause «يأكلون ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of inna.
The clause «يصدّون» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause يأكلون.
The clause «الذين يكنزون ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the response to the vocative.
The clause «يكنزون ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second relative (الذين).
The clause «لا ينفقونها ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يكنزون.
The clause «بشّرهم ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين).

* Rhetoric:
1- His saying, the Exalted: إِنَّ كَثِيراً مِنَ الْأَحْبارِ وَالرُّهْبانِ لَيَأْكُلُونَ أَمْوالَ النَّاسِ بِالْباطِلِ — expressing taking by eating is a majāz mursal (metonymic trope), the relation being that of cause and effect, or of concomitant and what it entails, since eating entails taking, as has been said. It has also been allowed that what is meant by "wealth" is the foods that are eaten, as a majāz mursal. Of this kind is the saying:
يأكلن كل ليلة أكافا (they eat every night a pack-saddle). For he means fodder bought with the price of a pack-saddle. This was chosen by the learned al-Ṭībī, and it is one of two views mentioned by al-Zamakhsharī; the second of them is that eating is borrowed (istiʿāra) for taking, on the basis that their state in taking people's wealth without distinguishing between right and falsehood, or separating the lawful from the unlawful, is likened to the state of an exhausted, hungry man who does not distinguish between one food and another in what he takes.
2- The singular pronoun: in His saying, the Exalted: يُنْفِقُونَها although two things were mentioned, namely gold and silver; the pronoun goes to the meaning rather than the wording, because each of them is a full sum and a great number, dinars and dirhams.

safi-cedvel:35-35.t:
* I'rab:
(يوم) an adverb of time, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb indicated by عذاب — in the previous verse — i.e. they will be punished on the day ... [Note: It may be attached to (أليم) in the sense of "painful" — in the previous verse.] (يحمى) an imperfect verb, passive, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the alif, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "it", i.e. the fuel [Note: This is if it is the imperfect of the quadriliteral أحمي; if it is the imperfect of the triliteral حمي, then the prepositional phrase (عليها) is the nāʾib fāʿil.] (على) a preposition and (ها) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (يحمى). (في نار) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يحمى). (جهنّم) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa [Translator's note: i.e. as a diptote]. (الفاء) conjunction. (تكوى) like يحمى. (بها) like عليها, attached to (تكوى). (جباه) nāʾib fāʿil, nominative, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (الواو) conjunction in both places. (جنوبهم، ظهورهم) two nouns conjoined by the two conjunctions to جباههم.. annexed to the third-person pronoun (هم). (ها) a particle of alerting. (ذا) a demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate). (كنزتم) a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn, and (تم) a pronoun, fāʿil (agent). (لأنفس) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of كنزتم or of its object. (الفاء) for linking the apodosis of an implied condition. (ذوقوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil. (ما) a relative, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. the recompense of what you were ... (كنتم) a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb ...
and (ثم) [Translator's note: so in the source; i.e. (تم)] the noun of kāna. (تكنزون) an imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The clause «يحمى عليها ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «تكوى.. جباههم» is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause يحمى عليها.
The clause «هذا ما كنزتم» is in the position of nominative as nāʾib fāʿil of an implied verb, implied as "it is said", i.e. it will be said to them: this is what you hoarded [Note: The reference here is to the branding.
The fāʾ may be a conjunction linking the effect to the cause, and the clause ذوقوا conjoined to] [Translator's note: the note breaks off here in the source; its remainder appears to be in the next note].
The clause «كنزتم ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the first relative (ما).
The clause «ذوقوا ...» is in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e. if you hoarded and did not spend, then taste [Note: the clause هذا ما كنزتم, which is part of the speech said to them.].
The clause «كنتم تكنزون» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second relative (ما) [Note: (ما) may be maṣdariyya (infinitival) ... and the clause is the ṣila of the particle relative (ما).] The clause «تكنزون» is in the position of accusative as the khabar of kuntum.

* Morphology:
(يحمى): it has iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by conversion, to suit the passive form; its origin is يحمي — the yāʾ was voweled after a fatḥa and was converted into an alif.
(تكوى): it has iʿlāl by conversion, following the course of (يحمى).
(جباه): plural of جبهة, the name of the well-known part of the body (the forehead); its pattern is فعلة with fatḥa then sukūn.

* Rhetoric:
1- His saying, the Exalted: فَتُكْوى بِها جِباهُهُمْ وَجُنُوبُهُمْ وَظُهُورُهُمْ — these were singled out for mention because the aim of the hoarders in hoarding and amassing is to have standing and leadership among people by means of wealth, and to enjoy delicious foods and splendid clothes. So for their standing, the branding was on their foreheads; for the filling of their sides (bellies) with food, they were branded on them; and for what they wore on their backs, these were branded. Or because when they saw the poor beggar they knitted the space between their eyes, turned aside from him, shunned him, turned their backs to him and faced another direction.

* Benefits:
The severity of the threat to whoever withholds zakāt:
This verse contains a threat and warning to those who hoard gold and silver and do not pay their zakāt. The commentators' views have differed concerning the meaning of the hoarding that necessitates this punishment, but the soundest of them is what Ibn ʿImrān [Translator's note: so in the source; this saying is well known from Ibn ʿUmar] said: All wealth whose zakāt has been paid is not a hoard, and hoarding it is not forbidden to its owner, even if it is much. And all wealth whose zakāt has not been paid, its owner is punished for it, for withholding zakāt, by the threat from Allah. Evidence of that is what
was narrated from Abū Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "There is no owner of gold or silver who does not pay what is due on it (i.e. zakāt) but that, when the Day of Resurrection comes, it will be made into plates of fire for him, which will be heated in the fire of Hell, and his forehead, his side and his back will be branded with them. Whenever they cool, they will be returned to him, on a day whose length is fifty thousand years, until judgement is passed among the servants, and he will see his way, either to Paradise or to the Fire." It was said: O Messenger [of Allah], and camels? He said: "Nor an owner of camels who does not pay what is due on them — and part of what is due on them is milking them on the day they come to water — but that, when the Day of Resurrection comes, he will be thrown down on his face for them on a vast level plain, they being as plentiful as they ever were, not missing a single young one of them; they will trample him with their hooves and bite him with their mouths. Whenever the first of them passes over him, the last of them is returned to him, on a day whose length is fifty thousand years, until judgement is passed among the servants, and he will see his way, either to Paradise or to the Fire." And likewise cattle and sheep,
as has come in this sound (ṣaḥīḥ) ḥadīth.

safi-cedvel:36-36.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّ) a particle resembling the verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) — (عدّة) the noun of inna, accusative (manṣūb). (الشهور) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr). (عند) an adverb, accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) عدّة, for it is a maṣdar (verbal noun). (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (اثنا) the khabar (predicate) of inna, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the alif, because it is treated like the dual. (عشر) a numeral word, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, with no grammatical position. (شهرا) tamyīz (specification), accusative. (في كتاب) a preposition and its genitive noun, a naʿt (adjective) of (اثنا عشر). (الله) like the first. (يوم) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to what the prepositional phrase (في كتاب) is attached to [Note: Or attached to الكتاب if it is taken as a maṣdar ... or attached to an omitted verb, implied as "that was written on the day He created.."], namely the sense of being established. (خلق) a past verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is "He". (السموات) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative, the sign of the accusative being the kasra. (الواو) conjunction. (الأرض) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to السموات, accusative. (من) a preposition and (ها) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to an omitted fronted khabar. (أربعة) a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative. (حرم) a naʿt of أربعة, nominative. (ذلك) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ..
the lām is for distance and (الكاف) for address, and the reference is to the prohibition. (الدين) the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, nominative. (القيّم) a naʿt of الدين, nominative. (الفاء) resumptive [Note: Or linking the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. if you are in them, then do not wrong..]. (لا) the prohibitive lā, causing the jussive. (تظلموا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil. (في) a preposition and (هنّ) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (تظلموا). (أنفس) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (الواو) conjunction. (قاتلوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil. (المشركين) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ. (كافّة) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun of the fāʿil or of المشركين, accusative. (الكاف) a preposition. (ما) an infinitival (maṣdariyya) particle. (يقاتلون) an imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (كم) in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi. (كافّة) like the first. (الواو) conjunction. (اعلموا) like قاتلوا. (أنّ الله) like إنّ عدّة. (مع) an adverb, accusative, attached to the omitted khabar of anna. (المتّقين) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
The clause «إنّ عدّة الشهور ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «خلق ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «منها أربعة حرم» is in the position of nominative as a naʿt of «اثنا عشر» [Note: Or resumptive, with no grammatical position.].
The clause «ذلك الدين ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «لا تظلموا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «قاتلوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause لا تظلموا ...
The clause «يقاتلونكم ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (ما).
The clause «اعلموا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause لا تظلموا ...
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ الله مع المتّقين) is in the position of accusative, taking the place of the two objects of اعلموا.

* Morphology:
(القيّم): a ṣifa mushabbaha (assimilated adjective) meaning "upright", derived from قام يقوم; so it has iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by conversion. Its origin is قيوم, on the pattern فيعل with kasra on the ʿayn; when the yāʾ and the wāw came together, the first of them having sukūn, the wāw was converted into a yāʾ, then the two yāʾs were assimilated because the first had sukūn, so it is (قيّم).

* Benefits:
In this verse occurs His saying, the Exalted: إِنَّ عِدَّةَ الشُّهُورِ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ اثْنا عَشَرَ شَهْراً. The i'rab of the word اثنا عشر is as follows: اثنا: the khabar of inna, nominative by the alif because it is treated like the dual; عشر: a part indeclinable on the fatḥa, with no grammatical position.
Here we shall explain an aspect of the i'rab of the compound numbers from eleven to nineteen, and we say:
1- The numbers from أحد عشر to تسعة عشر are indeclinable on the fatḥa of both parts, in the position of nominative, accusative or genitive. As when we say: جاء خمسة عشر رجلا (fifteen men came), and I say in its i'rab: خمسة عشر is indeclinable on the fatḥa of both parts, in the position of nominative as fāʿil. And His saying, the Exalted: إِنِّي رَأَيْتُ أَحَدَ عَشَرَ كَوْكَباً — أحد عشر: indeclinable on the fatḥa of both parts, in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi.
2- As for the number (اثنا عشر), its first part is declined as the dual is declined — by the alif in the nominative, and by the yāʾ in the accusative and genitive — and its second part is indeclinable on the fatḥa, with no grammatical position. Whoever wants further explanation should refer to the books of grammar. I have explained this because it is liable to be overlooked and forgotten, and Allah grants success.

safi-cedvel:5-5.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive; (إذا) an adverb of future time containing the meaning of condition, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of an accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the content of the apodosis; (انسلخ) past verb; (الأشهر) fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ); (الحرم) naʿt (adjective) of الأشهر, nominative; (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (اقتلوا) imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn … and the wāw is the fāʿil; (المشركين) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ; (حيث) adverb of place, indeclinable on ḍamma, in the position of an accusative, attached to (اقتلوا); (وجدتم) like عاهدتم [Note: In the previous verse (4).], and (الواو) is a vowel of lengthening (ishbāʿ) of the mīm, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (الواو) conjunction in the three places; (خذوهم، احصروهم، اقعدوا) like اقتلوا; (اللام) preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (اقعدوا); (كلّ) adverb of place standing in for the mafʿūl fīhi (adverbial), accusative, attached to (اقعدوا) [Note: Or it is accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "في كلّ مرصد" or "على كلّ مرصد".] (مرصد) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr). (الفاء) conjunction; (إن) a jussive conditional particle; (تابوا) past verb, indeclinable on ḍamma, in the position of a jussive, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) … and the wāw is the fāʿil; (الواو) conjunction in the two places; (أقاموا، آتوا) like تابوا and conjoined to it; (الصلاة، الزكاة) each of them a mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الفاء) linking the apodosis; (خلّوا) like اقتلوا; (سبيل) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (إنّ الله) its i'rab has already passed [Note: In the previous verse (4).] (غفور) khabar (predicate) of إنّ, nominative; (رحيم) second khabar, nominative.
The clause «انسلخ الأشهر …» is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi … and the condition, its verb and its apodosis form a resumptive statement to which what follows is conjoined.
The clause «اقتلوا …» has no grammatical position, the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «وجدتموهم» is in the position of a genitive by the annexation of (حيث) to it.
The clause «خذوهم» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the apodosis clause.
The clause «احصروهم» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the apodosis clause.
The clause «اقعدوا …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the apodosis clause.
The clause «إن تابوا» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «أقاموا …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause تابوا.
The clause «آتوا …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause تابوا.
The clause «خلّوا …» is in the position of a jussive, the apodosis of the condition, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «إنّ الله غفور …» has no grammatical position, causal (taʿlīliyya).

* Morphology:
(مرصد): noun of place from the verb رصد يرصد, of the نصر pattern; its wazn is مفعل with fatḥa on the mīm and the ʿayn.

* Benefits:
A benefit concerning the word (كل): His saying, the Exalted, occurs in the verse: وَاقْعُدُوا لَهُمْ كُلَّ مَرْصَدٍ.
The statements on its i'rab diverge into these views:
1- An adverb of place.
2- Standing in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), with the implied form "وارصدوهم كلّ مرصد".
3- Accusative by removal of the preposition, the implied form being "واقعدوا لهم بكل مرصد". Al-Zajjāj and al-ʿUkbarī preferred that it is an adverb of place. The word كل is a declinable noun according to its position in the sentence, but it sometimes comes as a tawkīd (emphasis), on condition that it is preceded by the thing emphasised and contains a pronoun referring back to it, as in His saying, the Exalted: فسجد الملائكة كلّهم أجمعون. Sometimes it acquires its i'rab from the noun to which it is annexed: if it is annexed to an adverb it is parsed as an adverb, e.g. سأزورك كلّ صباح ("I will visit you every morning"), سرت كلّ الأميال ("I travelled all the miles"). If it is annexed to a maṣdar (verbal noun) from the root of the verb, it is parsed as standing in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq, as in His saying, the Exalted: فَلا تَمِيلُوا كُلَّ الْمَيْلِ

safi-cedvel:6-6.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction; (إن) like the previous; (أحد) fāʿil (agent) of an omitted verb explained by the verb استجارك; (من المشركين) a preposition and its genitive noun, a naʿt (adjective) of أحد, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ; (استجار) past verb, and (الكاف) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو"; (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (أجره) imperative verb and its object, and the fāʿil is "أنت"; (حتّى) particle of end-limit and preposition; (يسمع) imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after حتّى, and the fāʿil is "هو"; (كلام) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يسمع) is in the position of a genitive by (حتّى), attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أجره).
(ثمّ) conjunction; (أبلغه) like أجره; (مأمنه) accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e.:
"إلى مأمنه". And (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (ذلك) demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of a nominative, mubtadaʾ (subject), the reference being to the two matters mentioned.. and (اللام) is for distance and (الكاف) for address; (الباء) preposition of causation; (أنّ) a particle resembling the verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) — and (هم) a pronoun in the position of an accusative, the noun of أنّ; (قوم) khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ); (لا) negative; (يعلمون) imperfect verb, nominative … and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّهم قوم …) is in the position of a genitive by the bāʾ, attached to the omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ ذلك.
The clause «(استجارك) أحد..» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause إن تابوا.
The overt clause «استجارك» has no grammatical position, explicative (tafsīriyya).
The clause «أجره» is in the position of a jussive (majzūm), the apodosis of the condition, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «يسمع …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle-relative (أن).
The clause «أبلغه …» is in the position of a jussive, conjoined to the apodosis clause.
The clause «ذلك بأنّهم …» has no grammatical position, causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «لا يعلمون» is in the position of a nominative, a naʿt of قوم.

* Morphology:
(أجره): it contains a weak-letter change by deletion (iʿlāl bi-l-ḥadhf) owing to the indeclinability on sukūn; its original form is أجيره, and when two quiescent letters met the yāʾ was deleted; its wazn is أفله.
(مأمن): noun of place from أمن يأمن, of the فرح pattern; its wazn is مفعل with fatḥa on the mīm and the ʿayn. It may also be a mīmī maṣdar of the said verb, i.e. "convey him to his security".

* Benefits:
The intelligence and acumen of Wāṣil ibn ʿAṭāʾ:
Al-Mubarrad mentioned in his book al-Kāmil, in the chapter on the Khārijites, that Wāṣil ibn ʿAṭāʾ was with a group of his companions, and they found that they had fallen into the territory of the Khārijites; at that they were certain of destruction. Wāṣil said to them: Do not say anything; I will argue on your behalf. The Khārijites asked them: Who are you? Wāṣil said: Unbelievers seeking safe-conduct; we wish to hear the speech of Allah. So the Khārijites took them and recited to them something of the Qur'an.
After that Wāṣil said: We want you to convey us to our place of safety. The Khārijites were about to fall upon them, but Wāṣil recited this verse to them, so they granted his request and conveyed them to their place of safety.

safi-cedvel:7-7.t:
* I'rab:
(كيف) interrogative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of an accusative, the khabar (predicate) of يكون, placed first because of its right to the head of the clause [Note: It may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) of عهد if (يكون) is parsed as a complete verb, or if it is parsed as incomplete with the khabar being (للمشركين) or (عند الله).], (يكون) incomplete imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); (للمشركين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl of (عهد) — an adjective that has been placed before the noun it qualifies; (عهد) the noun of the incomplete يكون, nominative [Note: Or the fāʿil (agent) of the complete (يكون).], (عند) adverb, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (عهد) [Note: Or attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of عهد.] (الله) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (الواو) conjunction; (عند رسوله) like the first and conjoined to it, and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi; (إلّا الذين عاهدتم) like the earlier [Note: In verse (4) of this sūra.], (عند المسجد) like عند الله, attached to (عاهدتم); (الحرام) naʿt of المسجد, genitive; (الفاء) resumptive; (ما) a maṣdar-forming adverbial particle containing the meaning of condition [Note: Or it is a jussive conditional noun in the position of an accusative as an adverb of time — this is the choice of al-ʿUkbarī — or it is a conditional noun in the position of a nominative, a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar is the clause استقاموا, the implied form being: "At whatever time they are upright toward you, be upright toward them" — this is the choice of al-Ḥarfī [Translator's note: so in the source; possibly al-Ḥawfī].], (استقاموا) past verb, indeclinable on ḍamma.. and the wāw is the fāʿil; (اللام) preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (استقاموا); (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (استقيموا) imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil; (لهم) like لكم, attached to (استقيموا).
The interpreted maṣdar (ما استقاموا لكم) is in the position of an accusative as an adverb of time, attached to (استقيموا). (إنّ الله يحبّ المتّقين) its i'rab has already passed [Note: In verse (4) of this sūra.].
The clause «يكون للمشركين عهد …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «عاهدتم» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «استقاموا …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle-relative (ما).
The clause «استقيموا …» has no grammatical position, the apodosis of a non-jussive condition [Note: Or it is in the position of a jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis of the jussive conditional (ما), because it is joined with the fāʾ. According to Ibn Mālik, the temporal maṣdar-forming (ما) can be a jussive conditional.].
The clause «انّ الله يحبّ …» has no grammatical position, causal (taʿlīliyya) or in its status.
The clause «يحبّ المتّقين» is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of أنّ [Translator's note: so in the source, i.e. إنّ].

* Rhetoric:
1- Repetition (al-takrīr): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «وَعِنْدَ رَسُولِهِ»; the word عند is repeated to signal that it [Translator's note: i.e. the covenant] carries no weight with either of them, each taken separately.
2- The device of rectification (al-istidrāk): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «إِلَّا الَّذِينَ عاهَدْتُمْ عِنْدَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرامِ»; the statement makes a rectification of the negation understood from the interrogative, whose immediate sense covers all those holding a covenant.

safi-cedvel:8-8.t:
* I'rab:
(كيف) like the earlier [Note: In the previous verse 7.], and what is asked about is omitted, indicated by what was mentioned, i.e. "how can they have a covenant", and it is a repetition to express how unlikely it is that they would keep to the covenant; (الواو) conjunction; (إنّ) [Translator's note: so in the source, with shadda; the particle is إنْ] a jussive conditional particle; (يظهروا) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (على) preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يظهروا); (لا) negative; (يرقبوا) like يظهروا, the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (فيكم) like عليكم, attached to (يرقبوا); (إلّا) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (الواو) conjunction; (ذمّة) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to (إلّا), accusative, and (لا) is redundant (zāʾida) to reinforce the negation. (يرضون) like يعلمون [Note: In verse (6) of this sūra.], and (كم) mafʿūl bihi; (بأفواه) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يرضون), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الواو) conjunction — or circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (تأبى) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif; (قلوب) fāʿil, nominative, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) conjunction; (أكثر) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative, and (هم) like the last; (فاسقون) khabar (predicate), nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw.
The clause «كيف وما تعلّقت به …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يظهروا عليكم» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause [Note: The clause headed by the interrogative that precedes is declarative in meaning, because the interrogative has the meaning of negation …
Abū Ḥayyān, however, made the clause يظهروا a ḥāl (circumstantial), because the condition has departed from its meaning and the wāw before the clause is circumstantial.].
The clause «يرقبوا» has no grammatical position, the apodosis of a jussive condition not joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «يرضونكم» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «تأبى قلوبهم» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يرضونكم [Note: It may be in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl.].
The clause «أكثرهم فاسقون» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يرضونكم.

* Morphology:
(إلّا): a noun meaning covenant or kinship; its plural is إلال, like قدح and قداح; its wazn is فعل with kasra on the fāʾ.
(ذمّة): a noun meaning covenant or guarantee! Some said: it was called ذمّة because every sanctity whose neglect brings you blame (الذّم) is called ذمّة. Al-Azharī said: الذمّة is security (al-amān). Its wazn is فعلة with kasra on the fāʾ; its ʿayn and lām come from a single letter.
(تأبى): it contains a weak-letter change by conversion (iʿlāl bi-l-qalb): the alif is converted from a yāʾ, because it is from أبى يأبى of the فتح pattern, and the yāʾ returns when it is attributed to the first-person pronoun in the past: أبيت … so when the yāʾ came voweled after a fatḥa it was converted to an alif.

safi-cedvel:65-65.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (اللام) the lām that prepares for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa lil-qasam); (إن) a conditional particle that makes the verb jussive (majzūm); (سألت) past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) ... and (التاء) is the fāʿil (agent), and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the second object is omitted, i.e. "about their mocking of you"; (اللام) the lām of the oath; (يقولنّ) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), its sign of nominative being the presence of the nūn, which has been dropped because of the succession of identical letters ... and the waw, dropped because of the meeting of two sukūns, is the fāʿil.. and (النون) is the nūn of emphasis; (إنّما) a restraining particle and the restrained one (kāffa wa-makfūfa); (كنّا) defective past verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) — and (نا) a pronoun in the position of nominative as the subject (ism) of kāna; (نخوض) imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is "naḥnu"; (الواو) conjunction; (نلعب) like نخوض; (قل) imperative verb, and the fāʿil is "anta"; (الهمزة) for the rebuking, disapproving interrogative; (بالله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تستهزئون); (الواو) conjunction in both places; (آيات)، (رسول) both conjoined (maʿṭūf) by the two conjunctions to the Divine Name, genitive (majrūr) like it, and (الهاء) in both is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (كنتم) like كنّا; (تستهزئون) imperfect verb, nominative ... and the waw is the fāʿil.
The clause «إن سألتهم ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يقولنّ ...» has no grammatical position, as the answer to the implied oath; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by the answer of the oath.
The clause «كنّا نخوض ...» is in the position of accusative (manṣūb) as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «نخوض ...» is in the position of accusative as the khabar (predicate) of كنّا.
The clause «نلعب» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause نخوض.
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «كنتم تستهزئون» is in the position of accusative as the object of speech.
The clause «تستهزئون» is in the position of accusative as the khabar of كنتم.

* Benefits:
The frivolity of the hypocrites:
Ibn Isḥāq said: A group of the hypocrites, among them Wadīʿa ibn Thābit and a man from Ashjaʿ called Makhshin ibn Ḥumayyir, were pointing at the Messenger ﷺ while he was setting out for Tabūk, and some of them said to others: "Do you reckon fighting the Banū al-Aṣfar (i.e. the Byzantines) to be like the Arabs fighting one another? By Allah, it is as though we already see you tomorrow bound together in ropes" — spreading alarm and terror among the believers. Makhshin said: "By Allah, I would love to agree to a settlement in which each man of us is given a hundred lashes, if only we could escape having Qur'an revealed about us for this talk of yours." And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said — according to what has reached me — to ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir:
"Catch up with the people, for they have burned themselves; ask them about what they said, and if they deny it, say: 'Indeed, you said such-and-such.'" So ʿAmmār went to them and said that to them, and they came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ apologizing to him. Wadīʿa said:
"O Messenger of Allah, we were only chatting idly and playing." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: وَلَئِنْ سَأَلْتَهُمْ لَيَقُولُنَّ إِنَّما كُنَّا نَخُوضُ وَنَلْعَبُ. Makhshin ibn Ḥumayyir said: "O Messenger of Allah, my name and my father's name held me back." The one who was pardoned in this verse was Makhshin; he took the name ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, and asked Allah to be killed as a martyr in a place where no one would know of him. He was killed on the day of al-Yamāma fighting the apostates, and no trace of him was found.

safi-cedvel:66-66.t:
* I'rab:
(لا) prohibitive, making the verb jussive; (تعتذروا) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), its sign of jussive being the dropping of the nūn.. and the waw is the fāʿil (agent); (قد) a particle of realization (taḥqīq); (كفرتم) past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, with its fāʿil; (بعد) adverb of time, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (mutaʿalliq) (كفرتم); (إيمان) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr), and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (إن) a conditional particle that makes the verb jussive; (نعف) imperfect verb, jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), its sign of jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "naḥnu"; (عن طائفة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (نعف); (من) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to an [omitted] naʿt (adjective) of (الطائفة); (نعذّب) imperfect verb, jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the fāʿil is "naḥnu"; (طائفة) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative; (الباء) a preposition; (أنّ) a particle resembling the verb, and (هم) a pronoun, the subject (ism) of anna; (كانوا) defective past verb ... and the waw is the subject of kāna; (مجرمين) khabar (predicate) of kāna, accusative, its sign of accusative being the yāʾ.
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أنّهم كانوا ...) is in the position of genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (نعذّب).
The clause «لا تعتذروا ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «قد كفرتم» has no grammatical position, causal (taʿlīliyya) or an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «إن نعف ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «نعذّب ...» has no grammatical position as the apodosis not joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «كانوا ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of anna.

* Morphology:
(نعف): it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion because of the jussive; its origin is نعفو, and its wazn is نفع with ḍamma on the ʿayn.

safi-cedvel:67-67.t:
* I'rab:
(المنافقون) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ), its sign of nominative being the waw; (الواو) conjunction; (المنافقات) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the mubtadaʾ, nominative; (بعض) mubtadaʾ, nominative, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (من بعض) a preposition and its genitive noun, khabar (predicate) of بعضهم, with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "of the kind of some others"; (يأمرون) imperfect verb, nominative.. and the waw is the fāʿil (agent); (بالمنكر) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يأمرون); (الواو) conjunction; (ينهون عن المعروف) like يأمرون بالمنكر, and the preposition phrase is attached to (ينهون); (الواو) conjunction; (يقبضون) like يأمرون; (أيديهم) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (نسوا) past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma ... and the waw is the fāʿil; (الله) the Divine Name, mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الفاء) conjunction, linking the effect to the cause; (نسي) past verb, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is "huwa"; (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb; (المنافقين) the subject (ism) of inna, accusative, its sign of accusative being the yāʾ; (هم) a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) [Note: Or a detached pronoun, a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is (الفاسقون), and the nominal clause is the khabar of inna.]; (الفاسقون) khabar of inna, nominative, its sign of nominative being the waw.
The clause «المنافقون.. بعضهم من بعض» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «بعضهم من بعض» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (المنافقون).
The clause «يأمرون ...» is in the position of nominative as a second khabar of the mubtadaʾ [Note: It may be a badal (substitute) for the clause (بعضهم من بعض) ... and it may be an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī), so it has no grammatical position.].
The clause «ينهون ...» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause يأمرون.
The clause «يقبضون ...» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause يأمرون.
The clause «نسوا ...» is in the position of nominative as a third khabar of the mubtadaʾ [Note: It may be resumptive, so it has no grammatical position.].
The clause «نسيهم» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause نسوا.
The clause «إنّ المنافقين ... الفاسقون» has no grammatical position, resumptive.

* Rhetoric:
1- Kināya (metonymy): in His saying, Exalted is He, (وَيَقْبِضُونَ أَيْدِيَهُمْ), for [withholding] spending in obedience to Allah and in seeking His pleasure. Closing the hand is a metonymy for stinginess and miserliness, just as opening it is a metonymy for generosity, because one who gives stretches out his hand, unlike one who withholds.
2- Majāz (figurative usage): in His saying, Exalted is He, نَسُوا اللَّهَ; forgetting is a figure for abandoning, and it is a metonymy for abandoning obedience, so what is meant is that they did not obey Him, Glorified is He.
3- Mushākala (verbal correspondence): in His saying, Exalted is He, فَنَسِيَهُمْ, i.e. He withheld His kindness and favour from them, and the expression with "forgetting" is for the sake of mushākala.

safi-cedvel:68-68.t:
* I'rab:
(وعد) past verb; (الله) the Divine Name, fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ); (المنافقين) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (الواو) conjunction; (المنافقات) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to المنافقين, accusative, its sign of accusative being the kasra; (الواو) conjunction; (الكفّار) conjoined to المنافقين, accusative; (نار) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (جهنّم) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr), its sign of genitive being the fatḥa; (خالدين) ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, from المنافقين — and it is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara) — its sign of accusative being the yāʾ; (في) a preposition and (ها) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (خالدين); (هي) a detached pronoun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (حسب) khabar (predicate), nominative; (وهم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) conjunction; (لعن) past verb, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (الله) the Divine Name, fāʿil, nominative; (الواو) conjunction; (اللام) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (عذاب) delayed mubtadaʾ, nominative; (مقيم) naʿt (adjective) of عذاب, nominative.
[Translator's note: The source writes the head as (وهم), although the parsed pronoun is (هم) of حسبهم.]
The clause «وعد الله ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «هي حسبهم» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from نار جهنم.
The clause «لعنهم الله» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «لهم عذاب» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.

* Rhetoric:
Rational figurative usage (al-majāz al-ʿaqlī): in His saying, Exalted is He, وَلَهُمْ عَذابٌ مُقِيمٌ; it is as in His saying, Exalted is He, عِيشَةٍ راضِيَةٍ, and the figure here lies in describing the punishment as "abiding".

safi-cedvel:37-37.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّما) the restricting particle and the restricted (kāffa wa-makfūfa). (النسيء) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ). (زيادة) khabar (predicate), nominative. (في الكفر) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (زيادة). (يضلّ) an imperfect verb, passive, nominative. (الباء) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (يضلّ); the bāʾ is causal. (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (كفروا) a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). (يحلّون) an imperfect verb, nominative ... and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (عاما) an adverb of time, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (يحلّونه). (الواو) conjunction. (يحرّمونه عاما) like يحلّونه عاما, and the adverb is attached to (يحرّمونه). (اللام) causal (taʿlīl). (يواطئوا) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied (muḍmara) أن after the lām, the sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil. (عدّة) mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (حرّم) a past verb. (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative. (الفاء) conjunction. (يحلّوا) an imperfect verb, accusative, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to (يواطئوا). (ما) a relative, mafʿūl bihi. (حرّم الله) like the first. (زيّن) a past verb, passive. (لهم) like به, attached to (زيّن). (سوء) nāʾib fāʿil, nominative. (أعمال) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يواطئوا) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to (يحرّمون) [Note: Or attached to both verbs (يحلّونه، ويحرّمونه).].
(الواو) resumptive. (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ, nominative. (لا) negative. (يهدي) an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the yāʾ. (القوم) mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (الكافرين) a naʿt (adjective) of القوم, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ.
The clause «إنّما النسيء زيادة ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يضلّ به الذين» is in the position of nominative as a second khabar of النسيء [Note: Or it has no grammatical position, as an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).].
The clause «كفروا» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «يحلّونه ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «يحرّمونه ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause يحلّونه.
The clause «يواطئوا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the implied particle relative (أن).
The clause «حرّم الله» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the first relative (ما).
The clause «يحلّوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يواطئوا.
The clause «حرّم الله (the second)» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second relative (ما).
The clause «زيّن لهم سوء ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «الله لا يهدي القوم» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «لا يهدي ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الله).

* Morphology:
(النسيء): it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the view of al-Zamakhsharī, its pattern being فعيل, from أنسأ, i.e. he postponed; or a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar), because it falls short of the number of letters of its verb. It has also been said that it is a derived adjective in the sense of a passive participle, i.e. منسوء. In al-Mukhtār: النسيء in the verse is فعيل in the sense of a passive participle, from your saying نسأه, of the pattern-class of قطع, i.e. he postponed it, so it is منسوء; then منسوء was changed into نسيء just as مقتول was changed into قتيل.
(زيادة): an aurally transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar of the verb زاد يزيد, its pattern being فعالة with kasra on the fāʾ. There are other maṣdars: زيد with fatḥa or kasra on the zāy and sukūn on the yāʾ, زيد with two fatḥas, and زيدان with fatḥa on the zāy and the yāʾ; and the mīmī maṣdar of it is مزيد with fatḥa on the mīm and kasra on the zāy, contrary to the regular pattern.

safi-cedvel:38-38.t:
* I'rab:
(يأيّها الذين آمنوا) its i'rab has already been given [Note: In verse (23) of this surah.], (ما) an interrogative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). (اللام) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ. (إذا) a pure adverb stripped of the conditional sense, indeclinable, in the position of accusative, attached to (اثّاقلتم) [Note: Because the clause اثّاقلتم has a grammatical position, as will come.], (قيل) a past verb, passive. (لكم) like the first, attached to (قيل). (انفروا) an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). (في سبيل الله) a preposition, its genitive noun and a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), attached to (انفروا). (اثّاقلتم) a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn.. and (تم) is the fāʿil. (إلى الأرض) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (اثّاقلتم). (أرضيتم) the interrogative hamza for rebuke, and a verb and its fāʿil. (بالحياة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (رضيتم). (الدنيا) a naʿt (adjective) of الحياة, genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the implied (muqaddar) kasra on the alif. (من الآخرة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (رضيتم) by its being made to include (taḍmīn) the sense of "you took in exchange" [Note: The prepositional phrase may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) of الحياة, i.e. as a substitute for the Hereafter.], (الفاء) resumptive and causal. (ما) negative. (متاع) mubtadaʾ, nominative (marfūʿ). (الحياة) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (الدنيا) like the first. (في الآخرة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (قليل). (إلّا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). (قليل) the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, nominative.
The vocative clause «يأيّها ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «ما لكم ...» has no grammatical position: the response to the vocative.
The clause «قيل لكم ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «انفروا ...» is in the position of nominative as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) [Note: Because when the verb is active it is the clause of the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).].
The clause «اثّاقلتم ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the second-person pronoun in (لكم) [Note: I.e. what is the matter with you, being sluggish at every time it is said to you: go forth.].
The clause «رضيتم» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «ما متاع.. إلّا قليل» has no grammatical position: resumptive and causal.

* Morphology:
(اثّاقلتم): its origin is تثاقلتم; then the tāʾ was converted into a thāʾ for assimilation after being given sukūn, and the connecting hamza was added to suit the sukūn. Its pattern was تفاعلتم, then it became افّاعلتم or أتفاعلتم, by analogy with the pattern of اضطرب, افتعل, since the pattern does not change through the presence of substitution in the word [Note: See the morphology of the word (ادّارأتم), verse (72) of al-Baqara.].

* Benefits:
In this verse occurs His saying, the Exalted: ما لَكُمْ إِذا قِيلَ لَكُمُ انْفِرُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ اثَّاقَلْتُمْ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ. This verse calls the believers to go forth in the way of Allah, and shows the state of sluggishness that comes over them at that. The Noble Quran uses the verb (اثّاقلتم), and if we reflect on this verb, with its sound and its suggestiveness, we see that it expresses the state of slowness and of clinging to the ground that comes over a person when he is called to something heavy on his soul.
