We almost feel, through the sound of this verb and its suggestiveness, that it depicts that heavy body tied to the ground which we try to raise, but it slips from our hand and returns to cling to the ground. The doubled thāʾ at the beginning of the verb comes to share in drawing this state and bringing it out. If we replaced the verb (اثاقلتم) occurring in the verse with the verb تثاقلتم, that sound, suggestiveness and force of expression would vanish, and the power running through the meaning of this verb would be extinguished. [Translator's note: the source has the two verbs in the reverse order — "if we replaced with the verb تثاقلتم the verb اثاقلتم"; the intended sense is as translated.] This is one of the aspects of the inimitability of the speech of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and its distinction from the speech of human beings.

safi-cedvel:39-39.t:
* I'rab:
(إن) a conditional particle causing the jussive. (لا) negative. (تنفروا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn ... and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). (يعذّب) an imperfect verb, jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil is "He". (عذابا) a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar (verbal noun), for it is a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar), accusative (manṣūb). (أليما) a naʿt (adjective) of (عذابا), accusative. (الواو) conjunction. (يستبدل) like يعذّب, and conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it. (قوما) mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (غير) a naʿt of (قوما), accusative, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) [Note: The annexation of (غير) to the pronoun did not make it definite, and so it is correct to parse it as a naʿt of (قوما). As for the other object of the verb يستبدل, it is omitted, its implied form being: He will replace you with a people other than you.], (الواو) conjunction. (لا) negative. (تضرّوا) like تنفروا, and conjoined to the verb يعذّبكم, and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (شيئا) a mafʿūl muṭlaq, accusative, standing in for the maṣdar, i.e. you will not harm Him with any harm. (الواو) resumptive. (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ). (على كلّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (قدير). (شيء) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr). (قدير) khabar (predicate), nominative.
The clause «تنفروا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يعذّبكم ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of the condition, not joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «يستبدل ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يعذّبكم.
The clause «لا تضرّوه ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يعذّبكم.
The clause «الله ... قدير» has no grammatical position: resumptive.

safi-cedvel:40-40.t:
* I'rab:
(إلّا تنصروا) like إلّا تنفروا [Note: In the previous verse (39).], and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (قد) a particle of realisation (taḥqīq). (نصر) a past verb, and (الهاء) like the first. (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ). (إذ) an adverb of past time, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (نصره). (أخرجه) like نصره, and the fāʿil is the relative noun (الذين), in the position of nominative. (كفروا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma.. and the wāw is the fāʿil. (ثاني) a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb), of the third-person pronoun in (أخرجه). (اثنين) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ. (إذ) like the first, and a badal (substitute) of it. (هما) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). (في الغار) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar (predicate). (إذ) like the first, and a badal of the second. (يقول) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "he", i.e. the Prophet, upon him be peace. (لصاحب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يقول), and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (لا) the prohibitive lā, causing the jussive. (تحزن) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), and the fāʿil is "you". (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) — (الله) the Name of Majesty, the noun of inna, accusative. (مع) an adverb, accusative, attached to the omitted khabar of inna, and (نا) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (الفاء) resumptive. (انزل) like نصر. (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative. (سكينة) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (على) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (أنزل); the pronoun in (عليه) refers to Abū Bakr. (الواو) conjunction. (أيّد) like نصر, and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, referring to the Messenger, upon him be peace. (الجنود) [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has بجنود] a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أيّد). (لم) a particle of negation and the jussive. (تروا) an imperfect verb, jussive, the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn ... and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (ها) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (الواو) conjunction. (جعل) like نصر, and the fāʿil is "He". (كلمة) mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (الذين) a relative, in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. (كفروا) like the first. (السفلى) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the implied (muqaddar) fatḥa. (الواو) resumptive. (كلمة) mubtadaʾ, nominative. (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (هي) a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) [Note: Or a detached, indeclinable pronoun, a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is العليا, and the nominal clause هي العليا is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ كلمة الله.], (العليا) the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the implied ḍamma on the alif. (الواو) resumptive. (الله عزيز) like الله قدير [Note: See the previous verse (39).], (حكيم) a second khabar, nominative.
The clause «إلّا تنصروه ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «قد نصره الله» has no grammatical position: it gives the reason for the omitted apodosis clause, the implied form being: if you do not help him, Allah will help him, because Allah has already helped him ...
The clause «أخرجه الذين ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «كفروا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «هما في الغار» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «يقول ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «لا تحزن» is in the position of accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «إنّ الله معنا» has no grammatical position: causal.
The clause «أنزل الله ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «أيّده ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause أنزل.
The clause «لم تروها» is in the position of genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of جنود.
The clause «جعل ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause أنزل الله.
The clause «كفروا (the second)» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second relative (الذين).
The clause «كلمة الله ... العليا» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «الله عزيز ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.

* Morphology:
(ثاني): a numeral noun on the pattern فاعل, indicating order.
(الغار): a name for a cave or grotto; its plural is غيران. The alif of الغار is converted from a wāw, since it is looked up under the root (غ ور).
(السفلى): the feminine of الأسفل, which is an elative (ism tafḍīl); it is necessarily made feminine because it bears (أل) and describes the word (كلمة). The pattern of السفلى is فعلى with ḍamma on the fāʾ.
(العليا): the feminine of الأعلى, which is an elative; it too is necessarily made feminine, like السفلى, and it describes (كلمة). The pattern of العليا is فعلى with ḍamma on the fāʾ, and the yāʾ in it is original, not converted from a wāw — as in الدنيا [Note: See verse (85) of Sūrat al-Baqara.] — because its verb has wāw and yāʾ as third radical.. علا يعلو, and علي يعلى of the class of فرح, and على يعلي of the class of ضرب.

safi-cedvel:69-69.t:
* I'rab:
(الكاف) a preposition; (الذين) relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "antum" [Note: al-ʿUkbarī made the preposition and its genitive noun a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "a promise like the promise of those before you".]; (من) a preposition; (قبل) a noun, genitive (majrūr) by the preposition, attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause), i.e. "who passed before you", and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (كانوا) defective past verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) — indeclinable on ḍamma..
and the waw is a pronoun in the position of nominative as the subject (ism) of kāna; (أشدّ) khabar of كانوا, accusative (manṣūb); (من) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (أشدّ); (قوّة) tamyīz (specification), accusative; (الواو) conjunction; (أكثر أموالا) like أشدّ قوّة, so it is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it; (الواو) conjunction; (أولادا) conjoined to (أموالا), accusative; (الفاء) conjunction; (استمعوا) past verb, indeclinable on ḍamma ... and the waw is the fāʿil (agent); (بخلاق) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (استمتعوا), and (هم) an attached pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الفاء) conjunction; (استمتعتم) past verb with its fāʿil; (بخلاقكم) like بخلافهم, attached to (استمتعتم); (الكاف) like the first; (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle; (استمتع) like the first; (الذين) relative noun, fāʿil, in the position of nominative; (من قبلكم) like the first, attached to (استمتع); (بخلافهم) like the first, attached to (استمتع).
[Translator's note: The source writes the heads as (استمعوا) and (بخلافهم), evidently typographical errors for (استمتعوا) and (بخلاقهم) of the verse.]
The interpreted maṣdar (ما استمتع) is in the position of genitive, attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "you enjoyed an enjoyment like the enjoyment of those before you".
(الواو) conjunction; (خضتم) like استمتعتم; (كالذي) like كالذين, attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq, i.e. "an engaging like that which they engaged in"; (خاضوا) like استمتعوا, and the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. خاضوه; (أولئك) demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ ... and (الكاف) a particle of address; (حبطت) past verb ... and (التاء) for the feminine; (أعمال) fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (في الدنيا) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (حبطت), its sign of genitive being the kasra implied (muqaddar) on the alif; (الواو) conjunction; (الآخرة) conjoined to الدنيا, genitive; (الواو) conjunction; (أولئك) like the first; (هم) a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) [Note: Or a detached pronoun, a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is (الخاسرون), and the nominal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أولئك).]; (الخاسرون) khabar of the mubtadaʾ, nominative.
The clause «(أنتم) كالذين من قبلكم» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «كانوا أشدّ ...» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «استمتعوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause كانوا.
The clause «استمتعتم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause استمتعوا.
The clause «استمتع الذين.» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the particle relative (ما).
The clause «خضتم» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause استمتعتم.
The clause «خاضوا» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (الذي).
The clause «أولئك حبطت أعمالهم» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «حبطت أعمالهم» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أولئك).
The clause «أولئك ... الخاسرون» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause أولئك حبطت.

* Morphology:
(خضتم): it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion, to suit the building on sukūn, because it is a hollow weak verb (muʿtall ajwaf); its origin is خوضتم with sukūn on the waw and the ḍād; the waw was dropped because of the meeting of two sukūns. Its wazn is فلتم with ḍamma on the fāʾ, because the dropped letter is the waw.

* Rhetoric:
1- Iltifāt (shift of address): in His saying, Exalted is He, كَالَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ, a shift from the third person to direct address, for intensification.
2- Repetition (takrīr): in repeating استمتعوا; that is because He likened their state to the state of the earlier peoples, so the repetition contains emphasis and exaggeration in censuring those addressed, and in showing the ugliness of their state and the repugnance of their affair.
3- Istiʿāra (metaphor): in خضتم, where He likened falsehood to water and borrowed for it the word خضتم, i.e. you entered into falsehood.

safi-cedvel:9-12.t:
* I'rab:
(اشتروا) past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif that was deleted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (بآيات) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (اشتروا), the verb being made to include the meaning of استبدلوا ("they exchanged"); (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (ثمنا) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (قليلا) naʿt (adjective) of (ثمنا), accusative; (الفاء) conjunction; (صدّوا) like اشتروا; (عن سبيل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (صدّوا), and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (أنّ) [Translator's note: so in the source; the particle in the verse is إنّ] a particle resembling the verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) — and (هم) a pronoun in the position of an accusative, the noun of إنّ; (ساء) past verb for expressing blame (inshāʾ al-dhamm), inflexible (jāmid) [Note: Or it is a fully conjugable transitive verb whose fāʿil is the interpreted maṣdar or the relative, and whose object is omitted, i.e. "their deeds grieved them" or "what they used to do grieved them"..], (ما) relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of a nominative, fāʿil [Note: Or it is a maṣdar-forming particle which, with the verb after it, is interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun).], and the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, its implied form being "عملهم هذا"; (كانوا) incomplete past verb — an abrogator — indeclinable on ḍamma.. and the wāw is a pronoun in the position of a nominative, the noun of كان; (يعملون) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) … and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The clause «اشتروا …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «صدّوا …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «إنّهم ساء ما كانوا …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «ساء ما كانوا …» is in the position of a nominative, the khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
The clause «كانوا …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (ما), and the resumptive pronoun is omitted, i.e. "يعملونه".
The clause «يعملون» is in the position of an accusative, the khabar of كانوا.
(لا) negative; (يرقبون) like يعملون; (في مؤمن) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يرقبون); (إلّا ولا ذمّة) its i'rab has already passed [Note: In verse (8) of this sūra.
(2, 3) Or [conjoined] to the clause إنّهم ساء …, and the clause لا يرقبون then becomes parenthetical.] [Translator's note: the footnotes are merged like this in the source; the text of footnote 2 (on the separating pronoun) does not appear, and the "(2, 3)" note appears to belong to footnote 3; the bracketed "conjoined" is supplied by the translator.] (الواو) conjunction; (أولئك) demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of a nominative, mubtadaʾ (subject).. and (الكاف) a particle of address; (هم) a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) «2», (المعتدون) khabar, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw.
The clause «لا يرقبون …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.. or a causal explanation of the blame.
The clause «أولئك هم المعتدون» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause لا يرقبون «3».
(الفاء) conjunction; (إن تابوا … الزكاة) its i'rab has already passed [Note: In verse (5) of this sūra.], (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (إخوان) khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هم", and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (في الدين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (إخوان), because it contains the meaning of sharing in good times and bad.
(الواو) resumptive; (نفصّل) imperfect verb, nominative.. and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "نحن", for majesty; (الآيات) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the kasra; (لقوم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (نفصّل); (يعلمون) like يعلمون.
The clause «تابوا …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause أولئك هم المعتدون.
The clause «أقاموا …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause تابوا.
The clause «آتوا …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause تابوا.
The clause «(هم) إخوانكم …» is in the position of a jussive (majzūm), the apodosis of the condition, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «نفصّل …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يعلمون» is in the position of a genitive, a naʿt of قوم.
(الواو) conjunction; (إن نكثوا) like إن تابوا; (إيمان) [Translator's note: so in the source; the word in the verse is أيمان] mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (من بعد) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (نكثوا); (عهد) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, and (هم) like the last; (الواو) conjunction; (طعنوا) like تابوا and conjoined to (نكثوا); (في دين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (طعنوا), and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الفاء) linking the apodosis; (قاتلوا) imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil; (أئمّة) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الكفر) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (إنّهم) like the first; (لا) the lā of generic negation; (أيمان) the noun of لا, indeclinable on fatḥa, in the position of an accusative; (اللام) preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to an omitted khabar of لا; (لعلّ) a particle resembling the verb — an abrogator — and (هم) a pronoun in the position of an accusative, the noun of لعلّ; (ينتهون) like يعملون.
The clause «نكثوا …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause تابوا, and what lies between them is a parenthesis.
The clause «طعنوا …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause نكثوا.
The clause «قاتلوا …» is in the position of a jussive, the apodosis of the condition, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «إنّهم لا أيمان لهم» has no grammatical position, giving the reason for the command to fight.
The clause «لا أيمان لهم» is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «لعلّهم ينتهون» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) … or causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «ينتهون» is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of لعلّ.

* Morphology:
(أئمّة): plural of إمام, a noun for one who is followed as an example; its wazn is فعال with kasra on the fāʾ, and the wazn of أئمّة is أفعلة. The original form is أأممة, with sukūn on the second hamza, kasra on the first mīm and fatḥa on the second.. the vowel of the first mīm was transferred to the quiescent letter before it, then the two mīms were assimilated. The Basrans require converting the second hamza into a yāʾ — and that was not permitted as a reading — while others keep it, or lighten the second "between the two" (bayna bayna), or insert an alif between them for lightening.
(ينتهون): it contains a weak-letter change by deletion (iʿlāl bi-l-ḥadhf); its original form is ينتهيون; the vowel on the yāʾ was felt heavy, so it was made quiescent and its vowel transferred to the hāʾ — a weak-letter change by quiescence (iʿlāl bi-l-taskīn) — so two quiescent letters met, the yāʾ and the wāw, and the yāʾ was deleted, giving ينتهون; its wazn is يفتعون.

* Rhetoric:
Metonymic trope (al-majāz al-mursal): in the saying of Allah the Exalted وَإِنْ نَكَثُوا أَيْمانَهُمْ, whereas those who broke were only some of them; so the general was mentioned and the particular intended, and the relation of this trope is generality.

safi-cedvel:13-13.t:
* I'rab:
(ألا) particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ); (تقاتلون) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) … and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (قوما) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (نكثوا) past verb and its fāʿil; (أيمان) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الواو) conjunction; (همّوا) like نكثوا; (بإخراج) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (همّوا); (الرسول) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (الواو) conjunction; (هم) detached pronoun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of a nominative, mubtadaʾ (subject); (بدؤوا) like نكثوا, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (أوّل) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative, standing in for the maṣdar, i.e. "بدءا أوّلا"; (مرّة) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (الهمزة) for the interrogative of affirmation (istifhām taqrīrī); (تخشون) like تقاتلون, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition; (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ, nominative; (أحقّ) khabar (predicate), nominative [Note: Or it is a fronted khabar, and the interpreted maṣdar (أن تخشوه) is a postponed mubtadaʾ; this is the view of al-ʿUkbarī.. and he permitted [Translator's note: the footnote breaks off here in the source]], (أن) maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle; (تخشوا) imperfect verb, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تخشوه) is in the position of a nominative, a badal (substitute) of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) from the Name of Majesty, i.e. "the fear of Allah is more deserving" [Note: The interpreted maṣdar may be in the position of a genitive by an omitted preposition, namely the bāʾ, i.e.: "more deserving of fear than anyone else".].
(إن) like the previous [Note: In verse (8) of this sūra.], (كنتم) incomplete past verb, indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of a jussive, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) … and (تم) a pronoun in the position of a nominative, the noun of كان; (مؤمنين) the khabar of كنتم, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ.
The clause «تقاتلون …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «نكثوا …» is in the position of an accusative, a naʿt (adjective) of (قوما).
The clause «همّوا …» is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause نكثوا.
The clause «هم بدؤوكم …» is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause نكثوا.
The clause «بدؤوكم …» is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ هم.
The clause «تخشونهم» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «الله أحقّ …» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e. "if you fear anyone, then Allah is more deserving …".
The clause «تخشوه» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «كنتم مؤمنين» has no grammatical position, resumptive … and the apodosis of إن is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "if you are believers, then fear Allah".

* Benefits:
His saying, the Exalted: أَلا تُقاتِلُونَ قَوْماً نَكَثُوا أَيْمانَهُمْ. In this noble verse the particle (ألا) occurs, and here it is a particle of urging. We shall treat this particle with some explanation; it is:
1- A particle of alerting (tanbīh), indicating the certainty of what follows it, as in His saying, the Exalted: أَلا إِنَّهُمْ هُمُ السُّفَهاءُ. The parsers say of it: "an opening particle" (adāt istiftāḥ), so they state its structure and neglect its meaning. Like it is (أما), which is followed by an oath, as in the saying of the poet Ḥātim al-Ṭāʾī:
أما والذي لا يعلم الغيب غيره ... ويحيي العظام البيض وهي رميم
(By Him besides whom none knows the Unseen, and who revives the white bones when they have decayed.)
2- It comes with the meaning of rebuke and disapproval, as in the saying of the poet:
ألا ارعواء لمن ولّت شبيبته ... وآذنت بمشيب بعده هرم
(Is there no restraint for one whose youth has turned away and announced grey hair, after which comes decrepitude?)
3- It comes for wishing, as in the saying of the poet:
ألا عمر ولّى مستطاع رجوعه ... فيرأب ما أثأت به الغفلات
(Would that a life that has passed could be brought back, so that it might mend what heedlessness has spoiled.)
The meaning of يرأب is "mends", and أثأت is "spoiled".
4- Asking about a negation, as in the saying of the poet Qays ibn al-Mulawwaḥ:
ألا اصطبار لسلمى أم لها جلد ... إذا ألاقي الذي لاقاه أمثالي
(Is there no patience for Salmā, or has she endurance, when I meet what those like me have met?)
5- Offer (ʿarḍ) and urging (taḥḍīḍ): both mean requesting something, but the offer is a gentle request and urging is a request with insistence. This ألا is restricted to verbal clauses, as in His saying, the Exalted: أَلا تُحِبُّونَ أَنْ يَغْفِرَ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ, and as occurs in this verse: أَلا تُقاتِلُونَ قَوْماً نَكَثُوا أَيْمانَهُمْ

safi-cedvel:14-15.t:
* I'rab:
(قاتلوا) imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (يعذّب) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) as the answer to the command (jawāb al-ṭalab), and (هم) like the first; (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ); (بأيدي) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يعذّبهم), the sign of the genitive being the kasra implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الواو) conjunction in the three places; (يخز، ينصر، يشف) jussive imperfect verbs conjoined to (يعذّب); the sign of the jussive of the first and the third is the dropping of the weak letter, and the fāʿil of each of the three verbs is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو", referring to the Name of Majesty; and the two pronouns (هم، كم) are in the position of an accusative, mafʿūl bihi; (على) preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (ينصر); (صدور) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb); (قوم) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (مؤمنين) naʿt (adjective) of قوم, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
The clause «قاتلوهم …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يعذّبهم الله» has no grammatical position, the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, not joined with the fāʾ, i.e.: "if you fight them, Allah will punish them".
The clause «يخزهم» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يعذّبهم.
The clause «ينصركم …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يعذّبهم.
The clause «يشف …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يعذّبهم.
(الواو) conjunction; (يذهب) imperfect verb, jussive, conjoined to (يعذّب), and the fāʿil is "هو"; (غيظ) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (قلوب) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi. (الواو) resumptive; (يتوب) imperfect verb, nominative; (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative; (على) like the first; (من) relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of a genitive, attached to (يتوب); (يشاء) like يتوب; (الواو) resumptive; (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative; (عليم) khabar (predicate), nominative; (حكيم) second khabar, nominative.
The clause «يذهب» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يعذّبهم.
The clause «يتوب» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يشاء» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).
The clause «الله عليم …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.

* Morphology:
(يخزهم): it contains a weak-letter change by deletion (iʿlāl bi-l-ḥadhf) owing to the jussive; its original form is يخزيهم; its wazn is يضعهم [Translator's note: so in the source; the expected wazn is يفعهم]. It also contains the deletion of the hamza for lightening, because its past is أخز [Translator's note: so in the source; i.e. أخزى]; it should have been يؤخزهم, but the deletion in it follows the pattern of يؤمنون [Note: See verse (3) of Sūrat al-Baqara.].
(يشف): it contains a weak-letter change by deletion owing to the jussive; its original form is يشفي; its wazn is يفع.

safi-cedvel:70-70.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for the interrogative of affirmation (istifhām taqrīrī); (لم) a particle of negation and jussive; (يأت) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), its sign of jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (نبأ) fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ); (الذين) relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (من قبل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ṣila (relative clause), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (قوم) badal (substitute) for the relative, genitive (majrūr); (نوح) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (الواو) conjunction in the five places; (عاد، ثمود) both conjoined (maʿṭūf) to نوح, genitive; (قوم) conjoined to the first قوم, genitive; (إبراهيم) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, its sign of genitive being the fatḥa; (أصحاب) conjoined to قوم, genitive; (مدين) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, its sign of genitive being the fatḥa, being barred from tanwīn; (المؤتفكات) conjoined to قوم, genitive, and it is with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "the people of al-Muʾtafikāt" [Note: al-Muʾtafikāt: the towns of the people of Lūṭ.]; (أتت) past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif that was dropped because of the meeting of two sukūns.. and (التاء) for the feminine; (رسل) fāʿil, nominative, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (بالبيّنات) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أتتهم); (الفاء) conjunction; (ما) negative; (كان) defective past verb — an abrogator (nāsikh); (الله) the Divine Name, the subject (ism) of kāna, nominative; (اللام) the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd); (يظلم) imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after the lām of denial, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is "huwa"; (الواو) conjunction; (لكن) a particle of rectification (istidrāk); (كانوا) its i'rab has been given [Note: in the previous verse (69).]. (أنفس) fronted mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (يظلمون) imperfect verb, nominative ... and the waw is the fāʿil.
The clause «لم يأتهم نبأ ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «أتتهم رسلهم» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «ما كان الله ليظلمهم» has no grammatical position, conjoined to implied clauses, i.e. "so they belied them, and so they were destroyed, and Allah was not ...".
The clause «يظلمهم ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the implied particle relative (أن).
The clause «لكن كانوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause ما كان ...
The clause «يظلمون» is in the position of accusative as the khabar (predicate) of كانوا.
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن يظلمهم) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to the omitted khabar of kāna.

* Morphology:
(نبأ): singular of أنباء.. see verse (44) of Sūrat Āl ʿImrān.
(المؤتفكات): plural of المؤتفكة, the feminine of المؤتفك, meaning "the overturned", which is turned upside down; it is the active participle of the five-letter verb ائتفك ... One says: أفكته فأتفك, i.e. I overturned it and it was overturned ... The wazn of المؤتفك is مفتعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.

safi-cedvel:71-71.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (المؤمنون والمؤمنات ... ويطيعون الله) the i'rab of its counterpart has been given [Note: in verse (67) of this sūra.]; (الواو) conjunction; (رسول) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the Divine Name, and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (أولئك سيرحمهم الله) like أولئك حبطت أعمالهم [Note: in verse (69) of this sūra.], and (السين) a particle of the future, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb — an abrogator (nāsikh); (الله) the Divine Name, the subject (ism) of inna, accusative (manṣūb); (عزيز) khabar (predicate) of inna, nominative (marfūʿ); (حكيم) second khabar, nominative.
The clause «المؤمنون ... بعضهم أولياء ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause (بعضهم أولياء بعض) is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (المؤمنون).
The clause «يأمرون ...» is in the position of nominative as a second khabar [Note: Or it is an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī), so it has no grammatical position, and likewise the clauses conjoined to it.].
The clause «ينهون ...» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause يأمرون.
The clause «يقيمون ...» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause يأمرون.
The clause «يؤتون ...» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause يأمرون.
The clause «يطيعون ...» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause يأمرون.
The clause «أولئك سيرحمهم الله» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «سيرحمهم الله» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أولئك).
The clause «إنّ الله عزيز ...» has no grammatical position, being in effect causal (taʿlīliyya).

safi-cedvel:72-72.t:
* I'rab:
(وعد الله ... جنّات) the i'rab of its counterpart has been given [Note: in verse (68) of this sūra.], and the sign of accusative of جنّات is the kasra; (تجري) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), its sign of nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ; (من تحت) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تجري) [Note: Or attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from الأنهار — a naʿt (adjective) placed before the noun it qualifies — [.....]], and (ها) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "from beneath its trees"; (الأنهار) fāʿil (agent), nominative; (خالدين) ḥāl from المؤمنين, accusative (manṣūb) — and it is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara) — its sign of accusative being the yāʾ; (في) a preposition and (ها) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (خالدين); (الواو) conjunction; (مساكن) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to جنّات, accusative like it, and barred from tanwīn because it is on the pattern of the ultimate plural (ṣīghat muntahā al-jumūʿ); (طيّبة) naʿt of مساكن, accusative; (في جنّات) a preposition and its genitive noun, a second naʿt of مساكن; (عدن) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (الواو) resumptive; (رضوان) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative; (من الله) a preposition and its genitive noun, naʿt of رضوان; (أكبر) khabar (predicate), nominative; (ذلك) demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ ... and (اللام) for distance and (الكاف) for address; (الفوز) khabar of the mubtadaʾ ذلك; (العظيم) naʿt of الفوز, nominative like it.
The clause «وعد الله ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «تجري ...» is in the position of accusative as a naʿt of جنّات.
The clause «رضوان ... أكبر» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «ذلك الفوز ...» has no grammatical position, causal (taʿlīliyya).

* Morphology:
(طيّبة): feminine of طيّب, its plural is طيّبات ... see verse (57) of Sūrat al-Baqara.
(عدن): a maṣdar (verbal noun) used as an adjective, and so it remains singular with the singular, dual and plural; it means "residence". Its wazn is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn. There is another maṣdar of the verb عدن يعدن, of the pattern of naṣara and of the pattern of ḍaraba, namely عدون with ḍamma on the ʿayn.

safi-cedvel:73-73.t:
* I'rab:
(يا) vocative particle; (أيّ) the one addressed (munādā), a specific indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma in the position of accusative, and (ها) a particle of alerting (tanbīh); (النبيّ) badal (substitute) for أيّ or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition), following it in the nominative in its wording; (جاهد) imperative verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is "anta"; it was vowelled with kasra because of the meeting of two sukūns; (الكفّار) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (الواو) conjunction; (المنافقين) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to الكفّار, accusative, its sign of accusative being the yāʾ; (الواو) conjunction; (اغلظ) like جاهد; (على) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (اغلظ); (الواو) resumptive [Note: al-ʿUkbarī said: "If it is asked how the waw is appropriate here when the fāʾ suits this place better, there are three answers. The first is that it is the waw of ḥāl, the implied sense being: do that while they deserve Hell, which is the state of their disbelief. The second is that the waw was brought as an indication that an omitted verb is intended, i.e. 'and know that their refuge ...'. The third is that the speech is construed according to meaning, namely that the punishment of this world through jihād and the punishment of the Hereafter through Hell have both been gathered for them." End quote.]; (مأوى) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ), its sign of nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (جهنّم) khabar (predicate), nominative; (الواو) conjunction; (بئس) a frozen (jāmid) past verb for expressing censure; (المصير) fāʿil, nominative, and the one specified for censure (al-makhṣūṣ bil-dhamm) is omitted, its implied form being "hiya", i.e. Hell.
The clause «يأيّها النبي ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «جاهد ...» has no grammatical position, as the answer to the vocative.
The clause «اغلظ ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause جاهد.
The clause «مأواهم جهنّم» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «بئس المصير» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause مأواهم جهنّم [Note: Or a fronted khabar, if the one specified [for censure] is parsed as a mubtadaʾ.].

safi-cedvel:107-107.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) a conjunction; (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject) of a fronted khabar (predicate), i.e. "among them are those who took a mosque" [Note: Or its khabar: "among those we have described are those who…". Al-Zamakhsharī made the relative noun in the position of accusative by way of specification (ikhtiṣāṣ).], (اتّخذوا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (مسجدا) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (ضرارا) mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), accusative [Note: Or a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), or a second mafʿūl bihi of the verb اتّخذوا. Some — other than Abū Ḥayyān — permitted it to be a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, i.e. "they harm the believers with harm (يضارّون المؤمنين ضرارا)".], (الواو) a conjunction in all three places; (كفرا، تفريقا، إرصادا) nouns conjoined to (ضرارا), accusative; (بين) an adverb, accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تفريقا); (المؤمنين) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ; (اللام) a preposition; (من) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive, attached to (إرصادا); (حارب) a past verb, and the fāʿil is "he", and it is the referent pronoun [Note: He is Abū ʿĀmir the monk, who waged war on the Messenger ﷺ.]; (الله) the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الواو) a conjunction; (رسول) conjoined to the Name of Majesty, accusative, and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (من) a preposition; (قبل) a noun indeclinable on the ḍamma in the position of genitive, attached to (حارب); (الواو) a conjunction; (اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied oath; (يحلفنّ) an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the retention of the nūn — it has been deleted because of the succession of identical letters — and the wāw, deleted because of the meeting of two sukūns, is the fāʿil; and (النون) the nūn of emphasis; (ان) negative; (أردنا) a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn, and (نا) a pronoun, fāʿil; (إلّا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (الحسنى) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and it is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted qualified noun, i.e. "except the best trait (إلّا الخصلة الحسنى)"; (الواو) resumptive; (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ, nominative; (يشهد) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is "he"; (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) — and (هم) a pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of inna; (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); (كاذبون) the khabar of inna, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw.
The clause «(منهم) الذين …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause «آخرون» [Note: In the previous verse (106).].
The clause «اتّخذوا …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «حارب …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (من).
The clause «يحلفنّ …» has no grammatical position, being the answer to an implied oath.
The clause «إن أردنا …» has no grammatical position, being the answer to an oath expressed by His saying يحلفنّ [Note: Or it is the answer to another implied oath, and the second oath clause is the speech (maqūl al-qawl) of an implied verb of saying — which is a ḥāl of the fāʿil of يحلفنّ — i.e. "they will surely swear, saying: By Allah, we intended nothing but the best…".].
The clause «الله يشهد …» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «يشهد …» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الله).
The clause «إنّهم لكاذبون» is in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl bihi governed by يشهد, and the hamza of (إنّ) is given kasra because of the lām coming in its khabar.

* Morphology:
(تفريقا): a regular maṣdar of the four-letter verb فرّق; its pattern is تفعيل.
(إرصادا): a regular maṣdar of the four-letter verb أرصد; its pattern is إفعال.

* Benefits:
The story of the Mosque of Harm (مسجد الضّرار): this verse was revealed concerning a group of hypocrites who built a mosque by which to harm the Mosque of Qubāʾ.
They were twelve men of the people of hypocrisy; they built this mosque «ضرارا», i.e. to cause harm among the Muslims) and «كفرا» (i.e. to disbelieve in it in Allah and His Messenger), and to split the community.
Mujammiʿ ibn Jāriya used to lead them in prayer in it; he was a young man who recited the Qur'an, but he did not know of their affair and their malice. When they finished building it, they came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was preparing for Tabūk and said: "O Messenger of Allah, we have built a mosque for the sick and the needy and for the rainy night, and we would love you to come to us, pray in it, and pray for blessing." He ﷺ said to him: "I am on the point of travelling; when we return, if Allah the Exalted wills, we will come to you and pray in it." When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was returning from Tabūk, he stopped at Dhū Awān, a place near Medina, and the hypocrites came to him and asked him to come to their mosque. He called for his shirt to put it on and go to them, and then Allah revealed this verse. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called Mālik ibn al-Dukhshum, Maʿn ibn ʿAdī, ʿĀmir ibn al-Sakan and Waḥshī, and said to them: "Go to this mosque whose people are wrongdoers, demolish it and burn it." They went out in haste until they entered the mosque, with its people in it, and they burned it and made it into rubble, and its people dispersed from it.
In this story there is a great lesson: how the enemies of the religion fight the religion through the religion itself, and through building mosques. So let the Muslims be wary and not be deceived by appearances.

safi-cedvel:108-108.t:
* I'rab:
(لا) the prohibitive lā, causing the jussive; (تقم) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), and the fāʿil (agent) is "you"; (في) a preposition, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive — attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تقم); (أبدا) an adverb of time, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (تقم); (اللام) the lām of commencement (lām al-ibtidāʾ); (مسجد) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ); (أسّس) a past verb, passive, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "it"; (على التقوى) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أسس), the sign of the genitive being the kasra implied (muqaddar) on the alif; (من أول) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أسّس); (يوم) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (أحقّ) khabar (predicate), nominative; (أن) a maṣdar-forming particle causing the subjunctive (naṣb); (تقوم) an imperfect verb, subjunctive (manṣūb), and the fāʿil is "you"; (فيه) like the first, attached to (تقوم).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تقوم) is in the position of genitive by an omitted bāʾ, attached to (أحقّ), i.e. «بأن تقوم».
(فيه) like the first, attached to a fronted khabar; (رجال) a postponed mubtadaʾ, nominative; (يحبّون) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (أن) like the first; (يتطهّروا) an imperfect verb, subjunctive, the sign of the subjunctive being the deletion of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يتطهّروا) is in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) governed by يحبّون.
(الواو) resumptive; (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ, nominative; (يحبّ) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is "he"; (المطّهّرين) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ.
The clause «لا تقم …» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «لمسجد أسّس …» has no grammatical position, being explanatory of cause (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «أسّس …» is in the position of nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of مسجد.
The clause «تقوم …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «فيه رجال …» has no grammatical position, being explanatory of cause [Note: The clause may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun الهاء in the first (فيه), or of مسجد because it has been qualified, just as it may be a naʿt of مسجد.].
The clause «يحبّون» is in the position of nominative as a naʿt of رجال.
The clause «يتطهّروا …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the second particle relative (أن).
The clause «الله يحبّ …» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «يحبّ …» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الله).

* Morphology:
(المطّهّرين): plural of المطّهّر, the active participle of the five-letter verb تطهّر. In it the tāʾ of the تفعّل form has been replaced by ṭāʾ because the two points of articulation are close. Its pattern is متفعّل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the doubled ʿayn, and the plural is المتفعّلون.

* Rhetoric:
The device of tardīd (فن الترويد): in His saying, the Exalted: «أَحَقُّ أَنْ تَقُومَ فِيهِ. فِيهِ رِجالٌ». The device of tardīd is that the speaker attaches a word in the discourse to one meaning, then repeats it exactly and attaches it to another meaning, as in His saying, the Exalted: «وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لا يَعْلَمُونَ يَعْلَمُونَ ظاهِراً مِنَ الْحَياةِ»: the first يعلمون is negated and the second affirmed, and each of the two meanings has an appropriateness that required that meaning. And in the verse under discussion, the first فيه is attached to تقوم, and the second فيه is a fronted khabar, and each of them has a meaning.
[Translator's note: The source writes «فن الترويد»; the usual name of this device is «الترديد» (tardīd), and its definition matches tardīd. Translated as tardīd with the source spelling kept.]

safi-cedvel:109-109.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for the interrogative of affirmation (istifhām taqrīrī); (الفاء) resumptive [Note: According to a group of grammarians it is a conjunction conjoining to something implied, i.e. "Is it, after what has become known of their state, that he who founded…", but there is no need for that.], (من) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ (subject); (أسس) a past verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is "he", and it is the referent pronoun; (بنيان) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; (على تقوى) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أسّس), the sign of the genitive being the kasra implied (muqaddar) on the alif; (من الله) a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تقوى, by its being made to include the meaning of "fear (مخافة)"; (الواو) a conjunction; (رضوان) conjoined to تقوى, genitive (majrūr); (خير) the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ من; (أم) a conjunction; (من) like the first and conjoined to it; (أسّس بنيانه على شفا) like its counterpart in the first, and the preposition phrase is attached to the second verb; (جرف) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (هار) a naʿt (adjective) of جرف, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the kasra implied on the deleted yāʾ, so it is a defective noun (manqūṣ) — or the overt kasra, so it is sound — ; (الفاء) a conjunction; (انهار) like أسّس, and the fāʿil is "it", i.e. the building or the crumbling bank; (الباء) a preposition, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive — attached to (أنهار) [Note: This is if the bāʾ is for transitivity; or it is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) if the bāʾ is for accompaniment.]; (في نار) a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (أنهار); (جهنّم) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa; (الواو) resumptive; (الله لا يهدي القوم) like «يحبّ المطّهّرين» [Note: In the previous verse (108).], and (لا) is negative; (الظالمين) a naʿt of القوم, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ.
The clause «من أسّس …» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «أسّس …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (من).
The clause «أسّس (the second)» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the second relative noun (من).
The clause «أنهار …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the second clause أسّس.
The clause «الله لا يهدي …» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «لا يهدي …» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الله).
[Translator's note: The source writes the verb as «أنهار» with a hamza in several places; the Quranic word is «انهار».]

* Morphology:
(البنيان): a noun taken from the wording of the maṣdar (verbal noun), for everything that is built; its pattern is فعلان with ḍamma on the fāʾ. It is also said to be a plural whose singular is بنيانة. The verb is بنى يبني, of the ضرب class.
(جرف): a noun meaning a pit, or what the flood sweeps away from the valleys; its pattern is فعل with two ḍammas, and it may be pronounced with ḍamma then sukūn in one of the seven canonical readings.
(هار): it is said that its origin is هاير or هاور, because it is from the verb هار يهور or هار يهير; then the weak letter was changed into a hamza, as is the case with every hollow weak verb; then the hamza was deleted arbitrarily — i.e. for no particular reason — and the case vowel is an overt vowel; its pattern is فال. It is also said to be a defective noun (manqūṣ) by metathesis, the lām having been placed before the ʿayn, so its pattern is فالع before the deletion of the weak letter and فال after the deletion. It is also said that its origin is هور or هير: the weak letter had a vowel and the letter before it had fatḥa, so it was changed into alif; the vowel is thus overt and its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn. هار means fallen, crumbling, collapsing.
[Translator's note: The source prints «بنيانه» for the singular; read as بنيانة (with tāʾ marbūṭa).]

* Rhetoric:
1- The explicit, realised metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-taṣrīḥiyya al-taḥqīqiyya): in His saying, the Exalted, «أَفَمَنْ أَسَّسَ بُنْيانَهُ عَلى تَقْوى مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرِضْوانٍ خَيْرٌ أَمْ مَنْ أَسَّسَ بُنْيانَهُ عَلى شَفا جُرُفٍ هارٍ فَانْهارَ بِهِ», where falsehood and hypocrisy are likened to the edge of a crumbling bank in their lack of firmness; then it was borrowed for that.
The contextual indicator (qarīna) is: placing the edge of the bank opposite piety.
And His saying, the Exalted, «فَانْهارَ بِهِ فِي نارِ جَهَنَّمَ» is a tarshīḥ (reinforcement of the metaphor).
2- The implicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-makniyya): in His saying, the Exalted, «أَفَمَنْ أَسَّسَ بُنْيانَهُ عَلى تَقْوى مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرِضْوانٍ», where piety is likened to the foundations of a building, a simile concealed in the mind.
It is indicated by something among its concomitants and necessary attributes, namely founding and building.

* Benefits:
The embodiment of abstract things: the Noble Qur'an has reached a far limit in the inimitability of its speech and in the embodiment of meanings. In this verse there is a proof of that: faith and piety are two abstract concepts, but the Qur'an embodies them when it likens them to a building; likewise He, the Exalted, embodies misguidance with the word (بنيان), and then draws a comparison between the two buildings, saying, the Exalted: أَفَمَنْ أَسَّسَ بُنْيانَهُ عَلى تَقْوى مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرِضْوانٍ خَيْرٌ أَمْ مَنْ أَسَّسَ بُنْيانَهُ عَلى شَفا جُرُفٍ هارٍ فَانْهارَ بِهِ فِي نارِ جَهَنَّمَ. Here He embodies faith as a building whose foundation is piety and the good pleasure of Allah, so we picture it as a solid, firm building, connected to the care of Allah. As for the disbelievers, their building is on the edge of a collapsing abyss. Here artistic depiction reaches its utmost in creativity, imagination and embodiment: here we are with the building of disbelief, on an edge, shaky and about to topple, and the edge is beside a deep abyss; it is a building that carries danger and death, and suddenly the building collapses with its owner into the fire of Hell. We have touched, with eye, sense and imagination, the corrupt, crumbling, falling image of disbelief, which rests on no pillars and stands on no foundation except a foundation of shakiness, cracking and trembling, and so it topples into Hellfire. Here the art of expression and depiction stands out, by its embodiment of meanings within a framework of images, visible and tangible things, in a complete and consummate form. That is the inimitability of the speech of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and its attainment of the utmost and of perfection!

safi-cedvel:110-110.t:
* I'rab:
(لا يزال) an incomplete imperfect verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) — nominative (marfūʿ), and (لا) is negative; (بنيان) the noun of the incomplete verb, nominative, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الذي) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of بنيان; (بنوا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif deleted because of the meeting of two sukūns, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (ريبة) the khabar (predicate) of the incomplete verb, accusative (manṣūb), with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "a cause of doubt (سبب ريبة)"; (في قلوب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt of ريبة, and (هم) like the last; (إلّا) a particle of exception; (أن) a maṣdar-forming particle causing the subjunctive; (تقطّع) an imperfect verb, subjunctive (manṣūb) — one of the two tāʾs has been deleted from it — ; (قلوب) fāʿil, nominative, and (هم) like the last.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تقطّع..) is in the position of accusative as the excepted, with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "except in the state of their hearts being cut (إلّا حال تقطّع قلوبهم)" or "the time of their hearts being cut (وقت تقطّع قلوبهم)" [Note: That from which the exception is made is omitted, and it is either the generality of states or the generality of times, i.e. "it will remain a doubt in every state" or "at every time, except…".].
(والله عليم حكيم): its i'rab has already been given [Note: In verse (106) of this surah.].
The clause «لا يزال بنيانهم …» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «بنوا …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذي).
The clause «تقطّع قلوبهم» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «الله عليم …» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.

* Morphology:
(بنوا): it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion. Its origin is بناوا; two sukūns met, the alif and the wāw, so the alif was deleted and the fatḥa was left on the letter before the wāw to indicate it. Its pattern is فعوا.
(ريبة): i.e. ريب in form and meaning; it is doubt and the unease and agitation of the soul. Its pattern is فعلة with kasra on the fāʾ and sukūn on the ʿayn.

safi-cedvel:41-41.t:
* I'rab:
(انفروا) an imperative verb.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). (خفافا) a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb), of the fāʿil of انفروا. (ثقالا) conjoined (maʿṭūf) by the wāw to (خفافا), accusative like it. (الواو) conjunction. (جاهدوا) like انفروا. (بأموال) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (جاهدوا), and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (الواو) conjunction. (أنفسكم) conjoined to أموالكم and parsed like it, genitive (majrūr). (في سبيل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb (جاهدوا). (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (ذلكم) a demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (اللام) is for distance and (الكاف) for address. (خير) khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ). (اللام) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (خير). (إن) a conditional particle causing the jussive. (كنتم) a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) — indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).. and (تم) a pronoun, the noun of kāna, in the position of nominative.. (تعلمون) an imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The clause «انفروا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «جاهدوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «ذلكم خير ...» has no grammatical position: causal.
The clause «إن كنتم تعلمون» has no grammatical position: resumptive.. and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. if you know that it is better for you, then do not be sluggish ...
The clause «تعلمون ...» is in the position of accusative as the khabar of kuntum.

safi-cedvel:42-42.t:
* I'rab:
(لو) a conditional particle not causing the jussive. (كان) a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) — and its noun is omitted, indicated by the context of the speech, i.e. had what you were called to been ... (عرضا) the khabar (predicate) of kāna, accusative (manṣūb). (قريبا) a naʿt (adjective) of (عرضا), accusative. (الواو) conjunction. (سفرا) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the khabar, accusative like it. (قاصدا) a naʿt of (سفرا), accusative. (اللام) linking the apodosis of law. (اتّبعوا) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī), with no position ... and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), and (الكاف) mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (الواو) conjunction. (لكن) a particle of rectification (istidrāk). (بعدت) a past verb ... and (التاء) is for the feminine. (على) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (بعدت). (الشقّة) fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ). (الواو) conjunction. (السين) a particle of the future. (يحلفون) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is the fāʿil. (بالله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يحلفون). (لو) like the first. (استطعنا) a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn.. and (نا) a pronoun, fāʿil. (اللام) like the first. (خرجنا) like استطعنا. (مع) an adverb, accusative, attached to (خرجنا), and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (يهلكون) like يحلفون. (أنفس) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (الواو) resumptive. (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative. (يعلم) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is "He". (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb — an abrogator — and (هم) a pronoun in the position of accusative, the noun of inna. (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa). (كاذبون) khabar, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw.
The clause «كان عرضا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «اتّبعوك ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a condition not causing the jussive.
The clause «بعدت عليهم الشقّة» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «سيحلفون ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «لو استطعنا ...» has no grammatical position: the response to an implied oath, indicated by His saying سيحلفون; and the oath clause with its response is in the position of accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl), i.e.:
they will swear by Allah, saying..
The clause «خرجنا ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of law [Note: And it is the response to the oath and the apodosis of the condition at one and the same time, in the view of Abū Ḥayyān.].
The clause «يهلكون ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive [Note: Al-Zamakhsharī made it a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of يحلفون or a badal (substitute) of the clause يحلفون, and Abū Ḥayyān rejected both views.].
The clause «الله يعلم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يعلم ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الله).
The clause «انّهم لكاذبون» is in the position of accusative, taking the place of the two objects of يعلم.. and the hamza of (انّ) is given kasra because of the lām entering the khabar.

* Morphology:
(قاصدا): on the pattern of the active participle, a derived noun meaning easy and near, or moderate.
(الشقّة): a name for the distance that is covered with hardship, since it is derived from المشقّة (hardship); its pattern is فعلة with ḍamma then sukūn.

safi-cedvel:43-43.t:
* I'rab:
(عفا) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the alif. (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ). (عن) a preposition and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (عفا). (اللام) a preposition. (ما) an interrogative noun in the position of genitive, attached to (أذنت); the alif was dropped from the interrogative noun because of the preposition entering it. (أذنت) a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn ... and (التاء) is the fāʿil. (لهم) like عنك, attached to (أذنت) [Note: The lām in (لم) is causal, and the lām in (لهم) is for conveying (tablīgh); for this reason it was permissible to attach both to the same verb.], (حتّى) a particle of limit and a preposition. (يتبيّن) an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muḍmara) أن after حتّى. (لك) like عنك, attached to (يتبيّن). (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as fāʿil. (صدقوا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma ... and the wāw is the fāʿil. (الواو) conjunction. (تعلم) like يتبيّن, and conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it, and the fāʿil is "you". (الكاذبين) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يتبيّن) is in the position of genitive by (حتّى), attached to an omitted verb required by the context of the speech, i.e. why did you not take them out with you, or why did you not refrain from giving permission.
The clause «عفا الله ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «أذنت لهم» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) ... or it is an explanation of the reason for the reproach that preceded.
The clause «يتبيّن ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle relative (أن).
The clause «صدقوا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
The clause «تعلم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila clause of the particle relative.

safi-cedvel:44-44.t:
* I'rab:
(لا) negative. (يستأذن) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ). (الكاف) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (الذين) like الذين صدقوا [Note: In the previous verse (43).], (يؤمنون) an imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). (بالله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يؤمنون). (الواو) conjunction. (اليوم) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the Name of Majesty, genitive (majrūr). (الآخر) a naʿt (adjective) of اليوم, genitive. (أن) an infinitival particle causing the accusative. (يجاهدوا) an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil. (بأموالهم وأنفسهم) like بأموالهم وأنفسكم [Note: In verse (41) of this surah.] [Translator's note: so in the source; verse 41 has بأموالكم وأنفسكم].
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يجاهدوا) is in the position of genitive by an omitted preposition, implied as (في), i.e. in that they strive ..., attached to (يستأذنك), i.e. they ask your permission regarding jihad [Note: The omitted preposition may be (عن), and it is then attached to an omitted word implied as "staying behind" or "sitting back", i.e. they ask your permission to stay behind or sit back from jihad.].
(الواو) resumptive. (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative. (عليم) khabar (predicate), nominative. (بالمتّقين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (عليم), the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
The clause «لا يستأذنك الذين ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يؤمنون ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «يجاهدوا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «الله عليم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.

safi-cedvel:45-45.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّما) the restricting particle and the restricted (kāffa wa-makfūfa). (يستأذنك الذين ... الآخر) like its counterpart «1», and (لا) negative. (الواو) conjunction. (ارتابت) a past verb.. and (التاء) is for the feminine. (قلوب) fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (الفاء) conjunction. (هم) a detached pronoun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). (في ريب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يتردّدون), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (يتردّدون) like يؤمنون «2».
[Translator's note: the markers «1» and «2» refer to footnotes whose text is not given in the source; the counterpart is in the previous verse (44).]
The clause «يستأذنك الذين ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «لا يؤمنون ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «ارتابت قلوبهم» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «هم ... يتردّدون» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause ارتابت.
The clause «يتردّدون» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ هم.

safi-cedvel:46-46.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive. (لو) a conditional particle not causing the jussive. (أرادوا) a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). (الخروج) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb). (اللام) linking the apodosis of law. (أعدّوا) like أرادوا. (اللام) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أعدّوا). (عدّة) mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (الواو) conjunction. (لكن كره) like لكن بعدت [Note: In verse (42) of this surah.], (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ). (انبعاث) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (الفاء) conjunction. (ثبّط) a past verb, and the fāʿil is "He", and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (الواو) conjunction. (قيل) a past verb, passive. (اقعدوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn ... and the wāw is the fāʿil. (مع) an adverb, accusative, attached to (اقعدوا). (القاعدين) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
The clause «أرادوا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «أعدّوا ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a condition not causing the jussive.
The clause «كره الله ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «ثبّطهم» has no grammatical position, conjoined to كره الله ...
The clause «قيل ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to كره الله.
The clause «اقعدوا ...» is in the position of nominative as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) [Note: Because it is the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl) of the verb in the active voice.. or it is an explanation of the implied nāʾib fāʿil, which is the maṣdar (القول, the saying).].

* Morphology:
(الخروج): an aurally transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the verb خرج يخرج, of the class of نصر; its pattern is فعول with ḍamma on the fāʾ.
(العدّة): a noun meaning the wealth and weapons you have prepared; it may also be a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar) of the quadriliteral verb أعدّ, in the sense of preparation. Its pattern is فعلة with ḍamma then sukūn, and its plural, when it is a noun, is العدد with ḍamma on the ʿayn.
(انبعاث): a regular (qiyāsī) maṣdar of the five-letter verb انبعث; it is on the pattern of the past tense, with kasra on its third letter and an alif added before its last letter.

* Rhetoric:
2- Tatmīm (completion): in the noble verse, by mentioning مع القاعدين and not being content with mentioning اقعدوا. This is one of its fine subtleties, and we shall expand on it further, saying: had اقعدوا alone been said, it would have conveyed nothing but commanding them to sit back; and likewise "be with those who sit back". This benefit — joining them to these kinds of people described among the people as staying behind and sitting back, branded with this mark — is not obtained except from the wording of the verse..
[Translator's note: the source numbers this point 2; no point 1 is given.]

safi-cedvel:74-74.t:
* I'rab:
(يحلفون) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) ... and the waw is the fāʿil (agent); (بالله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يحلفون); (ما) negative; (قالوا) past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma ... and the waw is the fāʿil; the object of قالوا is omitted, i.e. the abuse that reached you from them; (الواو) resumptive; (اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied oath; (قد) a particle of realization (taḥqīq); (قالوا) like the first; (كلمة) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (الكفر) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (الواو) conjunction; (كفروا) like قالوا; (بعد) adverb, accusative, attached to (كفروا); (إسلام) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) conjunction; (همّوا) like قالوا; (الباء) a preposition; (ما) relative noun [Note: Or an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective (nakira mawṣūfa), with the returning pronoun omitted], indeclinable, in the position of genitive, attached to (همّوا); (لم) a particle of negation and jussive; (ينالوا) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), its sign of jussive being the dropping of the nūn.. and the waw is the fāʿil. (الواو) resumptive; (ما نقموا) like ما قالوا; (إلّا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (أن) a maṣdar-forming particle; (أغنى) past verb, indeclinable on an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (الله) the Divine Name, fāʿil, nominative; (الواو) conjunction; (رسول) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the Divine Name, nominative, and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi. (الفاء) resumptive; (إن) a conditional particle that makes the verb jussive; (يتوبوا) imperfect verb, jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), its sign of jussive being the dropping of the nūn ... and the waw is the fāʿil; (يك) defective imperfect verb, jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), its sign of jussive being the sukūn on the nūn that was dropped for lightening, and its subject (ism) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "huwa", i.e. seeking repentance; (خيرا) khabar (predicate) of يكن, accusative; (اللام) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (خيرا); (الواو) conjunction; (إن يتولّوا) like إن يتوبوا; (يعذّب) imperfect verb, jussive as the apodosis of the second condition, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (الله) the Divine Name, fāʿil, nominative; (عذابا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), standing in for the maṣdar because it shares its derivation, accusative; (أليما) naʿt (adjective), accusative; (في الدنيا) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يعذّب), its sign of genitive being the kasra implied on the alif; (الواو) conjunction; (الآخرة) conjoined to النداي, genitive; (الواو) conjunction; (ما) negative; (لهم) like the first, attached to a fronted khabar; (في الأرض) a preposition and its genitive noun, ḥāl (circumstantial) from (وليّ) — a naʿt placed before the noun it qualifies; (من) a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; (وليّ) genitive in wording, nominative in position, delayed mubtadaʾ (subject); (الواو) conjunction; (لا) redundant, to emphasize the negation; (نصير) conjoined to وليّ, following it in the genitive in wording.
[Translator's note: «النداي» in the source is evidently a typographical error for «الدنيا».]
The clause «يحلفون ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «ما قالوا» has no grammatical position, as the answer to the oath.
The clause «قالوا ... (the second)» has no grammatical position, as the answer to the implied oath.
The clause «كفروا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause قالوا.
The clause «همّوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause قالوا.
The clause «لم ينالوا» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (ما).
The clause «ما نقموا ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن أغناهم) is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi, its governing word being نقموا.
The clause «أغناهم» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «إن يتوبوا ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يك ...» has no grammatical position as the apodosis not joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «إن يتولّوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause إن يتوبوا.
The clause «يعذّبهم الله» has no grammatical position as the apodosis not joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «ما لهم ... من وليّ» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يعذّبهم.

* Rhetoric:
Confirming praise by what resembles blame (taʾkīd al-madḥ bimā yushbih al-dhamm): in His saying, Exalted is He, وَما نَقَمُوا إِلَّا أَنْ أَغْناهُمُ اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ; it contains sarcasm and the confirming of a thing by its opposite, as in the saying: ولا عيب فيهم غير أن سيوفهم (There is no fault in them except that their swords ...) — to the end of the verse. What is meant is: they did not resent faith for any reason except Allah the Exalted's having enriched them.

* Benefits:
In this verse comes His saying, Exalted is He, وَما لَهُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ مِنْ وَلِيٍّ وَلا نَصِيرٍ. We are concerned here with (من), since it occurs as redundant, and the noun after it (ولي) is genitive in wording and nominative in position, as a delayed mubtadaʾ. We shall set out below some of the rules of redundant (من):
1- There are three conditions for its being redundant:
a- That it be preceded by a negation, a prohibition, or a question with هل, as in His saying, Exalted is He: وَما تَسْقُطُ مِنْ وَرَقَةٍ إِلَّا يَعْلَمُها، ما تَرى فِي خَلْقِ الرَّحْمنِ مِنْ تَفاوُتٍ فَارْجِعِ الْبَصَرَ هَلْ تَرى مِنْ فُطُورٍ.
b- That the noun it governs be indefinite, as in the preceding examples.
c- That the noun it governs fall in the position of nominative as fāʿil, or of accusative as mafʿūl bihi, or as mubtadaʾ.
2- Analogy dictates that it is not added to the second of the two objects of ẓanna, nor to the third of the objects of aʿlama, because these are originally a khabar, while it enters upon the mubtadaʾ, as we have learned.

safi-cedvel:75-75.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (من) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a fronted khabar (predicate) [Note: Or it is an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) with no grammatical position.]; (من) relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject); (عاهد) past verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is "huwa", and it is the returning pronoun; (الله) the Divine Name, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (اللام) the lām that prepares for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa lil-qasam); (إن) a conditional particle that makes the verb jussive; (آتى) past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif, in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and (نا) an attached pronoun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is "huwa"; (من فضل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (آتى), and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (اللام) the lām of the oath; (نصدّقنّ) imperfect verb, indeclinable on fatḥa, in the position of nominative ... and (النون) the nūn of emphasis, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "naḥnu"; (الواو) conjunction; (لنكوننّ) like لنصدّقنّ, and it is defective (nāqiṣ); its subject (ism) is a latent pronoun, implied as "naḥnu"; (من الصالحين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the khabar of نكوننّ, its sign of genitive being the yāʾ.
The clause «منهم من ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «عاهد ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).
The clause «إن آتانا ...» has no grammatical position, an explanation of the meaning of the covenant with Allah.
The clause «نصدّقنّ ...» has no grammatical position, as the answer to the oath.. and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by the answer of the oath.
The clause «نكوننّ» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause نصدّقنّ.

* Morphology:
(نصدّقنّ): it contains the assimilation (idghām) of the tāʾ of tafaʿʿul into the ṣād; its origin is نتصدقنّ, and its wazn is نتفعّلن.

safi-cedvel:76-76.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) conjunction; (لمّا) an adverb meaning "when", containing the sense of a condition; (آتاهم من فضله) like آتانا من فضله [Note: in the previous verse (75), and the verb has no grammatical position.]; (بخلوا) past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma ... and the waw is the fāʿil (agent); (الباء) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (بخلوا); (الواو) conjunction; (تولّوا) past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif that was dropped because of the meeting of two sukūns ... and the waw is the fāʿil; (الواو) of ḥāl (circumstantial); (هم) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (معرضون) khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ), its sign of nominative being the waw.
The clause «أتاهم» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The clause «بخلوا» has no grammatical position, as the answer of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «تولّوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause بخلوا.
The clause «هم معرضون» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.

* Benefits:
The story of Thaʿlaba:
His name was Thaʿlaba ibn Ḥāṭib. The exegetes have related his story, the gist of which is
that he was a poor man who would not leave the mosque, so that he was nicknamed "the dove of the mosque".
