He used to say to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Pray to Allah to grant me wealth, and if He grants it to me I will surely give everyone with a right his right." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would say to him: "Are you not content to be like me? By the One in whose hand is my soul, if I wished the mountains to move with me as gold and silver, they would move." Then he asked him again, and he said to him: "Woe to you, O Thaʿlaba! A little for which you give thanks is better than much that you cannot bear." He kept pressing the Prophet ﷺ, so he prayed for him, saying: "O Allah, grant Thaʿlaba wealth." He took sheep, and they multiplied quickly as worms multiply, until Medina became too narrow for him, so he moved away and settled in one of its valleys, until he was praying the noon and afternoon prayers in congregation and leaving the others. They increased, so he moved further away until he abandoned the prayers except the Friday prayer, and they kept multiplying as worms multiply, until he abandoned the Friday prayer. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "What has Thaʿlaba done?" They told him, and he said: "Woe to Thaʿlaba!" And Allah, exalted be His praise, revealed: خُذْ مِنْ أَمْوالِهِمْ صَدَقَةً تُطَهِّرُهُمْ وَتُزَكِّيهِمْ بِها. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent two men to collect the zakāt and said to them: "Pass by Thaʿlaba and by so-and-so of Banū Sulaym." They set out until they came to Thaʿlaba, read to him the letter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and asked him for the ṣadaqa. He said: "This is nothing but jizya; this is nothing but the sister of jizya! What is this?
Go on until you finish, then pass by me." They returned to him, and he said the same as his first words. When they came to the Prophet ﷺ, he said to them, before they spoke to him: "Woe to Thaʿlaba!" and he prayed for blessing for the Sulamī, because he (أعطى واتقى وصدّق بالحسنى). They told him what Thaʿlaba and the Sulamī had done, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed this verse. Neither the Messenger of Allah ﷺ nor the caliphs after him accepted the ṣadaqa from him, until he died in the caliphate of ʿUthmān, may Allah be pleased with him.

safi-cedvel:16-16.t:
* I'rab:
(أم) a particle meaning "بل" plus the hamza, i.e. for transitional digression (al-iḍrāb al-intiqālī) and the interrogative of disapproval (al-istifhām al-inkārī); (حسبتم) past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn … and (تم) the fāʿil (agent); (أن) maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle; (تتركوا) passive imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn … and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (لمّا) particle of negation and jussive; (يعلم) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), given a kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ); (الذين) relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of an accusative, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (جاهدوا) past verb and its fāʿil; (من) preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of جاهدوا; (الواو) conjunction [Note: Or circumstantial, and the clause after it is a ḥāl of the fāʿil of جاهدوا, i.e.: "they strove while not taking an intimate ally".], (لم) like لمّا; (يتّخذوا) imperfect verb, jussive, the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn … and the wāw is the fāʿil; (من دون) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi of the verb يتخذوا; (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (الواو) conjunction; (لا) redundant (zāʾida), to reinforce the negation understood from His saying من دون; (رسول) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the Name of Majesty, genitive, and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) conjunction; (لا) like the last; (المؤمنين) like رسول, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ; (وليجة) mafʿūl bihi, accusative.
The interpreted maṣdar (ان تتركوا) is in the position of an accusative, standing in place of the object of حسبتم.
(الواو) resumptive; (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative; (خبير) khabar (predicate), nominative; (الباء) preposition; (ما) maṣdar-forming particle [Note: Or a relative noun, or an indefinite noun qualified by what follows, with the resumptive pronoun omitted, i.e. "تعملونه".] (تعملون) imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما تعملون) is in the position of a genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (خبير).
The clause «حسبتم …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «تتركوا» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «يعلم الله» is in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl.
The clause «جاهدوا …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
The clause «لم يتّخذوا» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «الله خبير …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «تعملون» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle-relative (ما).

* Morphology:
(وليجة): a noun meaning intimate associate (biṭāna), and anything you have inserted into something of which it is not part; its wazn is فعيلة [Translator's note: the source prints "فعلية"]. It is used in a single form for the singular, dual and plural, and it may be pluralised as ولائج and ولج, like صحائف and صحف.

safi-cedvel:17-17.t:
* I'rab:
(ما) particle of negation; (كان) incomplete past verb — an abrogator (nāsikh); (للمشركين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); (أن) maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle; (يعمروا) imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn … and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (مساجد) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative; (الله) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (شاهدين) ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, of the fāʿil of يعمروا, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ; (على أنفس) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (شاهدين), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (بالكفر) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (شاهدين).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يعمروا) is in the position of a nominative, the postponed noun of كان.
(أولئك) demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of a nominative, mubtadaʾ (subject).. and (الكاف) a particle of address; (حبطت) past verb, and (التاء) for the feminine; (أعمال) fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ), and (هم) like the first; (الواو) conjunction; (في النار) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (خالدون); (هم) detached pronoun in the position of a nominative, mubtadaʾ; (خالدون) khabar, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw.
The clause «ما كان للمشركين …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يعمروا …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «أولئك حبطت …» has no grammatical position, causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «حبطت أعمالهم» is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ أولئك.
The clause «هم خالدون» is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause حبطت أعمالهم.

* Benefits:
In this verse occurs His saying, the Exalted: ما كانَ لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ أَنْ يَعْمُرُوا مَساجِدَ اللَّهِ شاهِدِينَ عَلى أَنْفُسِهِمْ بِالْكُفْرِ. أن يعمروا: أن is a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle which, with the verb after it, is interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) that has a grammatical position; in the verse it is in the position of a nominative as the noun of كان, the interpretation being (ما كان للمشركين عمارة مساجد الله). Hence, when a verb is preceded by a maṣdar-forming particle, it is interpreted together with it as a maṣdar that has a grammatical position according to its place. We shall explain something about the maṣdar-forming particles, which are: 1- أنّ with its noun and khabar, as when we say: يسرني أنك ناجح ("it pleases me that you are successful"); the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of a nominative as fāʿil, the interpretation being يسرني نجاحك ("your success pleases me").
2- أن which puts the imperfect in the accusative, e.g.: أحب أن أفعل الخير, i.e. أحب فعل الخير ("I love doing good").
3- كي, e.g. ذهبت كي أبحث عن المعرفة ("I went in order to search for knowledge"), the interpretation being ذهبت للبحث عن الحقيقة ("I went for searching for the truth") [Translator's note: so in the source; the interpretation changes المعرفة to الحقيقة].
4- لو, preceded by the verb رغب or (ودّ) and what has their meaning, as in His saying, the Exalted: وَدُّوا لَوْ تُدْهِنُ فَيُدْهِنُونَ, the interpretation being ودّوا ادّهانك ("they wished for your compromising").
5- The hamza of equalisation (hamzat al-taswiya): so called because it is usually preceded by the word سواء, as in His saying, the Exalted: سَواءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ أَأَنْذَرْتَهُمْ أَمْ لَمْ تُنْذِرْهُمْ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ.
6- (ما): it comes as maṣdar-forming, as in His saying, the Exalted: ثُمَّ لا يَجِدُوا فِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ حَرَجاً مِمَّا قَضَيْتَ, i.e. "حرجا من قضائك" ("any discomfort at your judgement"); and it comes as maṣdar-forming and adverbial, as in His saying, the Exalted: وَأَوْصانِي بِالصَّلاةِ وَالزَّكاةِ ما دُمْتُ حَيًّا, i.e. "مدة حياتي" ("for the duration of my life").

safi-cedvel:18-18.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّما) the restraining particle (mā kāffa) and the restrained (makfūfa); (يعمر) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); (مساجد الله) its i'rab has already passed [Note: In the previous verse (18) [Translator's note: so in the source; the previous verse is (17)]], (من) relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of a nominative, fāʿil (agent); (آمن) past verb, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو", and it is the resumptive pronoun; (بالله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (آمن); (الواو) conjunction; (اليوم) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the Name of Majesty, genitive (majrūr); (الآخر) naʿt (adjective) of اليوم, genitive; (الواو) conjunction; (أقام) like آمن; (الصلاة) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (الواو) conjunction; (آتى الزكاة) like أقام الصلاة; (الواو) conjunction; (لم) particle of negation and jussive; (يخش) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, and the fāʿil is "هو"; (إلّا) particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (الله) the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الفاء) conjunction; (عسى) incomplete, inflexible (jāmid) past verb; (أولئك) demonstrative in the position of a nominative, the noun of عسى, and (الكاف) for address; (أن) maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle; (يكونوا) incomplete imperfect verb, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the noun of يكون; (من المهتدين) a preposition and its genitive noun, the khabar (predicate) of يكون.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يكونوا) is in the position of an accusative, the khabar of عسى.
The clause «يعمر …» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «آمن …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).
The clause «أقام …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «آتى …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «لم يخش إلّا الله» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «عسى أولئك …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يعمر.
The clause «يكونوا …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).

* Benefits:
1- In this verse occurs His saying, the Exalted: وَلَمْ يَخْشَ إِلَّا اللَّهَ. We parse إلا as a particle of restriction, and الله, the Name of Majesty, as accusative, out of reverence (manṣūb ʿalā al-taʿẓīm) [Translator's note: in the I'rab section above, however, the author parses it as mafʿūl bihi]. Exception is of several kinds:
1- Complete and affirmative: the complete is that in which the one from which the exception is made is mentioned, and the affirmative is that which is not preceded by a negation, as when we say: عاد المسافرون إلا زيدا ("the travellers returned except Zayd"). The sentence is affirmative and the exception complete because the one from which the exception is made, namely «المسافرون», is present. In this case we parse إلا as a particle of exception and زيدا as excepted by إلا, accusative and nothing else.
2- If the exception is complete and negated, i.e. preceded by a negation, e.g.: ما عاد المسافرون إلا زيدا, and إلا زيد. Here we parse زيدا as excepted by إلا, or إلا as a particle of restriction and زيد as a badal (substitute) of المسافرون, nominative like it with the ḍamma.
3- Incomplete and negated: the incomplete is that from which the one excepted from is omitted, and the negated is that which is preceded by a negation. In this case we parse إلّا as a particle of restriction and parse what follows it according to its position in the sentence, e.g.:
ما جاء إلا زيد: إلا a particle of restriction, زيد: fāʿil, nominative. ما رأيت إلّا زيدا: إلّا a particle of restriction, زيدا: mafʿūl bihi. وَما مُحَمَّدٌ إِلَّا رَسُولٌ: إلّا a particle of restriction, رسول: khabar, nominative.
2- The maintenance (ʿimāra) of mosques:
The scholars differed over this meaning occurring in the noble verse, namely the ʿimāra of mosques. One group said: building them and erecting them; another group said: frequenting them and filling them with prayer and remembrance. The jurists deduced from His saying, the Exalted, إِنَّما يَعْمُرُ مَساجِدَ اللَّهِ مَنْ آمَنَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ, that the maintenance and building of mosques is not valid except from one who believes in Allah and the Last Day; so whoever is not a believer in Allah is barred from maintaining a place in which Allah is worshipped. Sound ḥadīths have come down on the merit of building mosques; from ʿUthmān, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: Whoever builds a mosque for Allah, seeking thereby the face of Allah the Exalted, Allah will build for him a house in Paradise; and in one narration: Allah will build for him the like of it in Paradise.

safi-cedvel:19-19.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for the interrogative of wonder (istifhām taʿajjubī); (جعلتم) past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn.. and (تم) a pronoun, fāʿil (agent); (سقاية) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (الحاجّ) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (الواو) conjunction; (عمارة المسجد) like سقاية الحاجّ and conjoined to it; (الحرام) naʿt (adjective) of المسجد, genitive; (الكاف) preposition; (من) relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of a genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted second mafʿūl bihi of (جعلتم) [Note: Or attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) if the verb takes one object; it is on the interpretation of an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "كإيمان من آمن".. It is also possible to assume the omission in سقاية, i.e. "أهل سقاية الحاجّ" or "أصحاب سقاية الحاجّ".
(2, 3) In the previous verse (18).] (آمن بالله واليوم الآخر) its i'rab has already passed «2»; (الواو) conjunction; (جاهد) like آمن «3»; (في سبيل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (جاهد); (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi; (لا) negative; (يستوون) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ).. and the wāw is the fāʿil; (عند) adverb, accusative, attached to (يستوون); (الله) like the last word; (الواو) resumptive; (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative; (لا) negative; (يهدي) imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ, and the fāʿil is "هو"; (القوم) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الظالمين) naʿt of القوم, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ.
The clause «جعلتم …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «آمن بالله …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).
The clause «جاهد …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «لا يستوون …» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «الله لا يهدي …» has no grammatical position, resumptive, containing the meaning of causation.
The clause «لا يهدي …» is in the position of a nominative, the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (الله).

* Morphology:
(سقاية): maṣdar (verbal noun) of سقى يسقي, like سعاية and حماية; or it is a noun for the place of giving water, used as a maṣdar meaning giving water; its wazn is فعالة with kasra on the fāʾ, and the yāʾ was not converted into a hamza because the feminine tāʾ comes after it.
(الحاجّ): active participle from the triliteral حجّ; its wazn is فاعل, and its ʿayn and lām are from a single letter.
(عمارة): maṣdar of يعمر الله منزله, i.e. He made it flourishing. Its wazn is فعالة with kasra on the fāʾ.
(يستوون): it contains a weak-letter change by quiescence and then by deletion; its original form is يستويون — with ḍamma on the second yāʾ — the ḍamma on the yāʾ was felt heavy, so its vowel was transferred to the wāw before it and it was made quiescent — a weak-letter change by quiescence (iʿlāl bi-l-taskīn) — then the yāʾ was deleted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters — the yāʾ and the wāw of the plural — giving يستوون; its wazn is يفتعون.

* Rhetoric:
The crafted simile (al-tashbīh al-ṣināʿī) by which the speech takes the form of disapproval: in the saying of Allah the Exalted «أَجَعَلْتُمْ سِقايَةَ الْحاجِّ وَعِمارَةَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرامِ كَمَنْ آمَنَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ». This is a disapproval of likening the polytheists to the believers, and their nullified deeds to their established deeds, and of placing them on an equal footing. In that is the fullest indication [Translator's note: the source prints "أو في", read here as "أوفى"] of the magnification of the state of the believer through faith, which is one of the purposes of the crafted simile.

safi-cedvel:111-111.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّ) a particle resembling the verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) — ; (الله) the noun of inna, accusative (manṣūb); (اشترى) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "he"; (من المؤمنين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (اشترى), the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ; (أنفس) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) a conjunction; (أموالهم) like أنفسهم and conjoined to it; (الباء) a preposition; (أنّ) a particle resembling the verb — an abrogator — ; (اللام) a preposition, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); (الجنّة) the noun of anna, accusative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ لهم الجنّة) is in the position of genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (اشترى) by its being made to include the meaning of "exchanged (استبدل)" [Note: Abū al-Baqāʾ al-ʿUkbarī called it the bāʾ of counter-value (bāʾ al-muqābala), i.e. "for their being entitled to Paradise".].
(يقاتلون) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil; (في سبيل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يقاتلون); (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi; (الفاء) a conjunction; (يقتلون) like يقاتلون; (الواو) a conjunction; (يقتلون) an imperfect verb, passive, nominative, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (عدا) a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, i.e. "He promised them a promise (وعدهم وعدا)", and it emphasises the content of what precedes it [Translator's note: The source prints «(عدا)»; the Quranic word is «وعدا».]; (على) a preposition, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive — attached to (وعدا); (حقّا) a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb, emphasising the content of what precedes it, i.e. "that promise has been made true, truly (حقّ ذلك الوعد حقّا)" [Note: Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted making it an adjective of the first maṣdar (وعدا).], (في التوراة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of (وعدا) [Note: Or attached to اشترى), because its meaning is "Allah promised them Paradise for striving in His way"; every nation was commanded to strive and was promised Paradise for it; that is why (الإنجيل والقرآن) were conjoined to التوراة.], (الواو) a conjunction in both places; (الإنجيل القرآن) two words conjoined by the two conjunctions to التوراة, genitive (majrūr); (الواو) parenthetical; (من) an interrogative noun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (أوفى) khabar, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied on the alif; (بعهد) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أوفى), and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi; (من اللَّه) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أوفى); (الفاء) connecting the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition; (استبشروا) an imperative verb, indeclinable on the deletion of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (ببيع) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (استبشروا), and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الذي) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive as a naʿt of بيع; (بايعتم) a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn, and its fāʿil [Translator's note: The sentence breaks off here in the source; the fāʿil is the attached pronoun تم.]; (به) like عليه, attached to (بايعتم); (الواو) resumptive; (ذلك) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ, and (اللام) for distance and (الكاف) for address; (هو) a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) [Note: Or a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ, whose khabar is (الفوز), and the nominal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ ذلك.]; (الفوز) khabar, nominative; (العظيم) a naʿt of الفوز, nominative.
The clause «إنّ اللَّه اشترى …» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «اشترى …» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of inna.
The clause «يقاتلون …» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) [Note: It cannot be parsed as a ḥāl (circumstantial), because the clause is declarative in wording but performative (inshāʾ) in meaning, since it is a command, and what is a command cannot be a ḥāl.].
The clause «يقتلون» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يقاتلون.
The clause «يقتلون» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يقاتلون.
The clause «من أوفى …» has no grammatical position, being parenthetical.
The clause «استبشروا» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if you have pledged to Allah for Paradise, then rejoice in your sale…".
The clause «بايعتم به» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذي).
The clause «ذلك.. الفوز …» has no grammatical position, being resumptive and explanatory of cause (taʿlīliyya).

* Rhetoric:
1- The implicit metaphor and the dependent metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-makniyya wa-l-tabaʿiyya): in His saying, the Exalted, «إِنَّ اللَّهَ اشْتَرى مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَنْفُسَهُمْ وَأَمْوالَهُمْ بِأَنَّ لَهُمُ الْجَنَّةَ», where Allah the Exalted's acceptance from the believers of their souls and wealth which they spent in His way, the Exalted, and His rewarding them with Paradise in return for it, is expressed as purchase, by way of the dependent metaphor; then He made the thing sold — which is the mainstay and the aim in the contract — the souls and wealth of the believers, and the price — which is the means in the transaction — Paradise.
2- Iltifāt (shift of address): in His saying, the Exalted, «فَاسْتَبْشِرُوا» there is a shift to second-person address, as honour upon honour for them and an increase of joy upon joy. Istibshār is showing joy, and the sīn in it is not for requesting, as in استوقد and أوقد. The fāʾ is to make the rejoicing, or the command to it, follow upon what precedes it, i.e. "if that is so, then be glad with the utmost gladness and rejoice with the utmost joy at the Paradise you have won".
3- Tadhyīl (appended confirmation): it is that the speaker appends to his speech, after its meaning is complete, a clause that confirms what precedes it. This addition is of two kinds: a- a kind that adds nothing to the first meaning but only emphasises and confirms it.
b- and a kind that the speaker casts in the form of a current proverb, so that the meaning becomes widely known through its frequent circulation on tongues. Both kinds have come in this noble verse:
a- His saying, the Exalted, «وَعْداً عَلَيْهِ حَقًّا»: the speech was complete and finished before that, then the appended clause came to confirm and emphasise what precedes it.
b- His saying «وَمَنْ أَوْفى بِعَهْدِهِ مِنَ اللَّهِ», casting it in the form of a proverb. So glory be to the One who speaks such speech.

safi-cedvel:112-112.t:
* I'rab:
(التائبون) the khabar (predicate) of a necessarily omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "they (هم)", so it is an adjective cut off for praise [Note: It may be a mubtadaʾ with what follows as multiple khabars; or a mubtadaʾ qualified by what follows it, whose khabar is الآمرون; or with its khabar omitted, its implied form being "are among the people of Paradise (من أهل الجنّة)". It is also said that (التائبون) may be a badal (substitute) of the pronoun in يقاتلون in the previous verse.], the sign of the nominative being the wāw; (العابدون … الآمرون) each of these words is a khabar of the omitted mubtadaʾ, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the wāw; (بالمعروف) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (الآمرون); (الواو) a conjunction; (الناهون) conjoined to (الآمرون), nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw; (عن المنكر) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (الناهون); (الواو) a conjunction; (الحافظون) conjoined to (الآمرون or التائبون), nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw; (لحدود) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (الحافظون); (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (الواو) resumptive; (بشّر) an imperative verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is "you"; (المؤمنين) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ.
The clause «(هم) التائبون …» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «بشّر …» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.

* Morphology:
(التائبون): plural of التائب, the active participle of تاب; its pattern is فاعل. Its ʿayn has been changed into a hamza because it comes after the alif of فاعل; its origin is تاوب. Such is the case of the active participle of every hollow weak verb, where the weak letter is changed into a hamza.
(الحامدون): plural of الحامد, the active participle of the three-letter verb حمد; its pattern is فاعل.
(السائحون): plural of السائح, the active participle of the three-letter verb ساح; its pattern is فاعل. It has been treated like التائب in the change; its origin is سايح.
(الآمرون): plural of الآمر, the active participle of the three-letter verb أمر; its pattern is فاعل. The hamza which is the fāʾ of the word has been merged with the alif of فاعل, with a madda over it; the origin is أمر.
(الناهون): plural of الناهي, the active participle of the three-letter verb نهى; its pattern is فاعل. In الناهي the yāʾ has been restored to its origin because the letter before it has kasra. In (الناهون) there is iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion, because it is a defective noun (manqūṣ); its origin is الناهيون: the ḍamma on the yāʾ was felt to be heavy, so it was given sukūn and the ḍamma was transferred to the hāʾ — which is iʿlāl by sukūn — then the yāʾ was deleted because of the meeting of two sukūns — iʿlāl by deletion.
(الحافظون): plural of الحافظ, the active participle of the three-letter verb حفظ; its pattern is فاعل.

safi-cedvel:113-113.t:
* I'rab:
(ما) negative; (كان) an incomplete past verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) — ; (للنبيّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, the fronted khabar (predicate) of kāna; (الواو) a conjunction; (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of genitive, conjoined to النبيّ; (آمنوا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (أن) a maṣdar-forming particle causing the subjunctive; (يستغفروا) an imperfect verb, subjunctive (manṣūb), the sign of the subjunctive being the deletion of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (للمشركين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يستغفروا), the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يستغفروا..) is in the position of nominative as the postponed noun of kāna.
(الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (لو) a non-jussive conditional particle; (كانوا) an incomplete past verb, and its noun [is the wāw]; (أولي) the khabar of كانوا, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ, being treated like the sound masculine plural; (قربى) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the kasra implied (muqaddar) on the alif; (من بعد) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the negated seeking of forgiveness; (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle [Note: Or a relative noun in the position of genitive, with the clause after it as its ṣila and the referent pronoun omitted, i.e. "that which became clear to them by it (الذي تبيّن لهم به)"; but supposing the referent together with the preposition is rare.]; (تبيّن) a past verb; (اللام) a preposition, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive — attached to (تبيّن); (أنّ) a particle resembling the verb, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of anna; (أصحاب) khabar, nominative (marfūʿ); (الجحيم) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.
[Translator's note: The words "[is the wāw]" are added for clarity; the source has only «واسمه» ("and its noun").]
The interpreted maṣdar (ما تبيّن) is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنهم أصحاب..) is in the position of nominative as the fāʿil of تبيّن.
The clause «ما كان للنبيّ …» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «يستغفروا …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «كانوا أولي قربى» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of المشركين.
The apodosis (jawāb) of لو is omitted, indicated by the preceding speech, i.e. "even if they were…, it would not be for them to seek forgiveness…".
The clause «تبيّن …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle relative (ما).

* Benefits:
The statements of the exegetes on the occasions of revelation of this verse conflict. Some said:
It was revealed concerning Abū Ṭālib, the uncle of the Prophet ﷺ, and that was
that the Prophet ﷺ wanted to seek forgiveness for him after his death, and Allah forbade him from that. What indicates this is what is narrated from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib from his father, who said: When death came to Abū Ṭālib, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came and found with him Abū Jahl and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Umayya ibn al-Mughīra, and he said: "O uncle, say 'There is no god but Allah', a word with which I will argue for you before Allah." Abū Jahl and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Umayya said: "Will you turn away from the religion of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ kept offering it to him and they kept returning to that statement, until the last thing Abū Ṭālib said to them was: "I am on the religion of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib," and he did not say the testimony. The Messenger ﷺ said: "I will certainly seek forgiveness for you as long as I am not forbidden from doing so." So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse. Qatāda said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "I will certainly seek forgiveness for my father as Ibrāhīm sought forgiveness for his father," and Allah revealed this verse. Al-Ṭabarī narrated with his chain, saying: It was mentioned to us that some men among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O Prophet of Allah, among our forefathers were those who were good neighbours, maintained the ties of kinship, freed captives and fulfilled pledges; shall we not seek forgiveness for them?" The Prophet ﷺ said: "Yes, by Allah, I will certainly seek forgiveness for my father as Ibrāhīm sought forgiveness for his father." Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed this verse.

safi-cedvel:114-114.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (ما كان) like the earlier one [Note: In the previous verse (113)], (استغفار) the noun of kāna, nominative (marfūʿ); (إبراهيم) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa; (لأبيه) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) استغفار, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ, and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (إلّا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (عن موعدة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) of kāna [Note: I.e. "except arising from a promise (إلّا ناشئا عن موعدة)".], (وعد) a past verb, and (ها) a pronoun, first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (إيّاه) a detached pronoun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative as second mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil (agent) is "he", i.e. Ibrāhīm; (الفاء) a conjunction; (لمّا) an adverb meaning "when (حين)", containing the sense of condition, attached to (تبرّأ); (تبيّن له أنّه عدو) like «تبيّن لهم أنّهم أصحاب» [Note: In verse (113) of this surah.], (لله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (عدوّ); (تبرأ) like وعد; (منه) like له, attached to (تبرّأ); (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) — ; (إبراهيم) the noun of inna, accusative (manṣūb), prevented from tanwīn because of being a proper name and foreign; (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis; (آوّاه) the khabar of inna, nominative; (حليم) a second khabar, nominative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّه عدوّ) is in the position of nominative as the fāʿil of تبيّن.
The clause «ما كان استغفار …» has no grammatical position, being resumptive, to confirm what preceded [Note: It is said to be an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) despite the entry of the wāw.]. The clause «وعدها إيّاه» is in the position of genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of موعدة.
The clause «تبيّن أنّه عدوّ» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «تبرّأ منه» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «إنّ إبراهيم لأواه» has no grammatical position, being explanatory of cause (taʿlīliyya).

* Morphology:
(استغفار): a regular maṣdar (verbal noun) of the six-letter verb استغفر; its pattern is استفعال — on the pattern of its past tense, with kasra on its third letter and an alif added before the last letter. (موعدة): a mīmī maṣdar of the three-letter verb وعد, the tāʾ being added for intensiveness; its pattern is مفعلة with fatḥa on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn, because its verb is an assimilated weak verb (mithāl) whose fāʾ is deleted in the imperfect.
(أوّاه): an intensive form from التأوّه, irregularly formed; its pattern is فعّال. Quṭrub alone reported that there is a three-letter verb آه يؤوه, like قام يقوم, but the grammarians rejected that from him. الأوّاه has many meanings, the best known being the statement of Abū ʿUbayda, i.e. "one who sighs out of compassion and fear, and who humbly implores with certainty, constancy and obedience".
[Translator's note: The source has «قول أبو عبيدة»; grammatically «قول أبي عبيدة».]

safi-cedvel:115-115.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) a conjunction — or resumptive — ; (ما كان) like the previous one [Note: In the previous verse (113). (2, 3) In the previous verse (114)], (الله) the noun of kāna, nominative (marfūʿ) [Translator's note: The source misprints «مرفوا» for «مرفوع».]; (اللام) the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd) — or of negation — ; (يضلّ) an imperfect verb, subjunctive (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām, and the fāʿil (agent) is "he"; (قوما) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative; (بعد) an adverb, accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يضلّ); (إذ) an adverb, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; (هدى) a past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is "he"; (حتى) a particle of limit and a preposition; (يبيّن) an imperfect verb, subjunctive by an implied أن after حتّى; (اللام) a preposition, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive — attached to (يبيّن); (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi; (يتّقون) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (إنّ الله.. عليم) like «إنّ إبراهيم لأوّاه» «2»; (بكلّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to عليم; (شيء) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr).
The clause «ما كان ليضلّ …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause «ما كان استغفار» «3», or it is resumptive.
The clause «يضلّ …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle relative (أن).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يضلّ..) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) of kāna.
The clause «هداهم» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «يبيّن لهم» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the implied particle relative (أن).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يبيّن..) is in the position of genitive by (حتّى), attached to (يضلّ).
The clause «يتّقون» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «إنّ الله … عليم» has no grammatical position, having the status of an explanation of cause (taʿlīl).
116-
[Translator's note: The markers «2» and «3» refer to the author's footnotes, which in the source are merged into the single note above: «2» = verse 114 (إنّ إبراهيم لأوّاه), «3» = verse 114 (ما كان استغفار). The final «116-» is a stray page/verse marker in the source.]

safi-cedvel:47-47.t:
* I'rab:
(لو خرجوا) like لو أرادوا [Note: In the previous verse (46).], (في) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (خرجوا), with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. in your army. (ما) a particle of negation. (زادوا) like أرادوا, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (الّا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). (خبالا) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb) [Note: In the view of al-Zamakhsharī it is an excepted (mustathnā) by (إلا), connected (muttaṣil), and the second object is omitted, i.e. they would not have added to you anything but corruption.], (الواو) conjunction. (اللام) linking the apodosis of law. (أوضعوا) like أرادوا. (خلال) an adverb of place, indeclinable (mabnī), attached to (أوضعوا), and (كم) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). [Translator's note: so in the source — "indeclinable"; خلال in the verse is in fact declined (accusative خِلالَ), and the source's own Morphology note calls it a non-inflecting (ghayr mutaṣarrif) adverb.] (يبغون) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ).. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi [Note: This pronoun was originally genitive by the lām, i.e. they seek for you; when the lām was dropped the pronoun was attached to the verb, so it became a mafʿūl bihi by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa).], (الفتنة) mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya). (فيكم) like the first, attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate). (سمّاعون) a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw. (لهم) like فيكم, attached to (سمّاعون). (الواو) resumptive. (الله عليم بالظالمين) like الله عليم بالمتّقين [Note: In verse (44) of this surah.].
The clause «خرجوا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «ما زادوكم ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a condition not causing the jussive.
The clause «أوضعوا..» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the apodosis of the condition.
The clause «يبغونكم» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of أوضعوا.
The clause «فيكم سمّاعون ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the object of يبغونكم or of its fāʿil [Note: It may be resumptive, and then it has no grammatical position.].
The clause «الله عليم» has no grammatical position: resumptive.

* Morphology:
(خلال): an adverbial noun, non-inflecting (ghayr mutaṣarrif), indeclinable; when it takes on other meanings it becomes declinable and leaves adverbial use.

* Rhetoric:
Istiʿāra makniyya (implicit metaphor): in His saying, the Exalted: وَلَأَوْضَعُوا خِلالَكُمْ. In the speech there is an implicit metaphor, since tale-bearing is likened to riding camels in their running and moving about, and hurrying (al-īḍāʿ) [Translator's note: the source writes الإيضاح here, apparently for الإيضاع] is affirmed for it by way of imaginative ascription (takhyīl). The meaning is: they would have run about among you with tale-bearing and with corrupting relations between you.
It has also been said: in it is a subordinate metaphor (istiʿāra tabaʿiyya), since the speed of their corrupting relations by tale-bearing is likened to the speed of the rider's journey; then al-īḍāʿ, which is for camels, is borrowed for it. The origin is: they would have hurried the mounts of their tale-bearing among you; then "tale-bearing" was dropped and the muḍāf ilayhi put in its place, so it was said: they would have hurried their mounts; then "the mounts" were dropped.

safi-cedvel:48-48.t:
* I'rab:
(اللام) occurring in the response to an implied oath. (قد) a particle of realisation (taḥqīq). (ابتغوا) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma ... and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). (الفتنة) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb). (من) a preposition. (قبل) a noun indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (ابتغوا). (الواو) conjunction. (قلّبوا) like ابتغوا. (اللام) a preposition and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (قلّبوا). (الأمور) mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (حتّى) a particle of limit and a preposition [Note: Or a particle of inception (ḥarf ibtidāʾ), and the clause after it is resumptive with no grammatical position.], (جاء) a past verb. (الحقّ) fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ). (الواو) conjunction. (ظهر أمر) like جاء الحقّ. (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr). (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya). (هم) a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ (subject). (كارهون) khabar (predicate), nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن جاء ...) is in the position of genitive by (حتّى), attached to (قلّبوا) [Note: Or attached to an omitted verb, i.e. they continued turning matters over until … came.].
The clause «ابتغوا ...» has no grammatical position: the response to an implied oath.
The clause «قلّبوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause ابتغوا ...
The clause «جاء الحقّ» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle relative (أن).
The clause «ظهر أمر الله» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause جاء الحقّ.
The clause «هم كارهون» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

* Morphology:
(ابتغوا): it has iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion; its origin is ابتغاوا. Two sukūns met, so the alif was deleted for this reason, and what preceded it remained with fatḥa as an indication of it. Its pattern is افتعوا.

* Rhetoric:
Majāz (trope): in His saying, the Exalted: وَقَلَّبُوا لَكَ الْأُمُورَ, i.e. the schemes; turning them over is a trope for planning them; or [the matters are] the opinions, and it is a trope for searching through them, i.e. they plotted schemes and stratagems against you, or they turned opinions over in order to bring your cause to nothing.

* Benefits:
An important point about (حتى):
In this verse occurs His saying, the Exalted: وَقَلَّبُوا لَكَ الْأُمُورَ حَتَّى جاءَ الْحَقُّ. (حتى) has many states, but we shall explain its state in this verse, seeking benefit, and because this escapes many people. Ibn Hishām listed several states of حتى, and among what he said is:
Among the uses of حتى is that it occurs as a particle of inception, i.e. a particle after which the clause is begun anew. It enters the nominal clause, as in the saying of al-Farazdaq:
فوا عجبا حتى كليب تسبّني ... كأنّ أباها نهشل أو مجاشع
(How astonishing — even Kulayb reviles me, as if its father were Nahshal or Mujāshiʿ!)
It also enters the verbal clause whose verb is imperfect, as in the saying of Ḥassān:
يغشون حتى ما تهرّ كلابهم ... لا يسألون عن السواد المقبل
(They are visited so often that their dogs no longer snarl; they do not ask about the approaching throng.)
Likewise it enters the verbal clause whose verb is past, as has come in the verse we are dealing with, and likewise His saying, the Exalted: ثُمَّ بَدَّلْنا مَكانَ السَّيِّئَةِ الْحَسَنَةَ حَتَّى عَفَوْا وَقالُوا قَدْ مَسَّ آباءَنَا الضَّرَّاءُ وَالسَّرَّاءُ
Ibn Mālik claimed that حتى here is a particle of limit and a preposition, and that after it is an implied أن. I know of no predecessor for him in that, and it involves the strain of supposing an implied element without necessity. Ibn Mālik said likewise of حتى entering إذا in His saying, the Exalted: حَتَّى إِذا فَشِلْتُمْ وَتَنازَعْتُمْ, and considered (إذا) to be in the position of genitive by حتى. This view was held before him by al-Akhfash and others, but the majority hold the contrary, that it is a particle of inception.

safi-cedvel:49-49.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive. (من) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate), i.e. some of them.. (من) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject). (يقول) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the fāʿil (agent) is "he", which is the referring pronoun (ʿāʾid). (ائذن) an imperative verb of supplication, and the fāʿil is "you". (اللام) a preposition and (الياء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (ائذن). (الواو) conjunction. (لا) prohibitive of supplication, causing the jussive. (تفتن) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), and (النون) is for protection (wiqāya), and (الياء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "you". (ألا) a particle of alerting. (في الفتنة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (سقطوا), which is a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma.. and the wāw is the fāʿil. (الواو) conjunction. (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) — (جهنّم) the noun of inna, accusative (manṣūb), and it is barred from nunation (a diptote). (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis. (محيطة) khabar, nominative. (بالكافرين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (محيطة), the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
The clause «منهم من يقول ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يقول ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).
The clause «ائذن ...» is in the position of accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «لا تفتنّي ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause ائذن.
The clause «سقطوا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «إنّ جهنّم لمحيطة ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause سقطوا.

* Rhetoric:
1- Majāz mursal (metonymic trope): in His saying, the Exalted: أَلا فِي الْفِتْنَةِ سَقَطُوا, the relation being that of the state (ḥāliyya), i.e. into Hell. The state is mentioned and the place is meant, because a person does not fall into trial (fitna), since it is one of the abstract notions; rather he settles in its place. So using fitna for its place is a trope in which the state is mentioned and the place meant.
2- Tamthīl (representative image): in His saying, the Exalted: وَإِنَّ جَهَنَّمَ لَمُحِيطَةٌ بِالْكافِرِينَ. The speech may be made a tamthīl, by likening their state when the causes surround them to their state when the Fire surrounds them, the deeds they are engaged in being the Fire itself, but appearing in the form of deeds in this life and appearing in fiery form in the other life — as has been said of the parallel in His saying, the Exalted: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَأْكُلُونَ أَمْوالَ الْيَتامى ظُلْماً إِنَّما يَأْكُلُونَ فِي بُطُونِهِمْ ناراً

safi-cedvel:50-50.t:
* I'rab:
(إن) a conditional particle causing the jussive. (تصب) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). (الكاف) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (حسنة) fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ). (تسؤ) an imperfect verb, jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "it" (hiya). (الواو) conjunction. (إن تصبك مصيبة) like إن تصبك حسنة. (يقولوا) an imperfect verb, jussive as the apodosis of the second condition, the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn ... and the wāw is the fāʿil. (قد) a particle of realisation (taḥqīq). (أخذنا) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn.. and (نا) a pronoun, fāʿil. (أمرنا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb).. and (نا) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (من) a preposition. (قبل) an indeclinable noun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أخذنا). (الواو) conjunction. (يتولّوا) like يقولوا, and conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it. (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya). (هم) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). (فرحون) khabar (predicate), nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw.
The clause «تصبك حسنة ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «تسؤهم» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a jussive-causing condition, not joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «تصبك مصيبة ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «يقولوا ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of the second condition, not joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «قد أخذنا ...» is in the position of accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «يتولّوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يقولوا.
The clause «هم فرحون» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of يتولّوا.

* Morphology:
(يتولّوا): it has iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion; its origin is يتولّاوا ... two sukūns met, the alif and the wāw, so the alif was deleted. Its pattern is يتفعّوا.

safi-cedvel:51-51.t:
* I'rab:
(قل) an imperative verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is "you". (لن) a particle of negation and the accusative. (يصيب) an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), and (نا) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (إلّا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as fāʿil. (كتب) a past verb. (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ), and the referring pronoun (ʿāʾid) is omitted, i.e. He wrote it. (اللام) a preposition and (نا) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (كتب). (هو) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). (مولى) khabar (predicate), nominative, the sign of the nominative being the implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the alif, and (نا) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (الواو) conjunction. (على الله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يتوكّل). (الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition [Note: Al-Jamal said in his gloss on Tafsīr al-Jalālayn: "The fāʾ is causal.. to indicate that Allah the Exalted loves reliance (tawakkul), as in His saying «فإيّاي فارهبون»." End quote.], (اللام) the lām of command. (يتوكّل) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), and given a kasra because of the meeting of two sukūns. (المؤمنون) fāʿil, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw.
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «لن يصيبنا إلّا ما ...» is in the position of accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «كتب الله ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (ما).
The clause «هو مولانا ...» has no grammatical position: causal — or parenthetical [Translator's note: the source writes اعراضيّة, apparently for اعتراضيّة].
The clause «ليتوكّل المؤمنون» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e. if the affliction is from Allah, or if what is written is from Allah, then let the believers rely on Allah.

* Rhetoric:
Using the overt noun where a pronoun would be expected (al-iẓhār fī maqām al-iḍmār), in His saying, the Exalted: وَعَلَى اللَّهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ.
For the Majestic Name is made overt where a pronoun would be expected, to show the seeking of blessing from it and delight in it.

safi-cedvel:77-77.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) conjunction; (أعقب) past verb, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil (agent) is "huwa", i.e. Allah [Note: The pronoun may refer back to the miserliness, i.e. the miserliness bequeathed them a hypocrisy firmly lodged in their hearts, continuing until the day they meet Him.]; (نفاقا) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb); (في قلوب) a preposition and its genitive noun, naʿt (adjective) of (نفاقا), and (هم) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (إلى يوم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a second naʿt of (نفاقا), i.e. "continuing"; (يلقون) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ).. and the waw is the fāʿil, and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (الباء) a preposition; (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle; (أخلفوا) past verb with its fāʿil; (الله) the Divine Name, mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (ما) relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative as second mafʿūl bihi; (وعدوا) like أخلفوا, and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi.
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (ما أخلفوا) is in the position of genitive by the bāʾ — which is causal — attached to (أعقبهم).
(الواو) conjunction; (بما كانوا) like بما أخلفوا.. and the waw is the subject (ism) of the defective verb; (يكذبون) like يلقون.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما كانوا ...) is in the position of genitive by the bāʾ, attached to what the first maṣdar is attached to, so it is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it.
The clause «أعقبهم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause بخلوا or تولّوا [Note: in the previous verse (76).], a conjoining of the effect to the cause.
The clause «يلقونه» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «أخلفوا» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (ما).
The clause «وعدوه» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «كانوا ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the second particle relative (ما).
The clause «يكذبون» is in the position of accusative as the khabar (predicate) of (كانوا).

* Morphology:
(نفاقا): a maṣdar transmitted by hearing (samāʿī) of the four-letter verb نافق; its wazn is فعال with kasra on the fāʾ ... The regular (qiyāsī) maṣdar is المنافقة.

safi-cedvel:78-78.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for the rebuking, reproaching interrogative; (لم) a particle of negation and jussive; (يعلموا) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), its sign of jussive being the dropping of the nūn ... and the waw is the fāʿil (agent); (أنّ) a particle resembling the verb — an abrogator (nāsikh); (الله) the Divine Name, the subject (ism) of anna, accusative (manṣūb); (يعلم) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the fāʿil is "huwa"; (سرّ) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الواو) conjunction; (نجواهم) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to سرّهم, accusative, its sign of accusative being the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif; (الواو) conjunction; (أنّ الله) like the first; (علّام) khabar (predicate) of anna, nominative; (الغيوب) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr).
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أنّ الله يعلم) is in the position of accusative, standing in place of the two objects of يعلموا.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ الله علّام..) is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the first interpreted maṣdar as a conjoining of cause, i.e. "and because Allah ...".
The clause «لم يعلموا ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يعلم ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of anna.

safi-cedvel:79-79.t:
* I'rab:
(الذين) relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) [Note: It may be the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "hum".]; (يلمزون) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ).. and the waw is the fāʿil (agent); (المطّوّعين) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), its sign of accusative being the yāʾ; (من المؤمنين) a preposition and its genitive noun, ḥāl (circumstantial) from المطّوّعين; (في الصدقات) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يلمزون), with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "in giving the alms"; (الواو) conjunction; (الذين) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to المطّوّعين, in the position of accusative; (لا) negative; (يجدون) like يلمزون; (إلّا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (جهد) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الفاء) conjunction; (يسخرون) like يلمزون; (من) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (يسخرون); (سخر) past verb; (الله) the Divine Name, fāʿil, nominative; (منهم) like the first, attached to (سخر); and (الواو) conjunction; (لهم) like منهم, attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (عذاب) delayed mubtadaʾ, nominative; (أليم) naʿt (adjective) of عذاب, nominative.
The clause «الذين يلمزون ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يلمزون ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «لا يجدون ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the second relative (الذين).
The clause «يسخرون منهم» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يلمزون.
The clause «سخر الله منهم ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين يلمزون) [Note: Or it is resumptive if it is not a khabar, or if the clause يسخرون is the khabar with the fāʾ redundant ... or it is explicative (tafsīriyya) if (الذين يلمزون) is parsed as the mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb explained by: سخر الله منهم.].
The clause «لهم عذاب ...» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the khabar clause.

* Morphology:
(المطّوّعين): plural of المطّوّع, active participle of the five-letter verb تطوّع.. It contains the change (ibdāl) of the tāʾ of tafaʿʿul into ṭāʾ; its origin is المتطوّع, and its wazn is متفعّل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.

safi-cedvel:80-80.t:
* I'rab:
(استغفر) imperative verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is "anta"; (اللام) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (استغفر); (أو) a particle of choice (takhyīr); (لا) prohibitive, making the verb jussive; (تستغفر) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), and the fāʿil is "anta"; (لهم) like the first, attached to (تستغفر); (إن) a conditional particle that makes the verb jussive; (تستغفر لهم) like the first, and it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (سبعين) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, accusative (manṣūb), its sign of accusative being the yāʾ, since it is treated like the sound masculine plural; (مرّة) tamyīz (specification), accusative; (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (لن) a particle of negation and accusative; (يغفر) imperfect verb, accusative; (الله) the Divine Name, fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ); (لهم) like the first, attached to (يغفر); (ذلك) demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), the reference being to the impossibility of forgiveness for them ...
and (اللام) for distance and (الكاف) for address; (الباء) a preposition; (أنّ) a particle resembling the verb, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of accusative as the subject (ism) of anna; (كفروا) past verb, indeclinable on ḍamma ... and the waw is the fāʿil; (بالله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (كفروا); (الواو) conjunction; (رسول) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the Divine Name, genitive (majrūr), and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الواو) resumptive; (الله) the Divine Name, mubtadaʾ, nominative; (لا) negative; (يهدي) imperfect verb, nominative, its sign of nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "huwa"; (القوم) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative; (الفاسقين) naʿt (adjective) of القوم, accusative, its sign of accusative being the yāʾ.
The clause «استغفر ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «لا تستغفر ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «ان تستغفر لهم ...» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «لن يغفر الله ...» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «ذلك بأنّهم ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «كفروا ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of anna.
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أنّهم كفروا) is in the position of genitive by the bāʾ, attached to the omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ.
The clause «الله لا يهدي ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive, containing the sense of causation.
The clause «لا يهدي ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الله).

* Rhetoric:
The command and the prohibition departing from their original meaning to another meaning, namely equating the two alternatives (taswiya): as in His saying, Exalted is He: أَنْفِقُوا طَوْعاً أَوْ كَرْهاً, and the verse:
أسيئي بنا أو أحسني لا ملومة ... لدينا ولا مقلية أثقلت
(Treat us badly or treat us well — you are not blamed by us, nor hated ...)
[Translator's note: The well-known wording of this verse of Kuthayyir ends «إن تقلّت»; the source has «أثقلت».]
It is as though he were saying to her: test your standing with me and the strength of my love for you; treat me with ill and with good, and see whether my state toward you differs whether you do ill or good. Likewise the meaning of the verse: ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them, and see whether they are forgiven in either case — asking forgiveness or leaving it. It is among the most eloquent of speech.

safi-cedvel:20-20.t:
* I'rab:
(الذين) relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of a nominative, mubtadaʾ (subject); (آمنوا) past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and likewise (هاجروا، جاهدوا); (في سبيل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (جاهدوا); (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (بأموال) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (جاهدوا), [Note: The i'rab of its counterpart has already passed in verse (72) of Sūrat al-Anfāl.] and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) conjunction; (أنفسهم) like أموالهم and conjoined to it; (أعظم) khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ الذين; (درجة) tamyīz (specification), accusative (manṣūb); (عند) adverb, accusative, attached to (أعظم); (الله) like the last; (الواو) conjunction; (أولئك) demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of a nominative, mubtadaʾ.. and (الكاف) a particle of address; (هم) a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) [Note: Or a detached pronoun, a second mubtadaʾ whose khabar is (الفائزون), and the nominal clause is the khabar of أولئك.], (الفائزون) khabar of the mubtadaʾ أولئك, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the wāw.
The clause «الذين آمنوا …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «هاجروا» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «جاهدوا …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «أولئك …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.

* Morphology:
(أعظم): elative noun (ism tafḍīl) whose verb is عظم يعظم, of the كرم pattern; its wazn is أفعل … and the one surpassed is omitted, i.e. "greater than others".
(الفائزون): plural of الفائز, active participle from فاز يفوز; its wazn is فاعل. The weak letter — the wāw — has been converted into a hamza because it comes after the alif of فاعل; its original form is فاوز, and this conversion is regular.

safi-cedvel:21-21.t:
* I'rab:
(يبشّر) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (ربّ) fāʿil (agent), nominative, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (برحمة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يبشّر); (من) preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to a naʿt (adjective) of (رحمة); (الواو) conjunction; (رضوان) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to رحمة, genitive (majrūr); (الواو) conjunction; (جنّات) maʿṭūf to رحمة, genitive; (لهم) like منه, attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); (فيها) like منه, attached to what لهم is attached to; (نعيم) postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative; (مقيم) naʿt of نعيم, nominative like it.
The clause «يبشّرهم …» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption [Note: Or in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in (الفائزون).].
The clause «لهم فيها نعيم …» is in the position of a genitive, a naʿt of جنّات.

* Morphology:
(نعيم): a noun meaning ease of living, comfort and a good life; its wazn is فعيل in the sense of فاعل, because it is an adjective used as a noun.

* Rhetoric:
Folding and unfolding (al-laff wa-l-nashr): in the saying of Allah the Exalted (يُبَشِّرُهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ بِرَحْمَةٍ مِنْهُ وَرِضْوانٍ وَجَنَّاتٍ لَهُمْ فِيها نَعِيمٌ مُقِيمٌ) ..
Since He described the believers with three attributes — faith, emigration, and striving with self and wealth — He matched them for that with glad tidings of three things: mercy, good pleasure (riḍwān) and the Garden. He, Glorified is He, began with mercy, set against faith, because it depends on it and because it is the most general of blessings and the first of them, just as faith is the first; the Exalted put second the good pleasure, which is the utmost of beneficence, set against striving, in which self and wealth are sacrificed; and He, Mighty and Majestic is He, put third the Gardens, set against emigration and leaving homelands, as an indication that, since they preferred to leave them, He gave them the Gardens in exchange for the abode of unbelief. This is a charming device, which they defined as: mentioning several things, in detail or in summary, then mentioning what belongs to each one of them without specifying it, trusting that the hearer will distinguish what belongs to each and refer it back to what it belongs to.

safi-cedvel:22-22.t:
* I'rab:
(خالدين) ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb), anticipated (muqaddara), of the accusative pronoun in (يبشّرهم) [Note: In the previous verse. The anticipated ḥāl is also called the future ḥāl.], the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ; (في) preposition and (ها) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (خالدين); (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb — an abrogator (nāsikh); (الله) the Name of Majesty, the noun of إنّ, accusative; (عند) adverb, accusative, attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate), and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (أجر) postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ); (عظيم) naʿt (adjective) of أجر, nominative like it.
The clause «إنّ الله عنده أجر …» has no grammatical position [Translator's note: so in the source; its type (presumably resumptive or causal) is not stated].
The clause «عنده أجر …» is in the position of a nominative (إنّ) [Translator's note: so in the source; i.e. the khabar of إنّ].

safi-cedvel:23-23.t:
* I'rab:
(يا) vocative particle; (أيّ) the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma, in the position of an accusative, and (ها) a particle of alerting; (الذين) relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of an accusative, a badal (substitute) of أيّ — or a naʿt (adjective) of it; (أمنوا) [Translator's note: so in the source, for آمنوا] past verb and its fāʿil (agent); (لا) prohibitive, jussive-governing; (تتّخذوا) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn … and the wāw is the fāʿil; (آباء) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الواو) conjunction; (إخوانكم) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to آباء … with its muḍāf ilayhi; (أولياء) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (إن) a jussive conditional particle; (استحبّوا) past verb, indeclinable on ḍamma, in the position of a jussive, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) … and the wāw is the fāʿil; (الكفر) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (على الإيمان) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (استحبّوا), the verb being made to include the meaning of اختاروا ("they chose"). (الواو) conjunction; (من) jussive conditional noun, indeclinable, in the position of a nominative, mubtadaʾ (subject); (يتولّ) imperfect verb, jussive, the protasis, the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the weak letter; (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو"; (من) preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of يتولّهم; (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (أولئك) demonstrative, mubtadaʾ, in the position of a nominative … and (الكاف) a particle of address; (هم) a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) [Note: Or a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ, with (الظالمون) as khabar (predicate), and the nominal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ أولئك.], (الظالمون) khabar of the mubtadaʾ أولئك..
The clause «يأيّها الذين …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «لا تتّخذوا …» has no grammatical position, the response to the vocative (jawāb al-nidāʾ).
The clause «استحبّوا …» is in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl of the fathers and brothers [Note: The condition here is formal only (lafẓī), since the implied sense is: "do not take them as allies while they prefer unbelief over faith, in every case" … It is also possible to make the clause the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هم", and the nominal clause is a ḥāl.] … and the apodosis of the condition is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e.: "if your fathers and brothers prefer unbelief, then do not take them as allies".
The clause «من يتولّهم …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause that is the response to the vocative.
The clause «يتولّهم …» is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: The khabar may be the two clauses of the condition and the apodosis together.].
The clause «أولئك … الظالمون» is in the position of a jussive, the apodosis of the condition, joined with the fāʾ.

safi-cedvel:24-24.t:
* I'rab:
(قل) imperative verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is "أنت"; (إن) a jussive conditional particle; (كان) incomplete past verb, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of a jussive, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (آباء) the noun of كان, nominative (marfūʿ); (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (أبناؤكم … عشيرتكم) nouns to which the second-person plural pronoun is annexed, conjoined by conjunctions to آباء, nominative like it; (أموال، تجارة، مساكن) nouns conjoined to آباء by conjunctions, nominative; (اقترفتم) past verb, indeclinable on sukūn … and (تم) a pronoun, fāʿil, and (الواو) is an extra letter, being the lengthening (ishbāʿ) of the vowel of the mīm, and (ها) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (تخشون) imperfect verb, nominative … and the wāw is the fāʿil; (كساد) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb), and (ها) muḍāf ilayhi; (ترضون) like تخشون, and (ها) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (أحبّ) khabar (predicate) of كان, accusative; (إلى) preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أحب); (من الله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أحبّ); (الواو) conjunction; (رسول) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the Name of Majesty, genitive (majrūr), and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) conjunction; (جهاد) maʿṭūf to the Name of Majesty, genitive; (في سبيل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (جهاد), and (الهاء) like the last; (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (تربّصوا) imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn..
and the wāw is the fāʿil [Note: The object is omitted, i.e. "تربّصوا عذاب الله", meaning "await His punishment".], (حتّى) particle of end-limit and preposition; (يأتي) imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after حتّى; (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative; (بأمر) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يأتي), and (الهاء) like the last.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يأتي الله) is in the position of a genitive by (حتّى), attached to (تربّصوا).
(الواو) resumptive; (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative; (لا) negative; (يهدي) imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ, and the fāʿil is "هو"; (القوم) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الفاسقين) naʿt (adjective) of القوم, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ.
The clause «قل …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «إن كان آباؤكم …» is in the position of an accusative, the speech (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «اقترفتموها» is in the position of a nominative, a naʿt of أموال.
The clause «تخشون …» is in the position of a nominative, a naʿt of تجارة.
The clause «ترضونها» is in the position of a nominative, a naʿt of مساكن.
The clause «تربّصوا» is in the position of a jussive (majzūm), the apodosis of the condition, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «يأتي الله …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle-relative (أن).
The clause «الله لا يهدي …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «لا يهدي …» is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الله).

* Morphology:
(عشيرتكم): a noun meaning the nearest kin; it was also said: it is the group gathered by lineage, pact or affection. It is taken from العشرة with fatḥa on the ʿayn ("ten"), for the clan goes back to a bond (ʿaqd) like the ʿaqd of ten [Translator's note: ʿaqd means both "bond" and a decade in finger-counting], so there is a kind of correspondence between the two derivations. العشيرة is pluralised as عشائر and عشيرات.
(كساد): an aural (samāʿī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the verb كسد يكسد, of the نصر pattern and the كرم pattern; its wazn is فعال with fatḥa on the fāʾ. There is another maṣdar, كسود with ḍamma on the kāf.
(مساكن): plural of مسكن, a noun of place from سكن; its wazn is مفعل with fatḥa on the mīm and the ʿayn, because the ʿayn of the imperfect has ḍamma.
(جهاد): an aural maṣdar of the quadriliteral verb جاهد — its regular (qiyāsī) maṣdar is مجاهدة; its wazn is فعال with kasra on the fāʾ.

safi-cedvel:81-81.t:
* I'rab:
(فرح) past verb; (المخلّفون) fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ), its sign of nominative being the waw; (بمقعد) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (فرح), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (خلاف) adverb of time or place, accusative (manṣūb), attached to the mīm-maṣdar مقعد; (رسول) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (الله) the Divine Name, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (الواو) conjunction; (كرهوا) past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma, and the waw is the fāʿil; (أن) a maṣdar-forming particle; (يجاهدوا) imperfect verb, accusative, its sign of accusative being the dropping of the nūn.. and the waw is the fāʿil; (بأموال) a preposition and its genitive noun, [attached] to (يجاهدوا), and (هم) like the last one; (الواو) conjunction; (أنفسهم) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to أموال, genitive, with a muḍāf ilayhi; (في سبيل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يجاهدوا); (الله) the Divine Name, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (الواو) conjunction; (قالوا) like كرهوا; (لا) prohibitive, making the verb jussive; (تنفروا) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), its sign of jussive being the dropping of the nūn ... and the waw is the fāʿil; (في الحرّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تنفروا) [Note: Or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of تنفروا, i.e. "being in the heat".]. (قل) imperative verb, and the fāʿil is "anta"; (نار) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative; (جهنّم) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, its sign of genitive being the fatḥa; (أشدّ) khabar (predicate), nominative; (حرّا) tamyīz (specification), accusative; (لو) a non-jussive conditional particle; (كانوا) defective past verb..
and the waw is the subject (ism) of kāna; (يفقهون) imperfect verb, nominative.. and the waw is the fāʿil.
The clause «فرح المخلّفون» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «كرهوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن يجاهدوا) is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object), its governing word being كرهوا.
The clause «يجاهدوا» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «لا تنفروا ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «نار جهنّم أشد ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of speech.
The clause «كانوا يفقهون» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يفقهون» is in the position of accusative as the khabar of كانوا ... and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, its implied form being "they would not have stayed behind".

* Morphology:
(المخلّفون): plural of المخلّف, passive participle of the four-letter verb خلّف; its wazn is مفعّل — its wazn is مفعّل with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the ʿayn.
(مقعد): a mīm-maṣdar from قعد; its wazn is مفعل with fatḥa on the mīm and the ʿayn.
(خلاف): either the maṣdar of the four-letter verb خالف, so it is a maṣdar transmitted by hearing (samāʿī) meaning "opposition" (al-mukhālafa), its wazn being فعال with kasra on the fāʾ; or a noun indicating adverbial sense; or a quasi-maṣdar (ism maṣdar) of the five-letter verb تخلّف.
(الحرّ): a noun transferred from the maṣdar of the verb حرّ يحرّ, of the pattern of naṣara, of ḍaraba and of fataḥa, the opposite of cold; its wazn is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.

safi-cedvel:82-82.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) linking the answer of an implied condition [Note: Or a conjunction linking the effect to the cause.]; (اللام) the lām of command; (يضحكوا) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), its sign of jussive being the dropping of the nūn.. and the waw is the fāʿil (agent); (قليلا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar [Note: Or an adverb of time standing in for the wording of the original adverb, i.e. "a little time".]; (الواو) conjunction; (ليبكوا كثيرا) like ليضحكوا قليلا; (جزاء) mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), accusative (manṣūb), its governing word being the laughing and weeping [Note: Or a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb, i.e. "they are recompensed a recompense".]; (الباء) a causal preposition; (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle; (كانوا يكسبون) like كانوا يفقهون [Note: in the previous verse (81).].
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (ما كانوا ...) is in the position of genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (جزاء).
