The clause «يضحكوا....» is in the position of jussive as the answer to an implied condition, i.e. "if they rejoiced and وكروا and said ..., then let them laugh ..." [Note: Or it is conjoined to the clause فرح and what is conjoined to it in the previous verse ... and the clause قل ... is parenthetical. Abū Ḥayyān said: The command to laugh and weep has the meaning of a statement, and the meaning is: they will laugh little and weep much ...].
[Translator's note: «وكروا» in the source is evidently a typographical error for «وكرهوا» (and they disliked).]

* Rhetoric:
1- Ṭibāq (antithesis): between laughing and weeping, and between little and much, so it is a muqābala (parallel antithesis) ...
2- Putting a statement in the form of a command: to indicate that what is reported will inevitably occur; that is because the form of command is originally and mostly for obligation, so it was used for what its meaning entails. That is in His saying, Exalted is He, فَلْيَضْحَكُوا قَلِيلًا وَلْيَبْكُوا كَثِيراً.
3- Kināya (metonymy): in His saying, Exalted is He, فَلْيَضْحَكُوا قَلِيلًا وَلْيَبْكُوا كَثِيراً; laughing is a metonymy for joy and weeping a metonymy for grief, and "little" may be an expression for non-existence and "much" an expression for permanence.

* Benefits:
Ambiguous accusatives:
Sometimes an accusative noun occurs in a sentence that admits more than one analysis, and this sometimes leads to confusion and uncertainty, or to disagreement. Since this matter is of great importance, we wished to uncover it. In this verse comes His saying, Exalted is He, فَلْيَضْحَكُوا قَلِيلًا: قليلا may be parsed as a stand-in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq, the implied sense being "let them laugh a little laughing", just as it may be parsed as an adverb of time, implying "a little time". Ibn Hishām devoted a section to this subject in al-Mughnī, saying:
1- What admits being a stand-in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq or a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), such as: ولا يظلمون نقيرا، ثم لم ينقصوكم شيئا.
2- What admits being a stand-in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq, or an adverb, or a ḥāl (circumstantial), such as سرت طويلا: i.e. a long journey, or a long time, or "I travelled it [while it was] long". Similar is His saying, Exalted is He, وَأُزْلِفَتِ الْجَنَّةُ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ غَيْرَ بَعِيدٍ, for غير admits the three analyses we mentioned.
3- What admits being a stand-in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq or a ḥāl: such as جاء زيد ركضا, the implied form being "running a run" or "running". Similar is His saying, Exalted is He: ائْتِيا طَوْعاً أَوْ كَرْهاً، قالَتا أَتَيْنا طائِعِينَ; the ḥāl came in His saying أَتَيْنا طائِعِينَ in the place of the maṣdar mentioned before, and طوعا may be a stand-in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq or a ḥāl according to the preceding interpretation ...
4- What admits being a stand-in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq, a ḥāl, or a mafʿūl li-ajlihi: among that is His saying, Exalted is He, يُرِيكُمُ الْبَرْقَ خَوْفاً وَطَمَعاً, the implied form being "so you fear a fearing", or "fearing", or "for the sake of fear". And we say جاء زيد رغبة, the implied form being: "desiring a desire", or "a coming of desire", or "desiring", or "out of desire".
5- What admits being a mafʿūl bihi or a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment): such as أكرمتك وزيدا; (وزيدا) may be considered conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the mafʿūl bihi, which is the kāf, or it may be a mafʿūl maʿahu, i.e. "I honoured you together with Zayd"; and we can consider (زيدا) a mafʿūl bihi of an implied verb, the implied form being "I honoured you and I honoured Zayd".

safi-cedvel:83-83.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive; (إن) a conditional particle that makes the verb jussive; (رجع) past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and (الكاف) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (الله) the Divine Name, fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ); (إلى طائفة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (رجع); (من) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to a naʿt (adjective) of طائفة; (الفاء) conjunction; (استأذنوا) past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma, in the position of jussive, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to رجع.. and the waw is the fāʿil, and (الكاف) like the first; (للخروج) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (استأذنوك); (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (قل) imperative verb, and the fāʿil is "anta"; (لن) a particle of negation and accusative; (تخرجوا) imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), its sign of accusative being the dropping of the nūn.. and the waw is the fāʿil; (مع) adverb, accusative, attached to (لن تخرجوا), its sign of accusative being the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the letter before the yāʾ, and (الياء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (أبدا) adverb of time, accusative, attached to (تخرجوا); (الواو) conjunction; (لن تقاتلوا معي) like لن تخرجوا معي; (عدوّا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb, and (كم) a pronoun in the position of accusative as the subject (ism) of inna; (رضيتم) past verb, indeclinable on sukūn, and (تم) the fāʿil; (بالقعود) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (رضيتم); (أوّل) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, its governing word being القعود, accusative; (مرّة) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (الفاء) linking the answer of an implied condition; (اقعدوا) imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn ... and the waw is the fāʿil; (مع) like the first, attached to (اقعدوا) [Note: Or attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of اقعدوا.]; (الخالفين) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, its sign of genitive being the yāʾ.
The clause «رجعك الله ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «استأذنوك» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «قل ...» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «لن تخرجوا ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «لن تقاتلوا ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the object-of-speech clause.
The clause «إنّكم رضيتم ...» has no grammatical position, causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «رضيتم ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of inna.
The clause «اقعدوا ...» is in the position of jussive as the answer to an implied condition ... i.e. "if you were content with staying behind the first time, then stay with those who stay behind every time".

* Morphology:
(الخالفين): plural of المخالف, active participle of the three-letter verb خلف; its wazn is فاعل.
[Translator's note: The source writes «المخالف» as the singular; the singular of الخالفين is الخالف.]

safi-cedvel:116-116.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّ الله) like «إنّ إبراهيم» [Note: In verse (114) of this surah.], (اللام) a preposition, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive — attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); (ملك) a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ); (السموات) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (الأرض) conjoined to السموات by the conjunction, genitive; (يحيي) an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "he"; (الواو) a conjunction; (يميت) an imperfect verb, nominative; (الواو) a conjunction; (ما) negative; (لكم) like له; (من دون) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of وليّ — an adjective placed before the noun it qualifies [Note: It may be attached to the khabar to which (لكم) is attached.] — ; (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (من) a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; (وليّ) genitive in wording, nominative in position, a postponed mubtadaʾ; (الواو) a conjunction; (لا) redundant, to emphasise the negation; (نصير) conjoined to وليّ, following it in the genitive in wording.
The clause «إنّ الله …» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «له ملك السموات …» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of inna.
The clause «يحيي …» is in the position of nominative as a second khabar [Note: Or in the position of nominative as a badal (substitute) of the clause «له ملك السموات», a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl).].
The clause «يميت» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause يحيي.
The clause «لكم.. وليّ» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.

* Benefits:
Types of the khabar: the khabar, whether of a mubtadaʾ, of inna or of kāna with their sisters, takes various forms, coming as:
1- A single word (i.e. neither a clause nor a quasi-clause), such as: إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ.
2- A verbal clause, such as His saying, the Exalted, إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُدافِعُ عَنِ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا: the clause يدافع is in the position of nominative as the khabar of inna.
3- A nominal clause, as occurs in the verse, as in our saying: العلم فوائده عظيمة ("knowledge — its benefits are great"). العلم is a first mubtadaʾ; فوائده is a second mubtadaʾ; عظيمة is the khabar of the second mubtadaʾ; and the clause فوائده عظيمة is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the first mubtadaʾ. Note the presence of a pronoun in the second mubtadaʾ referring back to the first mubtadaʾ; this is a condition when the khabar is a verbal or nominal clause. In the verbal clause the pronoun is latent, as has passed, or attached, as in His saying, the Exalted, إِنَّ الْمُنافِقِينَ يُخادِعُونَ اللَّهَ:
the wāw of the plural in the verbal clause يخادعون is an attached pronoun referring to the noun (المنافقين); and in the nominal clause the pronoun is attached, as has passed.
4- A quasi-clause (i.e. an adverb, or a preposition and its genitive noun). An example of the adverb: موعدنا يوم السبت ("our appointment is on Saturday"); an example of the preposition and its genitive noun: الخير بي وبأمتي ("good is in me and in my community"). This means that we attach the adverb or the preposition phrase to an omitted khabar, its implied form being كائن ("existing"), and say: يوم is a mafʿūl fīhi (adverbial), an adverb of time, attached to an omitted khabar, its implied form being كائن; the implied construction is (موعدنا كائن يوم السبت).
[Translator's note: The source labels the clause «إنّ الله …» with «لا محلّ له» (masculine) instead of the usual «لا محلّ لها»; the meaning is unaffected.]

safi-cedvel:117-117.t:
* I'rab:
(اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied oath; (قد) a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); (تاب) a past verb; (اللَّه) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ); (على النبيّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تاب); (الواو) a conjunction in both places; (المهاجرين، الأنصار) two nouns conjoined to النبيّ, genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive of the first being the yāʾ; (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of المهاجرين and الأنصار; (اتّبعوا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (في ساعة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (اتّبعوه); (العسرة) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (من بعد) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تاب); (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle; (كاد) an incomplete past verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) — [Note: After a long discussion of كاد and its khabar, Abū Ḥayyān made the verb redundant — as كان is sometimes made redundant — saying: "One escapes these difficulties by holding that كاد is redundant, its meaning intended, having no governing effect then on a noun or a khabar; so it is like كان when it is made redundant: its meaning is intended and it has no governing effect." End quote.], and its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), omitted [Note: The noun may be a pronoun whose implied form is "they (هم)", referring to the people understood from His saying فريق منهم, or a pronoun referring to the hearts.], (يزيغ) an imperfect verb, nominative; (قلوب) fāʿil, nominative [Note: The verb may be masculine singular because the fāʿil is a broken plural.], (فريق) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (من) a preposition, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive — attached to a naʿt of فريق; (ثمّ) a conjunction; (تاب) like the first; (عليهم) like منهم, attached to (تاب); (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb, for emphasis, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of inna; (بهم) like منهم, attached to (رؤف), which is the khabar (predicate) of inna, nominative; (رحيم) a second khabar, nominative.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما كاد….) is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «تاب اللَّه …» has no grammatical position, being the answer to an implied oath.
The clause «اتّبعوه …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «كاد يزيغ …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle relative (ما).
The clause «يزيغ قلوب …» is in the position of accusative as the khabar of كاد.
The clause «تاب عليهم» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause of the answer to the oath, and it emphasises it.
The clause «إنّه بهم رؤف» has no grammatical position, being explanatory of cause (taʿlīliyya).

safi-cedvel:118-118.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) a conjunction; (على الثلاثة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تاب) [Note: In the previous verse (117); this preposition phrase is conjoined to (عليهم), i.e. "He turned to them and to the three".], (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of الثلاثة; (خلّفوا) a past verb, passive, indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (حتّى) a particle of commencement (ḥarf ibtidāʾ); (إذا) an adverb of future time, indeclinable, in the position of accusative, attached to the content of the apodosis; (ضاقت) a past verb, and (التاء) for the feminine; (على) a preposition, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive — attached to (ضاقت); (الأرض) fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ); (الباء) a preposition; (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle; (رحبت) like ضاقت, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "it (هي)"; (الواو) a conjunction; (ضاقت عليهم أنفسهم) like «ضاقت عليهم الأرض», and (هم) is attached, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) a conjunction; (ظنّوا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (أن) lightened from the heavy (anna), and its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), omitted; (لا) the lā of generic negation; (ملجأ) the noun of lā, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of accusative; (من الله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ملجأ with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "from the punishment of Allah" or "from the displeasure of Allah"; (إلّا) a particle of exception [Note: Or a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr), and the preposition phrase (إليه) is attached to the khabar of lā.], (إلى) a preposition, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, a badal (substitute) of an implied thing excepted from [Note: I.e. "there is no refuge from the punishment of Allah for anyone except in Him".], (ثمّ) a conjunction; (تاب) a past verb; (عليهم) like the first, attached to (تاب); (اللام) for explaining cause (taʿlīl); (يتوبوا) an imperfect verb, subjunctive (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām, the sign of the subjunctive being the deletion of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb, for emphasis; (اللَّه) the Name of Majesty, the noun of inna; (هو) a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) [Note: Or it is a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar is (التوّاب), and the nominal clause (هو التوّاب..) is in the position of nominative as the khabar of inna.], (التوّاب) the khabar (predicate) of inna, nominative; (الرحيم) a second khabar, nominative.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما رحبت..) is in the position of genitive by the bāʾ, and the preposition phrase is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of الأرض, i.e. "it became narrow while being spacious", i.e. despite its spaciousness.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن لا ملجأ..) is in the position of accusative, standing in place of the two objects of ظنّوا.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يتوبوا..) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to (تاب).
The clause «خلّفوا …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «the condition, its protasis and its implied apodosis..» has no grammatical position, being resumptive [Note: The apodosis of إذا is implied, and His saying تابَ عَلَيْهِمْ is conjoined to it, i.e. "when it became narrow for them… they took refuge in Him", or "they repented, then Allah turned to them". إذا may also be stripped of condition, so that it needs no apodosis, the meaning being: "He turned to those who were left behind, up to this time".].
The clause «ضاقت.. الأرض» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «رحبت» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle relative (ما).
The clause «ضاقت.. أنفسهم» is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the first clause ضاقت.
The clause «ظنّوا..» is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the first clause ضاقت.
The clause «لا ملجأ …» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the lightened أن.
The clause «تاب عليهم» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the implied apodosis, i.e. "they took refuge in Him, then Allah turned to them".
The clause «يتوبوا» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the implied particle relative (أن).
The clause «إنّ اللَّه هو التوّاب» has no grammatical position, being explanatory of cause (taʿlīliyya).

* Rhetoric:
Majāz (figurative usage): in His saying, the Exalted, «وَضاقَتْ عَلَيْهِمْ أَنْفُسُهُمْ», i.e. their hearts; they were expressed thus figuratively because the self subsists through them. The meaning of their narrowness is their grief and sorrow, as if they could not contain joy because of their narrowness.

* Benefits:
The ḥadīth of the three who were left behind
This ḥadīth was narrated by ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kaʿb from his father, who stayed behind from the expedition of Tabūk.
We will present it in abridged form because of its length: Kaʿb ibn Mālik stayed behind from the expedition of Tabūk, though he was in health and had wealth and had no excuse; this expedition was in intense heat. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned from Tabūk, the hypocrites came swearing and making excuses, and he accepted it from them and left their inner states to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. As for Kaʿb, he told the Messenger of Allah ﷺ the truth and said: "I stayed behind and I have no excuse; I was well off."
The Prophet ﷺ said to him: "Get up, until Allah decides concerning your matter." Kaʿb asked: "Has anyone met with what I have met with?" He was told: "Yes, two men: Hilāl ibn Umayya and Murāra ibn al-Rabīʿ." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade speaking to these three who were left behind, so the Muslims boycotted them. Kaʿb says: "I climbed over the wall of my cousin Abū Qatāda, who was the dearest of people to me, and I greeted them, but he did not return the greeting. I said to him: 'Do you know that I love Allah and His Messenger?' He said: 'Allah knows best.' So I left him sad. On the fortieth day of the boycott, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent word to us that we should keep away from our wives and not approach them, so I sent my wife to her family. The earth became narrow for me, and my own self became narrow for me. Then, in the meantime, the king of Ghassān sent me a letter inviting me to come to him, saying: 'We have heard that your companion has treated you harshly.' I said: 'By Allah, this too is part of the trial,' and I burned the letter. At the completion of the fiftieth night, I was praying the dawn prayer on the roof of my house, when I heard a voice calling out to me the news of Allah's acceptance of my repentance. The bearers of good news came, and I rejoiced greatly, and I went to the Prophet ﷺ at the mosque, and he congratulated me on the repentance. When I entered the mosque, Ṭalḥa ibn ʿUbayd Allāh rose to me, received me and congratulated me; no one else rose to me" — and Kaʿb never forgot that for Ṭalḥa. "Then I gave all my wealth in charity, in recompense for the repentance, but the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered me to keep something, so I kept my share in Khaybar. Allah saved me through truthfulness and turned to me in repentance; no one has been tried in truthful speech as I was tried. We were called 'those left behind' (al-mukhallafūn) not because of our staying behind from the expedition, but because Allah left our matter behind and deferred it."
[Translator's note: The source has «فسلمت عليهم» ("I greeted them") followed by «فلم يرد» ("he did not return"); the shift from plural to singular is as in the source.]

safi-cedvel:119-119.t:
* I'rab:
(يا) a vocative particle; (أيّ) the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite noun (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma in the position of accusative, and (ها) a particle of alerting (tanbīh); (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative [Translator's note: The source has «في محل نصب»; this book and others normally put the follower of أيّ in the position of nominative (raf').], a badal (substitute) of أيّ or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition); (آمنوا) like ظنوا [Note: In the previous verse (118).], (اتّقوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable on the deletion of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (الله) the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (الواو) a conjunction; (كونوا) an incomplete imperative verb, and the wāw is the noun of كن; (مع) an adverb, accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of كونوا; (الصادقين) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
The vocative clause «يأيّها الذين» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «اتّقوا …» has no grammatical position, being the answer to the vocative.
The clause «كونوا …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the answer to the vocative.

safi-cedvel:52-52.t:
* I'rab:
(قل) like the previous one [Note: In the previous verse (51).], (هل) an interrogative particle carrying the sense of negation. (تربّصون) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), from which one of the two tāʾs has been dropped ... and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). (الباء) a preposition and (نا) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تربّصون) [Note: Or attached to an omitted verb, the implied form being: do you await that there befall us anything but one of the two best things.], (إلا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). (إحدى) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the alif. (الحسنيين) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ. (الواو) conjunction. (نحن) a detached pronoun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). (نتربّص) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "we". (بكم) like بنا, attached to (نتربّص). (أن) an infinitival particle causing the accusative. (يصيب) an imperfect verb, accusative, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative. (بعذاب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يصيب). (من عند) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a naʿt (adjective) of (عذاب), and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi. (أو) a conjunction of choice. (بأيدي) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a naʿt of (عذاب), conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the prepositional phrase before it, and (نا) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يصيبكم) is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi, its governor being نتربّص.
(الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition. (تربّصوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil. (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) — and (نا) a pronoun in the position of accusative, the noun of inna. (مع) an adverb, accusative, attached to (متربّصون), and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (متربّصون) the khabar (predicate) of inna, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw.
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «هل تربّصون بنا ...» is in the position of accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «نحن نتربّص ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause of the speech reported.
The clause «نتربّص ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (نحن).
The clause «يصيبكم الله ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «تربّصوا ...» is in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e. if each will meet what he awaits, then await ...
The clause «إنّا.. متربّصون» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).

* Morphology:
(الحسنيين): dual of الحسنى, the feminine of الأحسن.. See verse (95) of Sūrat al-Nisāʾ.
(متربّصون): plural of متربّص, the active participle of the five-letter verb تربّص; its pattern is متفعّل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.

* Rhetoric:
The art of taʿaṭṭuf (return of a word), or mushāraka: it is that the speaker announces a word of the speech with one meaning, then brings back that very word and attaches it to another meaning, the two being separated, each word at one end of the speech. It is in His saying, the Exalted: قُلْ هَلْ تَرَبَّصُونَ بِنا إِلَّا إِحْدَى الْحُسْنَيَيْنِ وَنَحْنُ نَتَرَبَّصُ بِكُمْ أَنْ يُصِيبَكُمُ اللَّهُ بِعَذابٍ مِنْ عِنْدِهِ أَوْ بِأَيْدِينا فَتَرَبَّصُوا إِنَّا مَعَكُمْ مُتَرَبِّصُونَ. The taʿaṭṭuf came from the opening of the verse, in His saying تَرَبَّصُونَ بِنا, and from its end, in His saying فَتَرَبَّصُوا إِنَّا مَعَكُمْ مُتَرَبِّصُونَ, together with the paronomasia of pairing (tajnīs al-izdiwāj).
Along with the taʿaṭṭuf there occurs a correspondence (muqābala) of meaning, in which the speech takes the form of concision by ellipsis (ījāz al-ḥadhf). For what eloquence requires is that the implied order of the wording be: say: do you await for us anything but one of the two best things: that Allah should afflict us with a punishment from Him or at your hands; and we await for you that Allah should afflict you with a punishment from Him or at our hands. So He omitted, seeking concision, the explanation of the two best things from the first clause, and affirmed it in the second clause, to avoid repeating and multiplying the wording; just as He omitted "the two best things" from the second clause, dispensing with it by its mention first. Thus there came together in the verse taʿaṭṭuf, muqābala and ījāz, and four kinds of rhetorical embellishment (badīʿ) were completed in it. This is lawful magic, and "indeed some eloquence is magic".

safi-cedvel:53-53.t:
* I'rab:
(قل) like the previous one [Note: In verse (51) of this surah.], (أنفقوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). (طوعا) a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb). (الواو) conjunction. (كرها) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to (طوعا), accusative [Note: See verse (83) of Sūrat Āl ʿImrān.], (لن) a particle of negation and the accusative. (يتقبّل) an imperfect verb, passive, accusative, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is omitted, indicated by His saying (أنفقوا), i.e. what you have spent will never be accepted from you. (من) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يتقبّل). (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb, and (كم) a pronoun in the position of accusative, the noun of inna. (كنتم) a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) — and (تم) a pronoun, the noun of kāna. (قوما) the khabar (predicate) of kāna, accusative. (فاسقين) a naʿt (adjective) of (قوما), accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ.
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «أنفقوا ...» is in the position of accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «لن يتقبّل منكم» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «إنّكم كنتم قوما ...» has no grammatical position: causal.
The clause «كنتم قوما ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of innakum.

safi-cedvel:54-54.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction. (ما) negative. (منع) a past verb, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (أن) an infinitival particle causing the accusative. (تقبل) an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), passive. (منهم) like منكم [Note: In the previous verse (53).], attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تقبل). (نفقات) nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative (marfūʿ), and (هم) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تقبل) is in the position of genitive by an omitted preposition, i.e. from that … be accepted [Note: Or in the position of accusative as a second mafʿūl bihi, its governor being منع.], attached to (منع).
(إلّا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). (أنّ) a particle resembling the verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) — and (هم) a pronoun in the position of accusative, the noun of anna. (كفروا) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma ... and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). (بالله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (كفروا). (الواو) conjunction. (برسول) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (كفروا), and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (الواو) conjunction. (لا) negative. (يأتون) an imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is the fāʿil. (الصلاة) mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (إلّا) a particle of restriction. (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya). (هم) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). (كسالى) khabar (predicate), nominative, the sign of the nominative being the implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the alif. (الواو) conjunction. (لا ينفقون إلّا وهم كارهون) like لا يأتون ... هم كسالى.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّهم كفروا..) is in the position of nominative as the fāʿil of منع [Note: The fāʿil may be Allah, and (أنّهم كفروا) a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. because they disbelieved.].
The clause «ما منعهم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause قل in the previous verse.
The clause «تقبل ... نفقاتهم» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «كفروا ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of anna.
The clause «لا يأتون» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause كفروا.
The clause «هم كسالى» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of يأتون.
The clause «لا ينفقون ...» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause لا يأتون.
The clause «هم كارهون ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the fāʿil of ينفقون.

safi-cedvel:55-55.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive [Note: Or linking the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. if you look at them, then let not their wealth impress you.] (لا) the prohibitive lā, causing the jussive. (تعجب) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), and (الكاف) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (أموال) fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (الواو) conjunction. (لا) redundant (zāʾida), to emphasise the negation. (أولادهم) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to أموالهم, nominative like it. (إنّما) the restricting particle and the restricted (kāffa wa-makfūfa). (يريد) an imperfect verb, nominative. (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative. (اللام) redundant [Note: It came after a transitive verb, i.e. Allah wants to punish them with it ...] (يعذب) an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muḍmara) أن after the lām, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is "He". (الباء) a preposition and (ها) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يعذّب), i.e. because of it. (في الحياة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يعذّب). (الدنيا) a naʿt (adjective) of الحياة, genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the implied (muqaddar) kasra on the alif. (الواو) conjunction. (تزهق) an imperfect verb, accusative, conjoined to (يعذّب). (أنفسهم) fāʿil, nominative, and muḍāf ilayhi.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يعذّبهم) is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi, its governor being يريد — this is the remote position — and of genitive, which is the near position.
(الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya). (هم) a detached [pronoun], mubtadaʾ (subject). (كافرون) khabar (predicate), nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw.
The clause «لا تعجبك أموالهم» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يريد الله ...» has no grammatical position: causal.
The clause «يعذّبهم ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle relative (أن).
The clause «تزهق أنفسهم» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يعذّبهم.
The clause «هم كافرون» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

safi-cedvel:56-56.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive. (يحلفون) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ).. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). (بالله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يحلفون). (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) — and (هم) a pronoun in the position of accusative, the noun of inna. (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and it emphasises the oath. (من) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) of inna. (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya). (ما) negative. (هم) a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ (subject) [Note: Or in the position of nominative as the noun of (ما) operating like laysa, with منكم the khabar.] (منكم) like the first, attached to the omitted khabar of هم. (الواو) conjunction. (لكنّ) a particle resembling the verb, for rectification (istidrāk) — an abrogator — and (هم) a pronoun in the position of accusative, the noun of lākinna. (قوم) the khabar of lākinna, nominative. (يفرقون) like يحلفون.
The clause «يحلفون ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «إنّهم لمنكم» has no grammatical position: the response to the oath; and the oath clause with its response is the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl) of an implied verb of saying which is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of يحلفون.
The clause «ما هم منكم» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.
The clause «لكنّهم قوم ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the ḥāl clause [Note: Or resumptive, with no grammatical position.].
The clause «يفرقون» is in the position of nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of قوم.

safi-cedvel:57-57.t:
* I'rab:
(لو) a conditional particle not causing the jussive. (يجدون) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ),
and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). (ملجأ) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb). (أو) a conjunction. (مغارات) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ملجأ, accusative like it, the sign of the accusative being the kasra; and likewise (مدّخلا). (اللام) occurring in the apodosis of law. (ولّوا) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma.. and the wāw is the fāʿil. (إلى) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (ولّوا). (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya). (هم) a pronoun, mubtadaʾ (subject). (يجمحون) like يجدون.
The clause «يجدون ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «ولّوا ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).
The clause «هم يجمحون» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of ولّوا.
The clause «يجمحون» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ هم.

* Morphology:
(ملجأ): a noun of place from the triliteral verb لجأ; its pattern is مفعل with fatḥa on the mīm and the ʿayn, for it is a sound verb whose imperfect has fatḥa on the ʿayn [Note: (ملجأ) and what follows it may properly be mīmī maṣdars meaning taking refuge, hiding and entering, i.e. had they been able to do that, they would have turned..].
(مغارات): plural of مغارة, with fatḥa or ḍamma on the mīm, or plural of مغار, with fatḥa or ḍamma on the mīm; a noun of place from the triliteral غار. The alif is converted from a wāw; its origin is مغورة — with fatḥa on the wāw — the wāw was voweled after a fatḥa and was converted into an alif.
(مدّخلا): a noun of place from the five-letter verb ادّخل; it is on the pattern مفتعل with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the ʿayn.

safi-cedvel:84-85.t:
[Note: This second verse is a repetition and confirmation of verse (55) of this sūra.]
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive — or a conjunction; (لا) prohibitive, making the verb jussive; (تصلّ) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), its sign of jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, and the fāʿil (agent) is "anta"; (على أحد) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (لا تصلّ); (من) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of (أحد) [Note: Or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of مات, i.e. he died while being one of them, i.e. a hypocrite.]; (مات) past verb, and the fāʿil is "huwa"; (أبدا) adverb of time, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (لا تصلّ); (الواو) conjunction; (لا تقم على قبره) like لا تصل على أحد, and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (إنّهم كفروا بالله ورسوله) the i'rab of its counterpart has been given [Note: in verse (80) of this sūra.]; (الواو) conjunction; (ماتوا) like كفروا; (الواو) of ḥāl; (هم فاسقون) like هم معرضون [Note: in verse (76) of this sūra.].
The clause «لا تصلّ ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive ... or conjoined to the clause إن رجعك الله ... in the previous verse.
The clause «مات» is in the position of genitive as a naʿt of أحد.
The clause «لا تقم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause لا تصلّ.
The clause «إنّهم كفروا.....» has no grammatical position, causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «كفروا ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of inna.
The clause «ماتوا ...» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause كفروا [Note: Or it has no grammatical position, conjoined to the causal clause.].
The clause «هم فاسقون» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.
(الواو) conjunction; (لا تعجب) like لا تصلّ, and the sign of jussive is the sukūn, and (الكاف) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (أموالهم) fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (أولادهم) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to أموالهم by the waw, nominative; (إنّما) a restraining particle and the restrained one (kāffa wa-makfūfa); (يريد) imperfect verb, nominative; (الله) the Divine Name, fāʿil, nominative; (أن) a maṣdar-forming particle that makes the verb accusative; (يعذّب) imperfect verb, accusative, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is "huwa"; (الباء) a preposition and (ها) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (يعذّب), and the bāʾ is causal; (في الدنيا) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يعذّبهم), its sign of genitive being the kasra implied (muqaddar) on the alif.
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن يعذّبهم) is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi, its governing word being يريد.
(الواو) conjunction; (تزهق) like يعذّب and conjoined to it; (أنفس) fāʿil, nominative, and (هم) muḍāf ilayhi; (وهم كافرون) like وهم فاسقون.
The clause «لا تعجبك أموالهم» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause لا تصلّ ...
The clause «إنّما يريد الله ...» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «يعذّبهم ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «تزهق أنفسهم» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «هم كافرون» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.

* Morphology:
(تصلّ): it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion to suit the jussive; the yāʾ, the lām of the word, was dropped, and its wazn is تفعّ.

* Rhetoric:
Variation and distinction between wordings: in His saying, Exalted is He, وَلا تُعْجِبْكَ أَمْوالُهُمْ وَأَوْلادُهُمْ etc., and in the verse mentioned earlier, namely «فَلا تُعْجِبْكَ أَمْوالُهُمْ وَلا أَوْلادُهُمْ». As for the secret of the repetition and the wisdom in it: renewed revelation carries weight in establishing and confirming what it was revealed for, and in intending that it remain in the mind of the one addressed, so that he neither forgets it nor overlooks it, and that he believe that acting on it is important and requires extra care — especially when the interval between the two revelations is long. So it resembles a thing that concerns its owner, so that he returns to it in the course of his talk and steers back to it. This meaning was repeated only because of its strength regarding what one must beware of.

* Benefits:
Disowning the hypocrites:
Allah the Exalted commanded His Messenger ﷺ to disown the hypocrites, and not to pray over any of them when he dies, nor to stand at his grave to ask forgiveness for him or to supplicate for him, because they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger and died upon that. This is a general ruling for everyone whose hypocrisy is known, even if the occasion of the verse's revelation was ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy, the head of the hypocrites — as al-Bukhārī said — for consideration is given to the generality of the meaning, not the specificity of the occasion.
Concerning the occasion of revelation of this verse it is narrated from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: When ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy died, his son ʿAbd Allāh came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and asked him to give him his shirt عليه, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ rose to pray over him. ʿUmar rose and took hold of يثوب the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, will you pray over him when your Lord has forbidden you to pray over him?!" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah has only given me a choice, saying: اسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ أَوْ لا تَسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ إِنْ تَسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ سَبْعِينَ مَرَّةً فَلَنْ يَغْفِرَ اللَّهُ لَهُمْ, and I will add to the seventy." He said: "He is a hypocrite!" He said: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed over him, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed this verse. After that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ never prayed over a hypocrite nor stood at his grave until Allah, Mighty and Majestic, took him.
[Translator's note: The wording «قميصه عليه» appears to be missing a word (in the well-known narration: "to give him his shirt to shroud him in it"), and «يثوب» is evidently a typographical error for «بثوب» ("took hold of the garment of").]

safi-cedvel:86-86.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (إذا) an adverb of the future containing the sense of a condition, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (استأذنك); (أنزلت) past verb, passive.. and (التاء) for the feminine; (سورة) nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative (marfūʿ); (أن) an explicative particle (ḥarf tafsīr) [Note: Because the verb (أنزلت) contains the meaning of saying without its letters ... It may also be a maṣdar-forming particle, with the interpreted maṣdar genitive by an omitted bāʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun attached to (أنزلت).]; (آمنوا) imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn ... and the waw is the fāʿil (agent); (بالله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (آمنوا); (الواو) conjunction; (جاهدوا) like آمنوا; (مع) adverb, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (جاهدوا), and (رسول) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr), and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi; (استأذن) past verb, and (الكاف) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (أولو) fāʿil, nominative, its sign of nominative being the waw, since it is treated like the masculine plural; (الطول) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (منهم) like the previous one [Note: in verse (84) of this sūra.], attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from (أولو الطول); (الواو) conjunction; (قالوا) past verb with its fāʿil; (ذر) imperative verb, and (نا) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is "anta"; (نكن) defective imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) as the answer to the request (jawāb al-ṭalab); (مع القاعدين) like مع الخالفين [Note: in verse (83) of this sūra.].
The clause «أنزلت سورة ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «آمنوا» has no grammatical position, explicative (tafsīriyya).
The clause «جاهدوا» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the explicative clause.
The clause «استأذنك أولو ...» has no grammatical position, as the answer of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause of the answer of the condition.
The clause «ذرنا ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «نكن.» has no grammatical position, as the answer to an implied condition, not joined with the fāʾ.

* Benefits:
The jussive as the answer to a request.
In this verse comes His saying, Exalted is He, ذَرْنا نَكُنْ مَعَ الْقاعِدِينَ. The verb (نكن) is a defective imperfect verb, which makes the first [noun] nominative and the second accusative, and it is jussive as the answer to a request. This construction occurs among the Arabs: the jussive verb is preceded by a request, and the request consists of an imperative verb, as in our saying ادرس تنجح, or an imperfect verb joined with the lām of command, such as لتزرع الخير تحصد الحمد, or an imperfect verb joined with prohibitive (لا), such as (لا تدن من الأشرار تسلم). The jussive in answer to a request resembles the jussive with the conditional particles that make two verbs jussive, and accordingly we interpret the preceding examples as: إن تدرس تنجح، إن تزرع الخير تحصد الحمد، إن لم تدن من الأشرار تسلم. It is not permissible to say لا تدن من الأشرار تؤذ, because it spoils the meaning and becomes (إن لم تدن من الأشرار تؤذّ). The grammarians also allowed a verbal noun of command (ism fiʿl al-amr) to be a cause of the imperfect's being jussive as the answer to a request, citing as evidence the saying of the poet ʿAmr ibn al-Iṭnāba:
وقولي كلما جشأت وجاشت ... مكانك تحمدي أو تستر يحي
(And my saying [to my soul] whenever it heaved and surged: "Stay in your place — you will be praised or find rest.")
In this verse the poet addresses his own soul, and the meaning of جشأت وجاشت is "it became agitated". The point of evidence in it is his saying (مكانك تحمدي), where the verb تحمدي is made jussive by the request, which is (مكانك), a verbal noun of command meaning "stand firm". And of the request clause we say:
the answer to the request has no grammatical position.

safi-cedvel:87-87.t:
* I'rab:
(رضوا) past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma ... and the waw is the fāʿil (agent); (الباء) a preposition; (أن) a maṣdar-forming particle that makes the verb accusative; (يكونوا) defective imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), its sign of accusative being the dropping of the nūn.. and the waw is the subject (ism) of يكون; (مع الخوالف) like مع الخالفين [Note: in verse (83) of this sūra.]. (الواو) conjunction; (طبع) past verb, passive; (على قلوب) a preposition and its genitive noun in the position of nominative as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الفاء) conjunction linking the effect to the effect [sic]; (هم) a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ (subject); (لا) negative; (يفقهون) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ).. and the waw is the fāʿil.
[Translator's note: The source has «لربط المسبّب بالمسبب» ("linking the effect to the effect"); elsewhere the book says «لربط المسبّب بالسبب» ("linking the effect to the cause").]
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن يكونوا ...) is in the position of genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (رضوا).
The clause «رضوا ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive, containing an explanation of the cause of what preceded.
The clause «يكونوا» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «طبع على قلوبهم» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «هم لا يفقهون» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause طبع على قلوبهم.
The clause «لا يفقهون» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (هم).

* Morphology:
(الخوالف): plural of الخالفة, which is the woman who stays behind; it is the feminine of خالف, active participle of the three-letter verb خلف; its wazn is فاعل.

safi-cedvel:25-25.t:
* I'rab:
(اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied oath; (قد) particle of verification (taḥqīq); (نصر) past verb, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ); (في مواطن) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (نصر), the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa because it is a diptote, being on the pattern of the ultimate plural (ṣīghat muntahā al-jumūʿ); (كثيرة) naʿt (adjective) of مواطن, genitive (majrūr); (الواو) conjunction; (يوم) adverb, accusative (manṣūb), attached to what (في مواطن) is attached to, because it is conjoined to it [Note: Or attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "اذكر", because (إذ أعجبتكم) is a badal (substitute) of يوم حنين; if the governing word were the overt one, the meaning would differ somewhat, because their great number did not please them in [Translator's note: the footnote breaks off here in the source]], (حنين) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive; (إذ) adverb of past time, indeclinable (mabnī), a badal of يوم; (أعجبت) like نصر, and (التاء) for the feminine, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (كثرة) fāʿil, nominative, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الفاء) conjunction; (لم) particle of negation and jussive; (تغن) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هي", i.e. the great number; (عن) preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (تغن); (شيئا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, i.e. "any availing at all"; (الواو) conjunction; (ضاقت) like أعجبت; (عليكم) like عنكم, attached to (ضاقت); (الأرض) fāʿil, nominative; (الباء) preposition and (ما) maṣdar-forming particle; (رحبت) like أعجبت; (ثمّ) conjunction; (ولّيتم) like اقترفتم [Note: In the previous verse (24).], (مدبرين) ḥāl (circumstantial) emphasising the meaning of the verb, accusative..
The interpreted maṣdar (ما رحبت) is in the position of a genitive by the bāʾ, attached to an omitted ḥāl of الأرض, because the bāʾ is for accompaniment (mulābasa), i.e. "it became narrow while bound up with its vastness".
The clause «نصركم الله» has no grammatical position, the answer to an implied oath.
The clause «أعجبتكم كثرتكم» is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «لم تغن …» is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the clause أعجبتكم.
The clause «ضاقت … الأرض» is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the clause أعجبتكم.
The clause «رحبت» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (ما).
The clause «ولّيتم …» is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the clause ضاقت.

* Morphology:
(مواطن): plural of موطن, a noun of place of the verb وطن يطن, of the ضرب pattern; its wazn is مفعل with fatḥa on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn, because its ʿayn in the imperfect has kasra; the wazn of مواطن is مفاعل.
(حنين): name of a valley between Mecca and al-Ṭāʾif; its wazn is فعيل with ḍamma on the fāʾ and fatḥa on the ʿayn.
(كثرة): an aural (samāʿī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the verb كثر يكثر, of the كرم pattern; its wazn is فعلة with fatḥa then sukūn. There is another maṣdar, كثارة with fatḥa on the kāf.
(مدبرين): plural of مدبر, active participle from the quadriliteral أدبر; its wazn is مفعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.

* Benefits:
1- The Day of Ḥunayn:
Ḥunayn is a valley near al-Ṭāʾif, between it and Mecca some ten-odd miles. The story of the battle
is that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, after the conquest of Mecca, went out to Ḥunayn to fight Hawāzin and Thaqīf with twelve thousand, while the polytheists were four thousand from Hawāzin and Thaqīf; over Hawāzin was Mālik ibn ʿAwf, and over Thaqīf Kināna ibn ʿAbd Yā Layl. When the two hosts met, some of the Muslims said: We will not be defeated today for lack of numbers. The polytheists had lain in ambush in the valley, and they rained a downpour of arrows on the Muslims, so the Muslims were exposed and fell back. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ began spurring his mule towards the unbelievers, and none remained around him except al-ʿAbbās, Abū Sufyān ibn al-Ḥārith and Ayman ibn Umm Ayman, and a small number were killed before him. Al-ʿAbbās said: I was holding the bridle [Translator's note: the source prints "بالجام", for "بلجام"] of the mule of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, holding it back so that it would not hasten. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: O ʿAbbās, call the people of the Samura. So al-ʿAbbās, who was a man with a loud voice, called out: O people of the Samura! By Allah, their turning back when they heard my voice was like the turning of cows to their young, and they said: Here we are, here we are! The battle grew fierce and the furnace grew hot, and he ﷺ was saying: "I am the Prophet, no lie; I am the son of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib", and he threw pebbles at the faces of the unbelievers, then said: They are defeated, by the Lord of Muḥammad. The narrator says: So they were defeated after that.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr related that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, reinforced His Messenger with five thousand angels. The polytheists fled to al-Ṭāʾif, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ besieged them, then withdrew from them and prayed for their guidance, and they came to him after that guided. Then he divided the spoils, and won over the hearts of some people with them. Some of the Anṣār said something objecting to the division of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gathered them and said to them: Are you not content that the people go back with sheep and camels while you go back with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? By Allah, if the people took one mountain pass and the Anṣār another pass, I would take the pass of the Anṣār. Indeed, your appointed meeting is at the Pool. So the people wept and apologised.
2- In this verse we are concerned with the word (مواطن), which is put in the genitive with the fatḥa instead of the kasra because it is a diptote. We shall set out below some of the diptote forms, because they are liable to be forgotten, and reminder benefits, renews and helps. These forms are:
1- What is on the wazn (مفاعل), like مساجد, or (مفاعيل), like مصابيح, and what resembles these two wazns, such as (فعائل) as in خزائن, (فعالل) as in قماقم, or (فعاليل) as in بهاليل (its singular is بهلول, meaning the noble chief).
These wazns and their like are called the forms of the ultimate plural (ṣiyagh muntahā al-jumūʿ).
2- The indefinite adjective on the wazn (أفعل) if its feminine is فعلاء, e.g.: أسمر سمراء, or فعلان if the wazn of its feminine is فعلى, e.g.: عطشان عطشى.
3- Every noun ending in the extended alif of the feminine, e.g.: غيداء، صحراء, or the shortened one, e.g. صغرى، كبري [Translator's note: so in the source, for كبرى].
4- Plurals on the wazn (فعلاء), like (شرفاء), and (أفعلاء), like (أنبياء). There are other cases in which a noun is barred from nunation which there is no room to mention here; let them be consulted in their proper sources.
An important observation:
The diptote noun is put in the genitive with the fatḥa instead of the kasra, except when it is annexed (muḍāf) or made definite with (ال), in which case it is put in the genitive with the kasra.

safi-cedvel:26-26.t:
* I'rab:
(ثمّ) conjunction; (أنزل) past verb; (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ); (سكينة) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) [Translator's note: the source prints "منصب"], and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (على رسول) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أنزل), and (الهاء) like the last; (الواو) conjunction; (على المؤمنين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to what the first genitive is attached to, because it is conjoined to it; (الواو) conjunction; (أنزل جنودا) like أنزل سكينة.. (لم) particle of negation and jussive; (تروا) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (الواو) conjunction; (عذّب) like أنزل, and the fāʿil is "هو"; (الذين) relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of an accusative, mafʿūl bihi; (كفروا) past verb and its fāʿil.
(الواو) resumptive; (ذلك) demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of a nominative, mubtadaʾ (subject).. and (اللام) for distance and (الكاف) for address; (جزاء) khabar (predicate), nominative; (الكافرين) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
The clause «أنزل الله …» is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the clause ولّيتم [Note: In the previous verse (25).].
The clause «أنزل جنودا …» is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the clause أنزل الله …
The clause «لم تروها» is in the position of an accusative, a naʿt (adjective) of (جنودا).
The clause «عذّب …» is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the clause أنزل الله.
The clause «كفروا» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «ذلك جزاء الكافرين» has no grammatical position, causal (taʿlīliyya).

safi-cedvel:27-27.t:
* I'rab:
(ثم) a particle of resumption [Note: (ثمّ) occurs in the Noble Book without the conjunction being intended, because the meaning would be impossible, as in verse (19) of Sūrat al-ʿAnkabūt: أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا كَيْفَ يُبْدِئُ اللَّهُ الْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ …; (ثمّ) there is for resumption, not for conjunction, because it is impossible that they should see the restoration of creation, since it has not occurred … And in this verse with which we are concerned, conjoining the turning in repentance — which is a verb for the future — to the sending down of the hosts and the punishment of the unbelievers — which is a past act that has already taken place — this conjoining does not accord with the meaning.], (يتوب) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil (agent), nominative; (من بعد) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يتوب); (ذلك) like the previous, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), in the position of a genitive; (على) preposition; (من) relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of a genitive, attached to (يتوب); (يشاء) like يتوب, and the fāʿil is "هو"; (الواو) resumptive; (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative; (غفور) khabar (predicate), nominative; (رحيم) second khabar, nominative.
The clause «يتوب الله …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يشاء» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).
The clause «الله غفور..» has no grammatical position, resumptive and causal (taʿlīliyya).

safi-cedvel:28-28.t:
* I'rab:
(يأيّها الذين آمنوا) its i'rab has already passed [Note: In verse (23) of this sūra.], (إنّما) the restraining particle (mā kāffa) and the restrained (makfūfa); (المشركون) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the wāw; (نجس) khabar (predicate), nominative, on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e.: "ذوو نجس"; (الفاء) conjunction, to link the effect with the cause [Note: Or it links the apodosis of an implied condition.], (لا) prohibitive, jussive-governing; (يقربوا) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn..
and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (المسجد) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (الحرام) naʿt (adjective) of المسجد, accusative; (بعد) adverb of time, accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (لا يقربوا); (عام) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (ها) a particle of alerting; (ذا) demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of a genitive, ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) of عام or a badal (substitute) of it; (الواو) conjunction; (إن) a jussive conditional particle; (خفتم) past verb, indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of a jussive, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) … and (تم) a pronoun, fāʿil; (عيلة) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (سوف) particle of the future; (يغني) imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative; (من فضل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يغني), and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (إن) like the first; (شاء) past verb, indeclinable, in the position of a jussive, and the fāʿil is "هو"; (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb — an abrogator (nāsikh); (الله) the Name of Majesty, the noun of إنّ, accusative; (عليم) khabar of إنّ, nominative; (حكيم) second khabar, nominative.
The clause «يأيّها الذين …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «المشركون نجس» has no grammatical position, the response to the vocative (jawāb al-nidāʾ).
The clause (لا يقربوا) has no grammatical position, conjoined to an implied clause which is an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) coming as an answer to an implied question, the implied form being: "Take heed, so let the polytheists not approach the Sacred Mosque" [Note: Or it is the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if they resolve to visit Mecca, then let them not approach the Sacred Mosque".].
The clause «إن خفتم …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause that is the response to the vocative.
The clause «سوف يغنيكم الله» is in the position of a jussive, the apodosis of the condition, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «إن شاء …» has no grammatical position, parenthetical … and the apodosis of the condition is omitted, its implied form being "فعل" ("He will do so").
The clause «إنّ الله عليم …» has no grammatical position, resumptive and causal (taʿlīliyya).

* Morphology:
(نجس): an aural (samāʿī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the verb نجس ينجس, of the فرح pattern and the كرم pattern, and in one dialect of the نصر pattern; its wazn is فعل with two fatḥas. In al-Qāmūs: النجس with fatḥa, with kasra, and with vowelled middle letter, like كتف and عضد.
(عيلة): maṣdar of عال يعيل, of the سار pattern; its wazn is فعلة with fatḥa then sukūn.

* Benefits:
In this verse occurs His saying, the Exalted: إِنَّمَا الْمُشْرِكُونَ نَجَسٌ. It is an eloquent simile (tashbīh balīgh) that bestows on the polytheists the attribute of impurity: they are not merely made impure, but they are pure impurity itself. By this the meaning of polytheism and unbelief is defined — how it brands its holder with the utmost attributes of filth, ugliness and foulness. For this creature, when he has turned aside from the highway of faith and mounted the devil of unbelief, has been transformed into impurity and filth; he does not deserve existence, and we cannot deal with him or live alongside him; rather, one must purify oneself of him and rid society of his plague and harm. There is no expression more severe and more forceful than this expression to embody the meaning of unbelief and polytheism in the reality and life of people. The majority of jurists hold that the impurity in the noble verse is figurative (maʿnawī): whoever touches an unbeliever does not become impure, and likewise when he dies his body remains pure. And Allah knows best.

safi-cedvel:120-120.t:
* I'rab:
(ما كان لأهل) like «ما كان للنبيّ» [Note: In verse 113 of this surah.], (المدينة) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (الواو) a conjunction; (من) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of genitive, conjoined to أهل; (حول) an adverb of place, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted ṣila (relative clause) of من, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (من الأعراب) a preposition and its genitive noun, a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the relative noun من; (أن يتخلّفوا) like «أن يستغفروا» [Note: In verse 113 of this surah.], (عن رسول) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يتخلّفوا); (اللَّه) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (الواو) a conjunction; (لا) negative; (يرغبوا) conjoined to (يتخلّفوا), subjunctive (manṣūb), the sign of the subjunctive being the deletion of the nūn [Note: It may be jussive by (لا), taking it as prohibitive.], and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (بأنفس) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يرغبوا), and (هم) like the last; (عن نفس) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يرغبوا), and (الهاء) like هم; (ذلك) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and (اللام) for distance and (الكاف) for address; (الباء) a preposition; (أنّ) a particle resembling the verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) — and (هم) a pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of anna; (لا) negative; (يصيب) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and (هم) mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (ظمأ) fāʿil, nominative; (الواو) a conjunction in the four places; (لا) redundant (zāʾida), to emphasise the negation, in both places; (نصب، مخمصة) both conjoined to ظمأ, nominative; (في سبيل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of مخمصة [Note: Or an adjective of الظمأ, النصب and المخمصة.], (الله) like the last; (لا) negative; (يطؤون) an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (موطئا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative [Note: Or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative, i.e. "they tread a treading".], (يغيظ) like يصيب, and the fāʿil is "it", i.e. the الموطئ [Note: A noun of place or a maṣdar.], (الكفّار) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (لا ينالون) like لا يطؤون; (من عدوّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (ينالون); (نيلا) mafʿūl muṭlaq, accusative [Note: Or it is a mafʿūl bihi, accusative — i.e. "something attained".], (إلّا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (كتب) a past verb, passive; (اللام) a preposition, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive — attached to (كتب); (الباء) a preposition, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive — attached to (كتب), the bāʾ being causal [Note: I.e. "because of each one of the five things".], (عمل) nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative; (صالح) a naʿt of عمل, nominative; (إنّ الله): its i'rab has already been given [Note: In verse (118) of this surah.], (لا يضيع) like لا يصيب, and the fāʿil is "he", i.e. Allah; (أجر) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (المحسنين) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
The clause «ما كان لأهل …» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «يتخلّفوا …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle relative (أن).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يتخلّفوا..) is in the position of nominative as the postponed noun of kāna.
The clause «يرغبوا..» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يتخلّفوا.
The clause «ذلك بأنّهم …» has no grammatical position, being explanatory of cause (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «لا يصيبهم ظمأ» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of anna.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّهم لا يصيبهم …) is in the position of genitive by the bāʾ, attached to the omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (ذلك).
The clause «لا يطؤون …» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause لا يصيبهم.
The clause «يغيظ..» is in the position of accusative as a naʿt of (موطئا).
The clause «لا ينالون …» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause لا يصيبهم.
The clause «كتب.. عمل» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the obedient believers.
The clause «إنّ الله لا يضيع …» has no grammatical position, being explanatory of cause.
The clause «لا يضيع …» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of inna.

* Morphology:
(ظمأ): an aurally transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the verb ظمئ يظمأ, of the فرح class; its pattern is فعل with two fatḥas. There are other maṣdars: ظمء with fatḥa then sukūn, ظماء with fatḥa on the ẓāʾ, and ظماءة with fatḥa on the ẓāʾ.
(نصب): an aurally transmitted maṣdar of the verb نصب ينصب, of the فرح class; its pattern is فعل with two fatḥas.
(موطئا): a noun of place from the three-letter verb وطأ, of the فرح class; its pattern is مفعل with fatḥa on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn, because the verb is an assimilated weak verb (mithāl) whose fāʾ is deleted in the imperfect.
It is also a mīmī maṣdar of the same verb and on the same pattern.
(نيلا): the maṣdar of نال ينال; its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn. It may be meant as the thing attained, and so used as a noun.

* Benefits:
In this verse there is proof that whoever intends obedience to Allah, his standing, sitting, walking, movement and stillness are all good deeds recorded with Allah. The scholars differed over the ruling of this verse.
Qatāda said: This ruling is specific to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: when he went on an expedition in person, no one could stay behind from him. Al-Walīd ibn Muslim said: I heard al-Awzāʿī, Ibn al-Mubārak, Ibn Jābir and Saʿīd saying about this verse: It is for the first of this Umma and its last. On this view the verse is firmly established (muḥkam) and was not abrogated. Ibn Zayd said: This was when the people of Islam were few; when they became many, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, abrogated it and permitted staying behind for whoever wished, by His saying: «وما كان المؤمنون لينفروا كافة». But the sound statement on this matter is what al-Wāḥidī transmitted from ʿAṭiyya, who said: It was not for them to stay behind from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he called them and commanded them, because obedience is not obligatory unless he commands; and likewise other imams and governors: when they summon or designate, obedience becomes obligatory.

safi-cedvel:121-121.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) a conjunction; (لا) negative; (ينفقون نفقة) like «يطؤون موطئا» «1»; (صغيرة) a naʿt (adjective) of نفقة, accusative (manṣūb); (الواو) a conjunction; (لا) redundant (zāʾida), to emphasise the negation; (كبيرة) conjoined to صغيرة, accusative; (الواو) a conjunction; (لا يقطعون واديا) like «لا يطؤون موطئا» «2»; (إلّا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (كتب لهم) like the earlier one [Note: In the previous verse (120).], and the implied nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is "the deed" indicated by the spending and the crossing of the valley; (اللام) the lām of explaining cause (taʿlīl); (يجزي) an imperfect verb, subjunctive (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām, and (هم) an attached pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ); (أحسن) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle [Note: Or a relative noun in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, with the clause as its ṣila and the referent pronoun omitted.], (كانوا) an incomplete past verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) — indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the wāw is the noun of kāna; (يعملون) like يطؤون «5».
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يجزيهم) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (كتب).
The interpreted maṣdar (ما كانوا) is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
[Translator's note: The markers «1», «2», «5» refer to footnotes not reproduced in this entry; they point back to verse 120 (يطؤون موطئا).]

* Morphology:
(واديا): a primitive (jāmid) noun for the low ground between two mountains; its pattern is فاعل. الوادي is derived from the verb يدي يدي وديا الشيء, meaning "to flow", because water flows (يدي) in it, i.e. runs; the verb is of the ضرب class.
[Translator's note: The source prints «يدي يدي»; the verb meant is ودى يدي.]

safi-cedvel:122-122.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) a conjunction; (ما كان): its i'rab has already been given [Note: In the previous verse (120).], (المؤمنون) the noun of kāna, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the wāw; (اللام) the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd); (ينفروا) an imperfect verb, subjunctive (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām; (كافّة) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent), accusative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن ينفروا) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of kāna.
(الفاء) resumptive; (لولا) a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ) meaning "why not (هلّا)"; (نفر) a past verb; (من كلّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl of طائفة — an adjective placed before the noun it qualifies — ; (فرقة) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (من) a preposition, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive — attached to an adjective of فرقة; (طائفة) the fāʿil of نفر, nominative; (اللام) for explaining cause (taʿlīl); (يتفقّهوا) an imperfect verb, like ينفروا; (في الدين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يتفقّهوا); (الواو) a conjunction; (لينذروا) like (ليتفقّوا) [Translator's note: Thus in the source; meant is «ليتفقّهوا».]; (قوم) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative, and (هم) muḍāf ilayhi.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يتفقّهوا) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to (نفر).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن ينذروا) is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the first interpreted maṣdar and attached to what it is attached to.
(إذا) an adverb of future time, stripped of condition, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative, attached to (ينذروا); (رجعوا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (إليهم) like منهم, attached to (رجعوا); (لعلّ) a particle resembling the verb, for hope (tarajjī) — an abrogator (nāsikh) — and (هم) a pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of laʿalla; (يحذرون) like يطؤون «1».
The clause «ما كان المؤمنون لينفروا …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause «ما كان لأهل» «2».
The clause «ينفروا …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle relative (أن).
The clause «نفر.. طائفة» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «يتفقّهوا …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the implied particle relative (أن).
The clause «ينذروا …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the implied particle relative (أن).
The clause «رجعوا …» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «لعلّهم يحذرون» has no grammatical position, being explanatory of cause (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «يحذرون» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of laʿalla.
[Translator's note: The markers «1» and «2» refer to footnotes not reproduced in this entry; they point back to verse 120.]

safi-cedvel:123-123.t:
* I'rab:
(يأيّها الذين آمنوا قاتلوا) like «يأيّها … اتّقوا» [Note: In verse (119) of this surah.], (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (يلون) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (من الكفّار) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of يلونكم; (الواو) a conjunction; (اللام) the lām of command; (يجدوا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the deletion of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (في) a preposition, and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive — attached to (يجدوا) [Note: Or attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi of the verb يجدوا. (3, 5) In verse (119) of this surah.], (غلظة) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb); (الواو) a conjunction; (اعلموا) like اتّقوا «3»; (أنّ اللَّه) like «إنّ اللَّه» [Note: In verse (118) of this surah.], (مع المتقين) like «مع الصادقين» «5».
The clause «(the vocative) يأيّها الذين …» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «قاتلوا …» has no grammatical position, being the answer to the vocative.
The clause «يلونكم …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the second relative noun (الذين).
The clause «يجدوا …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the answer to the vocative.
The clause «اعلموا …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the answer to the vocative [Note: It may be cut off as a resumption, also with no grammatical position.].
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ اللَّه مع المتّقين) is in the position of accusative, standing in place of the two objects of اعلموا.

* Morphology:
(يلونكم): it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by sukūn and iʿlāl by deletion. Its origin is يليونكم with ḍamma on the second yāʾ; the ḍamma on the yāʾ was felt to be heavy, so it was given sukūn and the vowel was transferred to the lām. When two sukūns met, the yāʾ and the wāw, the yāʾ was deleted, and it became يلونكم. It also contains iʿlāl by deletion because its past tense is a separated doubly-weak verb (lafīf mafrūq), whose fāʾ — the wāw — is deleted in the imperfect; so the pattern is يعونكم.
(غلظة): an aurally transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the verb غلظ يغلظ, of the نصر, ضرب and كرم classes; its pattern is فعلة with kasra on the fāʾ. There are other maṣdars with ḍamma and fatḥa on the fāʾ, and غلظ with kasra on the ghayn, and غلاظة with kasra on the ghayn.

safi-cedvel:58-58.t:
* I'rab:
(ومنهم من يلمز) like ومنهم من يقول [Note: In verse (49) of this surah.], and (الكاف) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (في الصدقات) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يلمز), with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. regarding the distribution of the alms. (الفاء) conjunction. (إن) a conditional particle causing the jussive. (أعطوا) a past verb, passive, in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ)..
and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (من) a preposition and (ها) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (أعطوا); the preposition is partitive or explicative. (رضوا) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma..
and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), and it is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (الواو) conjunction. (إنّ) [Translator's note: so in the source, for (إن)] like the first. (لم) a particle of negation. (يعطوا) an imperfect verb, jussive as the protasis, the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn ... and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil. (منها) like the first, attached to (يعطوا). (إذا) of surprise (fujāʾiyya). (هم يسخطون) like هم يجمحون [Note: In the previous verse (57).]
The clause «منهم من يلمزك ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause in the previous verse.
The clause «يلمزك» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).
The clause «إن أعطوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause منهم من يلمزك.
The clause «رضوا» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a jussive-causing condition, not joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «إن لم يعطوا» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause إن أعطوا.
The clause «هم يسخطون» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined with the (إذا) of surprise.
The clause «يسخطون» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (هم).

* Morphology:
(أعطوا): it has iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion; its origin is أعطيوا with ḍamma on the hamza and the yāʾ.
