The ḍamma on the yāʾ was felt heavy, so its vowel was transferred to the ṭāʾ — iʿlāl by making quiescent — then the yāʾ was deleted because it met, quiescent, with the wāw of the plural, so it became أعطوا. Its pattern is أفعوا.
(يعطوا): it has iʿlāl by deletion; its origin is يعطاوا. Two sukūns met, the alif and the wāw, so the alif was deleted and it became يعطوا. Its pattern is يفعوا with fatḥa on the ʿayn, and the fatḥa was left on the ṭāʾ as an indication of the deleted alif.

* Benefits:
In this verse occurs His saying, the Exalted: وَإِنْ لَمْ يُعْطَوْا مِنْها إِذا هُمْ يَسْخَطُونَ. The grammarians parsed (إذا) as a particle of surprise. We shall clarify something of what relates to this particle, because it may be obscure to many.
1- The إذا of surprise is restricted to nominal clauses; it needs no response, does not occur at the start of speech, and indicates the present, not the future, as in: خرجت فإذا الأسد بالباب (I went out, and lo, the lion was at the door). Of this is His saying, the Exalted: فَأَلْقاها فَإِذا هِيَ حَيَّةٌ تَسْعى. The scholars have differed about it in several views:
a- It is a particle according to al-Akhfash, and this view is supported by their saying: خرجت فإذا إنّ زيدا بالباب, with kasra on إن, because what comes after (إنّ) does not govern what precedes it.
b- It is an adverb of place according to al-Mubarrad, and an adverb of time according to al-Zajjāj. Ibn Mālik chose that it is a particle of surprise, Ibn ʿUṣfūr chose that it is an adverb of place, and al-Zamakhsharī chose that it is an adverb of time. The first view, which considers it a particle of surprise, is the most preponderant of the views, since it does not need interpretation. As for those who considered it an adverb, they supposed an omitted governor for it. We side with the science of the principles of grammar (uṣūl al-naḥw), where the theorists established the following rule:
If two analyses are equal, one of them needing an implied element and the other not needing one, then not supposing an implied element is preferable.
2- If the إذا of surprise occurs joined to the clause of the apodosis of a jussive-causing condition, as in this noble verse, the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis. It is known that the clause of the apodosis of a jussive-causing condition must be joined with the fāʾ or the إذا of surprise in order to be in the position of jussive as the apodosis.

safi-cedvel:59-59.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction. (لو) a conditional particle not causing the jussive. (أنّ) a particle resembling the verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) — and (هم) a pronoun in the position of accusative, the noun of anna. (رضوا) like the previous one [Note: In the previous verse (58).], (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (آتى) a past verb, indeclinable on the implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the alif. (هم) an attached pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ). (الواو) conjunction. (رسول) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the Name of Majesty, nominative, and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (الواو) conjunction. (قالوا) a past verb and its fāʿil. (حسب) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative, and (نا) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (الله) the Name of Majesty, khabar (predicate), nominative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّهم رضوا) is in the position of nominative as the fāʿil of an omitted verb, implied as ثبت, i.e. had their contentment been established ...
(السين) a particle of the future. (يؤتي) an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the implied ḍamma on the yāʾ, and (نا) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative. (من فضل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يؤتي), and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (الواو) conjunction. (رسول) conjoined to the last Name of Majesty, and (الهاء) like the last. (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb — an abrogator — and (نا) a pronoun in the position of accusative, the noun of inna. (إلى الله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (راغبون), which is the khabar of inna, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw.
The clause «(ثبت) رضاهم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to an earlier resumptive clause.
The clause «رضوا ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of anna.
The clause آتاهم الله ... has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative.
The clause «وقالوا ...» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause رضوا.
The clause «حسبنا الله ...» is in the position of accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «سيؤتينا الله ...» has no grammatical position: a resumption carrying the sense of giving the reason for, or explaining, the speech reported.
The clause «إنّا ... راغبون» has no grammatical position: resumptive and causal, or explicative.
The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of (لو) is omitted, i.e. had they done that, it would have been better for them.

* Morphology:
(راغبون): plural of راغب, the active participle of رغب; its pattern is فاعل.

safi-cedvel:60-60.t:
* I'rab:
(انّما) the restricting particle and the restricted (kāffa wa-makfūfa). (الصدقات) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ). (للفقراء) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ. (الواو) conjunction in the seven following places. (المساكين، العاملين، المؤلّفة الغارمين، ابن ...) genitive (majrūr) words conjoined (maʿṭūf) to الفقراء, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ in the words المساكين، العاملين، الغارمين. (على) a preposition and (ها) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (العاملين). (قلوب) nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of the passive participle المؤلّفة, nominative, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (في الرقاب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar and conjoined to the first prepositional phrase. (في سبيل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar and conjoined to the first prepositional phrase. (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; and likewise (السبيل). (فريضة) a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb [Note: Or a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial).. and (فريضة) may mean "made obligatory", so it follows the course of] [Translator's note: the note breaks off here in the source], accusative (manṣūb). (من الله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (فريضة). (الواو) resumptive. (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ, nominative. (عليم) khabar, nominative. (حكيم) a second khabar, nominative.
The clause «الصدقات للفقراء ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «(فرض) فريضة ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «الله عليم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.

* Morphology:
(المؤلّفة): the passive participle of the quadriliteral ألّف; its pattern is مفعّلة with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the ʿayn.
(الغارمين): plural of الغارم, the active participle of the triliteral غرم; and of it is فاعل [Translator's note: so in the source; i.e. its pattern is فاعل].

* Rhetoric:
Variation of particles (mukhālafat al-ḥurūf): in His saying, the Exalted: إِنَّمَا الصَّدَقاتُ لِلْفُقَراءِ to the end of the verse. This is a charming art among the arts of rhetoric, subtle in its derivation and fine in its purport. He turned from «اللام» to «في» in the last four, and that is for a secret hidden from the superficial observer: namely, that the first four categories are owners of whatever may be paid to them, and they take it only as property, so the entry of the lām was fitting for them. As for the last four, they do not own what is spent toward them — indeed it is not even spent to them, but on interests connected with them. The wealth spent on the necks (slaves) is received by the masters with whom the slaves have contracted (al-mukātabūn) and the sellers; their share is not spent into their own hands so that it should be expressed with the lām, which indicates their owning what is spent toward them; rather they are the places of this spending and of the interest connected with it. Likewise the workers (al-ʿāmilūn) [Translator's note: so in the source; the context requires the debtors (al-ghārimūn)]: their share is spent to their creditors, to free their liability, not to them. As for the way of Allah, that is clear in it. As for the wayfarer, it is as if he were included in the way of Allah, and he was singled out for mention only to draw attention to his particular status. Moreover, it is stripped of both particles, and conjoining it to what is made genitive by the lām is possible, but conjoining it to what is nearer to it is more fitting.

* Benefits:
The recipients of zakāt.
This verse defined the eight categories to whom zakāt is due, and they are:
1- The poor (al-fuqarāʾ).
2- The needy (al-masākīn): they are the needy people whose income does not meet their need. The scholars then differed about the difference between the faqīr and the miskīn. Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid, ʿIkrima and al-Zuhrī said: the faqīr is the one who does not beg and the miskīn is the beggar. Al-Shāfiʿī said: the faqīr is one who has neither wealth nor trade, and the miskīn is one who has wealth or a trade, but it does not suffice him. The jurists said: the faqīr is one whose resources are less than half his need, and the miskīn is one whose resources are more than half his need.
3- الْعامِلِينَ عَلَيْها (those employed over it): they are the collectors who undertake gathering the alms, receiving them from those who owe them and placing them where they belong; they are given from the alms wealth according to the wages of their work, whether they are poor or rich. This is the view of Ibn ʿUmar, and al-Shāfiʿī held it.
4- الْمُؤَلَّفَةِ قُلُوبُهُمْ (those whose hearts are to be reconciled): they are of two kinds, Muslims and unbelievers. The Muslims are of two kinds: a group of the Arab nobles and tribal leaders whom the Prophet ﷺ used to give in order to reconcile their hearts, their Islam being weak; and people who had embraced Islam and whose Islam was strong, but the Prophet ﷺ gave them to win over their people. As for the second kind, they are the Muslims far from their brethren and bordering on the unbelievers, who are weak; they are given so that their faith remains strong and so that the unbelievers do not lead them astray. As for those to be reconciled from among the unbelievers, they are people whose evil is feared and whose Islam is hoped for.
5- وَفِي الرِّقابِ (and for the necks): they are the slaves under a contract of manumission (al-mukātabūn), who are given so that they may be freed. This is the view of al-Shāfiʿī and most of the jurists. Another view is that slaves are bought and freed.
6- The debtors (al-ghārimīn): those unable to repay a debt, on condition that the cause of the debt was not disobedience to Allah.
7- In the way of Allah: i.e. in jihad, or every deed that pleases Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
8- The wayfarer (ibn al-sabīl): the traveller cut off from his wealth; he is given what will bring him to his destination.

safi-cedvel:88-89.t:
* I'rab:
(لكن) a particle of rectification (istidrāk), its last letter vowelled with kasra because of the meeting of two sukūns; (الرسول) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ); (الواو) conjunction; (الذين) relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to الرسول; (آمنوا) like رضوا «1»; (مع) adverb, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (mutaʿalliq) (آمنوا), and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (جاهدوا) like رضوا «2»; (بأموال) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (جاهدوا), and (هم) muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) conjunction; (أنفسهم) conjoined to أموالهم, genitive (majrūr), with a muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) resumptive; (أولئك) demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ ...
and (الكاف) a particle of address; (اللام) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); (الخيرات) delayed mubtadaʾ, nominative; (الواو) conjunction; (أولئك) like the first; (هم) a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) [Note: Or a detached pronoun, a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is (المفلحون), and the nominal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ أولئك.]; (المفلحون) khabar of the mubtadaʾ أولئك.
The clause «الرسول ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «جاهدوا ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ.
The clause «أولئك لهم الخيرات» is "in the position of [sic]" resumptive [Note: Or conjoined to the resumptive clause لكن الرسول..].
[Translator's note: The source reads «في محلّ لها استئنافيّة», evidently a slip for «لا محلّ لها استئنافيّة» ("has no grammatical position, resumptive").]
The clause «لهم الخيرات» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أولئك).
The clause «أولئك ... المفلحون» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause أولئك لهم ...
(أعدّ) past verb; (الله) the Divine Name, fāʿil (agent), nominative; (لهم) like the earlier one [Note: in the previous verse (88).], attached to (أعدّ); (جنّات) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative, its sign of accusative being the kasra; (تجري ... العظيم) its i'rab has been given [Note: in verse (72) of this sūra.].
The clause «أعدّ الله ...» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) of the success.
The clause «تجري ...» is in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of جنّات.
The clause «ذلك الفوز ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
Part Eleven
The remainder of Sūrat al-Tawba
from verse 93 to verse 129; Sūrat Yūnus from verse 1 to verse 109; and Sūrat Hūd from verse 1 to verse 5 90-

safi-cedvel:90-90.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (جاء) past verb; (المعذّرون) fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ), its sign of nominative being the waw; (من الإعراب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from (المعذّرون); (اللام) the lām of cause (lām al-taʿlīl); (يؤذن) imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after the lām of cause, and it is passive; (اللام) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, and it is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), in the position of nominative.
[Translator's note: «من الإعراب» in the source is evidently a typographical error for «من الأعراب» of the verse.]
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن يؤذن..) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to (جاء).
(الواو) conjunction; (قعد) like جاء; (الذين) relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as fāʿil; (كذبوا) like رضوا «1»; (اللَّه) the Divine Name, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative; (الواو) conjunction; (رسول) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the Divine Name, accusative, and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) [Note: i.e. they held back from coming and did not make excuses.]; (السين) a particle of the future; (يصيب) imperfect verb, nominative; (الذين) relative, mafʿūl bihi; (كفروا) like رضوا «3»; (منهم) like لهم, attached to an omitted ḥāl from the fāʿil of كفروا; (عذاب) fāʿil, nominative; (أليم) naʿt (adjective) of عذاب, nominative.
The clause «جاء المعذّرون ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يؤذن لهم» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle relative (أن).
The clause «قعد الذين ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «كذبوا ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
The clause «سيصيب.. عذاب» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «كفروا ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the second relative (الذين).

* Morphology:
(المعذّرون): plural of المعذّر, an active participle either from عذّر, i.e. he took pains to make excuses, the doubling having come [for that meaning], or from the five-letter verb اعتذر, the tāʾ then being changed to dhāl after being made quiescent and its vowel transferred to the ʿayn before it.. In either case its wazn is مفتعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.
(الأعراب): a generic collective noun (ism jamʿ jinsī), they being the people of the desert; the singular is أعرابيّ, and the wazn of أعراب is أفعال.

safi-cedvel:91-91.t:
* I'rab:
(ليس) defective, frozen (jāmid) past verb — an abrogator (nāsikh); (على الضعفاء) a preposition and its genitive noun, the fronted khabar (predicate) of laysa; (الواو) conjunction; (لا) redundant (zāʾida), to emphasize the negation; (على المرضى) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) what the first preposition phrase is attached to, so it is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it; its sign of genitive is the kasra implied (muqaddar) on the alif; (الواو) conjunction; (لا) like the first; (على) a preposition; (الذين) relative, in the position of genitive, attached to what the first preposition phrase is attached to, so it is conjoined to it; (لا) negative; (يجدون) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ).. and the waw is the fāʿil (agent); (ما) an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective (nakira mawṣūfa) [Note: Or a relative noun in the position of accusative, the clause after it being the ṣila (relative clause), with the returning pronoun omitted.], in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (ينفقون) like يجدون; (حرج) the delayed subject (ism) of laysa, nominative; (إذا) an adverb of the future containing the sense of a condition, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative, attached to the content of the implied answer; (نصحوا) past verb with its fāʿil; (للَّه) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (نصحوا); (الواو) conjunction; (رسول) conjoined to the Divine Name, genitive (majrūr), and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (ما) negative; (على المحسنين) a preposition and its genitive noun, a fronted khabar, its sign of genitive being the yāʾ; (من سبيل) a redundant preposition and its noun, genitive in wording, nominative in position, as mubtadaʾ (subject); (الواو) resumptive; (اللَّه) the Divine Name, mubtadaʾ, nominative; (غفور) khabar, nominative; (رحيم) second khabar, nominative.
The clause «ليس على الضعفاء ... حرج» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «لا يجدون ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
The clause «ينفقون ...» is in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of (ما), with the returning pronoun omitted.
The clause «نصحوا ...» is in the position of genitive through (إذا) being annexed to it.. and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes, i.e.: if they are sincere.. then there is no blame on them.
The clause «ما على المحسنين من سبيل» has no grammatical position, a resumption that confirms the content of what precedes.
The clause «اللَّه غفور» has no grammatical position, resumptive.

* Rhetoric:
The art of talmīʿ or talmīḥ (allusion): in His saying, Exalted is He, «ما عَلَى الْمُحْسِنِينَ مِنْ سَبِيلٍ». It is to allude, within the purport of the speech, to a current proverb, a rare line of poetry, a famous story, or what functions as a proverb. This clause of the verse is a resumption confirming the content of what preceded in the most eloquent manner and the finest composition, and it is among eloquent speech, because its meaning is that there is no way for a reproacher against them, i.e. the reproacher does not pass by them nor cross their land — how far reproach is from them! It functions as a proverb.

safi-cedvel:92-92.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction; (على الذين) like the previous one «1»; (إذا) its i'rab has been given «2», attached to the answer قلت; (ما) redundant (zāʾida); (أتوا) past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif that was dropped because of the meeting of two sukūns.. and the waw is the fāʿil (agent), and (الكاف) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (اللام) the lām of cause (lām al-taʿlīl); (تحمل) imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after the lām, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "anta"; (قلت) past verb with its fāʿil; (لا) negative; (أجد) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ)..
and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, implied as "anā"; (ما) an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective (nakira mawṣūfa) [Note: Or a relative noun in the position of accusative, the clause after it being the ṣila (relative clause), with the returning pronoun omitted.], in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi; (أحمل) like أجد, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (على) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أحملكم).
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن تحملهم ...) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to (أتوك).
(تولّوا) like أتوا; (الواو) of ḥāl (circumstantial); (أعين) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (تفيض) imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is "hiya"; (من الدمع) a preposition and its genitive noun, tamyīz (specification) [Note: It is converted from the fāʿil, i.e. their tears overflow; and (من) may be for the beginning of the extent, so the genitive noun is attached to (تفيض).]; (حزنا) mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), accusative [Note: Or a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl.. or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb.]; (أن) a maṣdar-forming particle that makes the verb accusative; (لا) negative; (يجدوا) imperfect verb, accusative, its sign of accusative being the dropping of the nūn.. and the waw is the fāʿil; (ما) an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective [Note: Or a relative noun in the position of accusative ... the clause being the ṣila, with the returning pronoun omitted, i.e. ما ينفقونه.], in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi; (ينفقون) imperfect verb, nominative.. and the waw is the fāʿil.
The interpreted maṣdar (ألّا يجدوا ...) is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl li-ajlihi, its governing word being حزنا.. or its governing word being تفيض [Note: The interpreted maṣdar may be in the position of genitive by an omitted lām or من.. attached to (تفيض).].
The conditional clause — [the particle], its verb and answer ... — has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
The clause «أتوك ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «تحملهم ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the implied particle relative (أن).
The clause «قلت ...» has no grammatical position, as the answer of a non-jussive condition [Note: The clause (تولّوا..) may be the answer, and the clause قلت in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, with (قد) implied.].
The clause «لا أجد ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «أحملكم عليه» is in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of (ما).
The clause «تولّوا ...» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «أعينهم تفيض ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.
The clause «تفيض ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (أعين).
The clause «يجدوا ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «ينفقون» is in the position of accusative as a naʿt of (ما).

* Benefits:
(إذا) departing from the future:
Mostly إذا, together with its verb, conveys the meaning of the future, but it sometimes departs from this meaning, as occurs in this noble verse. Ibn Hishām explained this in al-Mughnī, saying:
إذا departs from the future, and that is in two ways:
1- That it comes for the past, as in His saying, Exalted is He, وَلا عَلَى الَّذِينَ إِذا ما أَتَوْكَ لِتَحْمِلَهُمْ قُلْتَ لا أَجِدُ ما أَحْمِلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ تَوَلَّوْا وَأَعْيُنُهُمْ تَفِيضُ مِنَ الدَّمْعِ, and His saying, Exalted is He, وَإِذا رَأَوْا تِجارَةً أَوْ لَهْواً انْفَضُّوا إِلَيْها.
2- That it comes for the present, and that is after an oath: as in His saying, Exalted is He, وَاللَّيْلِ إِذا يَغْشى and وَالنَّجْمِ إِذا هَوى, for here it indicates the present.

safi-cedvel:124-125.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (إذا) an adverb of future time containing the meaning of condition, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the content of the apodosis; (ما) redundant (zāʾida); (أنزلت) a past verb, passive, and the tāʾ for the feminine; (سورة) nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative (marfūʿ); (الفاء) connecting the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (من) a preposition, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive — attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate) [Note: The preposition phrase may be an adjective of an omitted fronted khabar, i.e. "a group of them (فريق منهم)" or "some of them (بعض منهم)".], (من) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); (يقول) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil (agent) is "he", and it is the referent pronoun; (أيّ) an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ, nominative, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (زادت) a past verb, and (التاء) for the feminine, and (الهاء) a pronoun, first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (ها) a particle of alerting (tanbīh); (ذه) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as fāʿil; (إيمانا) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb); (الفاء) resumptive; (أمّا) a particle of condition and detailing (tafṣīl); (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ; (آمنوا) like رجعوا [Note: In verse (122) of this surah.], (الفاء) occurring in the apodosis of أمّا; (زادتهم إيمانا) like «زادته إيمانا»; (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (هم) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ; (يستبشرون) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The clause «أنزلت سورة …» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «منهم من يقول …» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «يقول …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (من).
The clause «أيّكم زادته هذه …» is in the position of accusative as the speech (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «زادته هذه …» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أيّكم).
The clause «الذين آمنوا …» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا …» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
[Translator's note: The source lists «آمنوا …» twice, once as resumptive and once as a ṣila; the first line appears to be a duplication.]
The clause «زادتهم إيمانا …» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين) [Note: The connecting fāʾ was originally at the head of the nominal clause, because the original expression is: "whatever may be the case, then those who… (مهما يكن من شيء فالذين …)"; when أمّا took the place of مهما, the fāʾ moved to the khabar.].
The clause «هم يستبشرون …» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the hāʾ in (زادتهم).
The clause «يستبشرون» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).
(الواو) a conjunction; (أمّا الذين) like the first; (في قلوب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (مرض) a postponed mubtadaʾ, nominative; (فزادتهم رجسا) like «فزادتهم إيمانا»; (إلى رجس) a preposition and its genitive noun, a naʿt (adjective) of (رجسا), and (هم) like the last; (الواو) a conjunction; (ماتوا) like رجعوا; (وهم) a pronoun, mubtadaʾ; (كافرون) the khabar of the mubtadaʾ هم, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw.
The clause «الذين في قلوبهم مرض …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause «الذين آمنوا …».
The clause «في قلوبهم مرض..» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «زادتهم رجسا …» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين).
The clause «ماتوا …» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause زادتهم.
The clause «هم كافرون» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the fāʿil of ماتوا.

* Benefits:
أيّ and its uses:
In this verse there occurs His saying, the Exalted, فَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَقُولُ: أَيُّكُمْ زادَتْهُ هذِهِ إِيماناً. We are concerned with (أيّ) with doubled yāʾ; in the noble verse it is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ, nominative. We shall explain below its uses, because of the great benefit in that.
أيّ is a noun and comes in five ways:
1- A conditional noun: as in His saying, the Exalted: أَيًّا ما تَدْعُوا فَلَهُ الْأَسْماءُ الْحُسْنى.
2- An interrogative noun: as in His saying, the Exalted, أَيُّكُمْ زادَتْهُ هذِهِ إِيماناً.
3- A relative noun: as in His saying, the Exalted, ثُمَّ لَنَنْزِعَنَّ مِنْ كُلِّ شِيعَةٍ أَيُّهُمْ أَشَدُّ عَلَى الرَّحْمنِ عِتِيًّا; the implied construction is: "We will surely draw out the one who is most severe (لننزعن الذي هو أشد)". There is disagreement about this verse: Sībawayh said this, while the Kufans and a group of the Basrans differed with him and claimed that in the verse it is interrogative, that it is a mubtadaʾ, and أشدّ is the khabar.
4- It comes indicating the meaning of perfection, occurring as an adjective of an indefinite noun, as in: زيد رجل أيّ رجل ("Zayd is a man — what a man!"), i.e. perfect in the qualities of men. It also comes as a ḥāl after a definite noun, likewise indicating perfection, as in:
مررت بعبد اللَّه أيّ رجل ("I passed by ʿAbd Allāh — what a man!").
5- It is used as a means to address in the vocative what has ال, as in: يا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ حَسْبُكَ اللَّهُ

safi-cedvel:126-126.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for the interrogative of rebuke (istifhām tawbīkhī); (لا) negative, and (الواو) a conjunction; (يرون) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (أنّ) a particle resembling the verb, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of anna; (يفتنون) an imperfect verb, passive, nominative, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (في كلّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يفتنون); (عام) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (مرّة) a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, accusative (manṣūb), i.e. "one trial"; (أو) a conjunction; (مرّتين) conjoined to مرّة, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ; (ثمّ) a conjunction; (لا يتوبون) like لا يطؤون [Note: In verse (120) of this surah.], (الواو) a conjunction; (لا) redundant (zāʾida), to emphasise the negation; (هم يذكّرون) like «هم يستبشرون» [Note: In verse (124) of this surah.].
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّهم يفتنون) is in the position of accusative, standing in place of the two objects of يرون [Note: This is if the verb is one of the heart (mental perception); or it stands in place of the one object if it is one of sight.].
The clause «يرون …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to an earlier resumption [Note: Namely the clause of the condition, its protasis and its apodosis at the beginning of verse (124) of this surah.].
The clause «يفتنون..» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of anna.
The clause «لا يتوبون» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause يفتنون.
The clause «هم يذّكّرون» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause يفتنون.
The clause «يذّكّرون» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (هم).

safi-cedvel:127-127.t:
* I'rab:
(وإذا ما أنزلت سورة): its i'rab has already been given [Note: In verse (124) of this surah.], (نظر) a past verb; (بعض) fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (إلى بعض) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (نظر); (هل) an interrogative particle; (يرى) an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (من) a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; (أحد) genitive in wording, nominative in position, the fāʿil of يرى; (ثمّ) a conjunction; (انصرفوا) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (صرف) like نظر; (اللَّه) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative; (قلوب) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb), and (هم) muḍāf ilayhi; (الباء) a preposition; (أنّهم) like the previous [Note: In the previous verse (126).], (قوم) the khabar (predicate) of anna, nominative; (لا يفقهون) like لا يطؤون [Note: In verse (120) of this surah.].
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّهم قوم..) is in the position of genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (صرف), the bāʾ being causal.
The clause «أنزلت سورة..» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «نظر بعضهم …» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «هل يراكم من أحد …» is in the position of accusative as the speech (maqūl al-qawl) of an implied verb of saying, and this implied saying is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of نظر, i.e. "saying: does anyone see you…".
The clause «انصرفوا..» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause نظر بعضهم.
The clause «صرف اللَّه …» has no grammatical position, being a resumption of supplication, or a resumption for mere information.
The clause «لا يفقهون» is in the position of nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of قوم.

safi-cedvel:128-129.t:
* I'rab:
(اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied oath; (قد) a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); (جاءكم) a past verb, and the pronoun is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (رسول) fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ); (من أنفس) a preposition and its genitive noun, a naʿt (adjective) of رسول [Note: Or attached to (جاءكم), i.e. "from among you".], and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (عزيز) a naʿt of رسول, nominative [Note: Or a fronted khabar (predicate), with the interpreted maṣdar (ما عنّتم) a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause an adjective of رسول.], (على) a preposition, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive — attached to (mutaʿalliq) عزيز; (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle [Note: Or a relative noun in the position of nominative as a postponed mubtadaʾ, with the clause after it as its ṣila and the referent pronoun omitted, i.e. «عنّتم به», i.e. "because of it"; or it is the fāʿil of the resembling adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) عزيز.], (عنتّم) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, and (تم) a pronoun, fāʿil.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما عنتّم) is in the position of nominative as the fāʿil of the resembling adjective عزيز.
(حريص) another naʿt of رسول, nominative; (عليكم) like عليه, attached to حريص; (بالمؤمنين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (رؤف), which is a naʿt of رسول, nominative, and likewise (رحيم).
The clause «جاءكم رسول …» has no grammatical position, being the answer to the implied oath.
The oath clause has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «عنّتم..» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (ما), or of the nominal one.
(الفاء) a conjunction; (إن) a jussive conditional particle; (تولّوا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the sign of the jussive being the deletion of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; one of the two tāʾs has been deleted from the verb for lightness; (الفاء) connecting the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (قل) an imperative verb, and the fāʿil is "you"; (حسبي) mubtadaʾ, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the letter before the yāʾ, and (الياء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (اللَّه) the Name of Majesty, khabar, nominative; (لا) the lā of generic negation; (إله) the noun of lā, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of accusative, and the khabar is omitted, its implied form being "existing (موجود)"; (إلّا) a particle of exception; (هو) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as a badal (substitute) of the pronoun latent in the khabar — or of the position of lā together with its noun — ; (عليه) like the first, attached to (توكّلت), which is a past verb indeclinable on the sukūn, and (التاء) is the fāʿil; (الواو) a conjunction; (هو) mubtadaʾ, in the position of nominative; (ربّ) khabar, nominative; (العرش) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (العظيم) a naʿt of العرش, genitive.
The clause «إن تولّوا …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the implied oath clause.
The clause «قل …» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «حسبي اللَّه» is in the position of accusative as the speech (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «لا إله إلّا هو» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) [Note: A ḥāl may come from the khabar and from the mubtadaʾ, just as it may come from the fāʿil, the mafʿūl, the noun made genitive by a preposition, and from the muḍāf ilayhi when the muḍāf is part of the muḍāf ilayhi.].
The clause «توكّلت» has no grammatical position, being resumptive, emphasising the speech — or parenthetical.
The clause «هو ربّ …» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the ḥāl clause.

* Morphology:
(حريص): a resembling adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) of the verb حرص يحرص, of the ضرب class and the فرح class; its pattern is فعيل. Its feminine is حريصة, and the plural is حرصاء with ḍamma on the ḥāʾ, حراص with kasra on the ḥāʾ and an undoubled rāʾ, and حرّاص with ḍamma on the ḥāʾ and a doubled rāʾ; the plural of حريصة is حراص with kasra on the ḥāʾ, and حرائص.

safi-cedvel:61-61.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive. (من) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, and it is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate), i.e. some of them. (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject). (يؤذون) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ).. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). (النبيّ) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb). (الواو) conjunction. (يقولون) like يؤذون. (هو) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ. (أذن) khabar, nominative. (قل) an imperative verb, and the fāʿil is "you". (أذن) the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, implied as "he". (خير) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr). (اللام) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt of (أذن). (يؤمن) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "he". (بالله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يؤمن). (الواو) conjunction. (يؤمن) like the first. (للمؤمنين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يؤمن) by its being made to include (taḍmīn) the sense of "believes" or "accepts". (الواو) conjunction. (رحمة) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to أذن, nominative. (اللام) a preposition. (الذين) a relative, in the position of genitive, attached to (رحمة). (آمنوا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma..
and the wāw is the fāʿil. (منكم) like منهم, attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of آمنوا. (الواو) conjunction. (الذين) a relative, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ. (يؤذون رسول الله) like يؤذون النبيّ, and the Name of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi. (لهم) like لكم, attached to an omitted fronted khabar. (عذاب) a delayed mubtadaʾ, nominative. (أليم) a naʿt of عذاب, nominative.
The clause «منهم الذين ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يؤذون..» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «يقولون ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «هو أذن..» is in the position of accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «(هو) أذن خير» is in the position of accusative as the speech reported.
The clause «يؤمن بالله» is in the position of nominative as a second khabar of the omitted mubtadaʾ [Note: Or in the position of nominative as a second naʿt of أذن.].
The clause «يؤمن للمؤمنين» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause يؤمن بالله.
The clause «آمنوا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second relative (الذين).
The clause «الذين يؤذون ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «يؤذون رسول ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the third relative (الذين).
The clause «لهم عذاب ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين).

* Morphology:
(أذن): the name of the well-known part of the body (the ear); in the noble verse it is used figuratively, i.e. a listener. Its pattern is فعل with two ḍammas.

* Rhetoric:
Majāz mursal (metonymic trope): in His saying, the Exalted: هُوَ أُذُنٌ. It is originally the name of the organ, and applying it to the person in the sense mentioned is of the category of majāz mursal, like applying "the eye" to the people's lookout, since the eye is what is intended of him. This is applying the part to the whole, and the relation is called partiality (al-juzʾiyya). The poet said:
إذا ما بدت ليلى فكلي أعين ... وإن هي ناجتني فكلي مسامع
(When Laylā appears, all of me is eyes; and if she speaks to me privately, all of me is ears.)

safi-cedvel:62-62.t:
* I'rab:
(يحلفون بالله) its i'rab has already been given [Note: In verse (56) of this surah.], (اللام) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يحلفون). (اللام) causal (taʿlīl). (يرضوا) an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muḍmara) أن after the lām ... and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يرضوكم) is in the position of genitive, attached to (يحلفون).
(الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya). (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ). (الواو) conjunction. (رسول) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the Name of Majesty, nominative. (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (أحقّ) the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, nominative. (أن) an infinitival particle causing the accusative. (يرضوا) like the first, and (الهاء) mafʿūl bihi.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يرضوه) is in the position of nominative as a badal (substitute) of the Name of Majesty or of رسول [Note: If it is a badal of one of them, there is a way for it to be a badal of the other ... and the meaning is: pleasing Allah and pleasing His Messenger is more deserving than pleasing anyone else ... There are other analyses of the i'rab of the verse, among them: (أحقّ) is a fronted khabar and the interpreted maṣdar a delayed mubtadaʾ, and the clause is the khabar of (الله ورسوله), i.e. Allah and His Messenger — pleasing them is more deserving.. It has also been said: (أحق) is the khabar of الرسول because it is the nearer, and the khabar of the Name of Majesty is omitted, indicated by what is mentioned.. And it has been said: the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of genitive by an omitted bāʾ, attached to (أحقّ), i.e. more deserving of being pleased — Ibn Hishām rejected this last derivation. Further, the word (أحقّ) came as the khabar of the two nouns (الله، رسوله) because the Messenger's affair follows Allah's affair, and it was made singular while in the place of the dual; or because (أحقّ), being an elative (ism tafḍīl), came stripped of (ال) and of annexation, with the comparative من implied.].
(إن) a conditional particle causing the jussive. (كانوا) a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) — indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma ... and the wāw is a pronoun, the noun of kāna, and the verb is in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). (مؤمنين) khabar, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ.
The clause «يحلفون ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يرضوكم ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle relative (أن).
The clause «الله ورسوله أحقّ ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of يحلفون.
The clause «يرضوه» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the overt particle relative (أن).
The clause «كانوا مؤمنين» has no grammatical position: resumptive.. and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. if they are believers, then Allah and His Messenger are more deserving of being pleased.

* Morphology:
(يرضوكم): it has iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by making quiescent and iʿlāl by deletion. Its origin is يرضيوكم — with ḍamma on both yāʾs [Translator's note: so in the source]; the ḍamma on the yāʾ was felt heavy, so it was made quiescent and the vowel transferred to the ḍād — iʿlāl by making quiescent — then the yāʾ was deleted because it met, quiescent, with the wāw of the plural — iʿlāl by deletion — so it became يرضوكم. Its pattern is يفعوكم.

* Benefits:
In this verse occurs His saying, the Exalted: وَاللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَحَقُّ أَنْ يُرْضُوهُ. The grammarians parsed: الله, the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ; and رسوله, a conjoined noun. As for the khabar, the views of the grammarians have conflicted about it:
What Abū al-Baqāʾ al-ʿUkbarī says:
The khabar is (أحقّ), and it is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ which is (الله); and الرسول is a second mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, indicated by the khabar of the first, and the implied form becomes (والله أحق أن ترضوه ورسوله أحق) [Translator's note: the source writes ترضوه here and below; the verse has يرضوه].
What Sībawayh says:
As for Sībawayh, he said أحق is the khabar of الرسول and the khabar of the first is omitted, because (رسوله) is nearer to the khabar. This is stronger, since it does not entail separating the mubtadaʾ from its khabar, and also because it is the khabar of what is nearer to it. Like it is the saying of the poet:
نحن بما عندنا وأنت بما ... عندك راض والرأي مختلف
(We are content with what we have, and you with what you have, though opinion differs.)
The point of evidence is that (راض) is the khabar of أنت and cannot be the khabar of نحن. This supports Sībawayh's view, because راض is nearer to the mubtadaʾ (أنت).
It has also been said that (أحقّ) is the khabar of both nouns, because the Messenger's affair follows the affair of Allah the Exalted; and it has been said that the word (أحقّ) was made singular while it has a dual meaning, and the interpreted maṣdar from (أن ترضوه) is in the position of genitive by the implied yāʾ [Translator's note: so in the source, apparently for "the implied bāʾ"], and the implied form becomes (أحق بالرضا).

safi-cedvel:63-63.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for the interrogative of rebuke and disapproval. (لم) a particle of negation and the jussive. (يعلموا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn ... and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). (أنّ) a particle resembling the verb, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of accusative, the noun of anna — it is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn). (من) a conditional noun causing the jussive, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). (يحادد) an imperfect verb, jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and given a kasra because of the meeting of two sukūns, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "he". (الله) the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb). (الواو) conjunction. (رسول) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the Name of Majesty, accusative, and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (أنّ) like the first. (اللام) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of anna. (نار) the delayed noun of anna, accusative. (جهنّم) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa. (خالدا) a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, of the pronoun in (له). (فيها) like له, attached to (خالدا).
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّه من ...) is in the position of accusative, taking the place of the two objects of يعلموا.. or as its single object, in the sense of "know (be acquainted with)".
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ له نار ...) is in the position of nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ — or a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted — the implied form being: his matter is that the fire of Hell is his ... or: that the fire of Hell is his is a true matter.
(ذلك) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ; the reference is to the punishment, (اللام) is for distance and (الكاف) for address. (الخزي) khabar, nominative (marfūʿ). (العظيم) a naʿt (adjective) of الخزي, nominative.
The clause «يعلموا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «من يحادد ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of anna.
The clause «يحادد الله» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: The khabar may be the two clauses of the condition and the apodosis together.].
The clause «(أمره) أنّ له نار» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «ذلك الخزي ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.

safi-cedvel:64-64.t:
* I'rab:
(يحذر) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ). (المنافقون) fāʿil (agent), nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw. (أن) an infinitival particle causing the accusative. (تنزّل) an imperfect verb, passive, accusative (manṣūb). (على) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تنزّل) [Note: Al-Zamakhsharī said: the pronoun in (عليهم) refers to the believers, and the pronoun in (تنبّئهم) refers to the hypocrites ... Others said: the pronoun in both refers to the hypocrites, because if the surah was revealed concerning them, then it is revealed upon them, informing them.], (سورة) nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative. (تنبّئ) like يحذر, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil is "it" (hiya). (الباء) a preposition. (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of genitive, attached to (تنبّئهم). (في قلوب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted ṣila (relative clause) of ما, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تنزّل) is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi [Note: The verb يحذر is intransitive according to al-Mubarrad, and the interpreted maṣdar is genitive by an omitted preposition, implied as (من), i.e. the hypocrites are wary of a surah being revealed ... But Abū Ḥayyān rejected al-Mubarrad's view.].
(قل) an imperative verb, and the fāʿil is "you". (استهزءوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil. (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb. (الله) the Name of Majesty, the noun of inna, accusative. (مخرج) the khabar (predicate) of inna, nominative. (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as the mafʿūl bihi of the active participle مخرج, and the referring pronoun (ʿāʾid) is omitted. (تحذرون) an imperfect verb, nominative ... and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The clause «يحذر المنافقون ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «تنزّل ... سورة» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «تنبئّهم ...» is in the position of nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of سورة.
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «استهزءوا ...» is in the position of accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «إنّ الله مخرج ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption ... or causal.
The clause «تحذرون» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (ما).

safi-cedvel:93-93.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّما) a restraining particle and the restrained one (kāffa wa-makfūfa); (السبيل) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ); (على) a preposition; (الذين) relative, in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; (يستأذنون) imperfect verb, nominative, its sign of nominative being the presence of the nūn.. and the waw is the fāʿil (agent), and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (الواو) of ḥāl (circumstantial); (هم) a detached pronoun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ; (أغنياء) khabar, nominative, barred from tanwīn because it is attached to the extended feminine alif, being on the wazn أفعلاء; (رضوا) past verb, indeclinable on ḍamma..
and the waw is the fāʿil; (الباء) a preposition; (أن) a maṣdar-forming particle that makes the verb accusative; (يكونوا) defective imperfect verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) — accusative (manṣūb), its sign of accusative being the dropping of the nūn.. and the waw is its subject (ism); (مع) adverb, accusative, attached to the khabar of يكونوا; (الخوالف) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr).
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن يكونوا) is in the position of genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (رضوا). (الواو) conjunction; (طبع) past verb; (اللَّه) the Divine Name, fāʿil, nominative; (على قلوب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (طبع), and (هم) an attached pronoun in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; (الفاء) conjunction linking the effect to the cause; (هم) a detached [pronoun], mubtadaʾ; (لا) negative; (يعلمون) like يستأذنون.
The clause «السبيل على الذين ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يستأذنونك..» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «هم أغنياء» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.
The clause «رضوا..» has no grammatical position, a resumption in the context of giving a reason.. or it is an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «يكونوا» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «طبع اللَّه ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause رضوا..
The clause «هم لا يعلمون» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause طبع اللَّه.
The clause «لا يعلمون» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).

safi-cedvel:94-94.t:
* I'rab:
(يعتذرون) like يستأذنون [Note: in verse (93) of this sūra.]; (إلى) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يعتذرون); (إذا) an adverb of the future stripped of the conditional sense, in the position of accusative, attached to (يعتذرون); (رجعتم) past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn.. and (تم) a pronoun, fāʿil (agent); (إليهم) like إليكم, attached to (رجعتم); (قل) imperative verb, and the fāʿil is "anta"; (لا) prohibitive, making the verb jussive; (تعتذروا) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), its sign of jussive being the dropping of the nūn.. and the waw is the fāʿil; (لن) a particle of negation and accusative; (نؤمن) imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "naḥnu"; (لكم) like إليكم, attached to (نؤمن) [Note: It has been said that (اللام) is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), governed by نؤمن in the sense of "we believe [you]".]; (قد) a particle of realization (taḥqīq); (نبأ) past verb, and (نا) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is the Divine Name (اللَّه), nominative (marfūʿ); (من أخبار) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of the implied second object, i.e. "a portion of your news", and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) [Note: If the verb is transitive to three objects, the third object is omitted, its implied form being "established (muthbata)".]; (الواو) conjunction; (السين) a particle of the future; (يرى) imperfect verb, nominative, its sign of nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif; (اللَّه) like the last; (عمل) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (كم) like the last; (الواو) conjunction; (رسول) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the Divine Name, nominative, and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi; (ثمّ) a conjunction; (تردّون) imperfect verb, passive, nominative, its sign of nominative being the presence of the nūn.. and the waw is an indeclinable pronoun in the position of nominative as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (إلى عالم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تردّون); (الغيب) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (الواو) conjunction; (الشهادة) conjoined to الغيب, genitive like it; (الفاء) conjunction; (ينبّئ) imperfect verb, nominative, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (الباء) a preposition; (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle [Note: Or a relative noun in the position of genitive, the clause being the ṣila (relative clause) of (ما), with the returning pronoun omitted, i.e. تعملونه.]; (كنتم) defective past verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) — indeclinable on sukūn. and (تم) a pronoun in the position of nominative as the subject (ism) of kāna, and تعلمون is like يتعذرون.
[Translator's note: «تعلمون» and «يتعذرون» in the source are evidently typographical errors for «تعملون» of the verse and «يعتذرون» at the start of this entry.]
The clause «يعتذرون إليكم ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «رجعتم إليهم» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «لا تعتذروا ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «لن نؤمن لكم» has no grammatical position, causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «قد نبّأنا اللَّه ...» has no grammatical position, giving the reason for the absence of belief and credence.
The clause «سيرى اللَّه» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause نبأنا ...
The clause «تردّون» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause سيرى اللَّه ...
The clause «ينبّئكم» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause تردّون.
The clause «كنتم تعملون» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the particle relative (ما).
The clause «تعملون» is in the position of accusative as the khabar (predicate) of كنتم.
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (ما كنتم ...) is in the position of genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (ينبّئكم).

safi-cedvel:95-95.t:
* I'rab:
(السين) a particle of the future; (يحلفون) like يستأذنون [Note: in verse (93) of this sūra.]; (باللَّه) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يحلفون); (اللام) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (يحلفون); (إذا انقلبتم إليهم) like إذا رجعتم إليهم [Note: in the previous verse (94).]; (اللام) the lām of cause (lām al-taʿlīl); (تعرضوا) imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after the lām, its sign of accusative being the dropping of the nūn.. and the waw is the fāʿil (agent); (عن) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (تعرضوا).
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن تعرضوا..) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to (يحلفون).
(الفاء) linking the answer of an implied condition; (أعرضوا) imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn.. and the waw is the fāʿil; (عنهم) like the first, attached to (أعرضوا); (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) — and (هم) a pronoun in the position of accusative as the subject (ism) of inna; (رجس) khabar (predicate) of inna, nominative (marfūʿ); (الواو) conjunction; (مأوى) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (جهنّم) khabar of the mubtadaʾ, nominative, barred from tanwīn because of being a proper name and feminine; (جزاء) mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), accusative [Note: Because His saying مأواهم جهنم contains the meaning of settling.. or it is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb.]; (بما كانوا يكسبون) like بما كنتم تعملون [Note: in the previous verse.].
The interpreted maṣdar (ما كانوا..) is in the position of genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (جزاء).
The clause «سيحلفون ...» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) [Note: It may be a badal (substitute) for the clause يعتذرون in the previous verse.
(2, 3, 4, 5) in the previous verse.].
The clause «انقلبتم ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «تعرضوا عنهم ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle relative (أن).
The clause «أعرضوا عنهم ...» is in the position of jussive as the answer to an implied condition, i.e. "if they swear to you.. then turn away ...".
The clause «إنّهم رجس ...» has no grammatical position, giving the reason for the command to turn away.
The clause «مأواهم جهنّم» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause إنّهم رجس.
The clause «كانوا يكسبون ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the particle relative (ما).
The clause «يكسبون» is in the position of accusative as the khabar of كانوا.

safi-cedvel:96-96.t:
* I'rab:
(يحلفون لكم) like سيحلفون لكم «2»; (لترضوا عنهم) like لتعرضوا عنهم «3».
(الفاء) resumptive; (إن) a conditional particle that makes the verb jussive; (ترضوا) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), its sign of jussive being the dropping of the nūn.. and the waw is the fāʿil (agent); (عنهم) like the previous one «4», attached to (mutaʿalliq) (ترضوا); (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (إنّ) like the previous one «5»; (اللَّه) the Divine Name, the subject (ism) of inna, accusative (manṣūb); (لا) negative; (يرضى) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), its sign of nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif, and the fāʿil is "huwa"; (عن القوم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يرضى); (الفاسقين) naʿt (adjective) of القوم, genitive (majrūr), its sign of genitive being the yāʾ.
The clause «يحلفون ...» has no grammatical position, a badal (substitute) for the clause سيحلفون in the previous verse.
The clause «ترضوا ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle relative (أن).
The clause «إن ترضوا ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.. and the apodosis is omitted, i.e. "your being pleased will not benefit them".
The clause «إنّ اللَّه لا يرضى..» has no grammatical position, giving the reason for the implied apodosis.
The clause «لا يرضى ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of inna.

safi-cedvel:97-97.t:
* I'rab:
(الأعراب) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ); (أشدّ) khabar (predicate), nominative; (كفرا) tamyīz (specification), accusative (manṣūb); (الواو) conjunction; (نفاقا) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the tamyīz, accusative; (الواو) conjunction; (أجدر) conjoined to أشدّ, nominative; (أن) a maṣdar-forming particle; (لا) a particle of negation; (يعلموا) imperfect verb, accusative, its sign of accusative being the dropping of the nūn.. and the waw is the fāʿil (agent); (حدود) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative; (ما) relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (أنزل) past verb; (اللَّه) the Divine Name, fāʿil, nominative; (على رسول) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أنزل), and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi.
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (ألّا يعلموا..) is in the position of genitive by an omitted bāʾ, attached to (أجدر), i.e. أجدر بألّا يعلموا ...
(الواو) resumptive; (اللَّه) the Divine Name, mubtadaʾ, nominative; (عليم) khabar, nominative; (حكيم) second khabar, nominative.
The clause «الأعراب أشدّ كفرا ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يعلموا ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «أنزل اللَّه» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «اللَّه عليم ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.

* Morphology:
(أجدر): an elative noun (ism tafḍīl) from the verb جدر يجدر of the pattern of naṣara; its wazn is أفعل, and it means "more deserving, more fitting".. al-Rāghib drew attention to the origin of its derivation, that it is from الجدار, i.e. the wall; but al-Jamal says: "What appears is that its derivation is from الجدر, i.e. the root of the tree, as though it were firm like the firmness of the root.."

safi-cedvel:98-98.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction; (من الأعراب) a preposition and its genitive noun, naʿt (adjective) of an omitted fronted khabar (predicate), i.e. "some of the Bedouins"; (من) relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject); (يتّخذ) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the fāʿil (agent) is "huwa", and it is the returning pronoun; (ما) relative, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (ينفق) like يتّخذ, and the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. ينفقه; (مغرما) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb); (الواو) conjunction; (يتربّص) like يتّخذ; (الباء) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يتربّص); (الدوائر) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (عليهم) like بكم, attached to a fronted khabar; (دائرة) delayed mubtadaʾ, nominative; (السوء) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (واللَّه سميع عليم) like اللَّه عليم حكيم [Note: in the previous verse (97).
(2, 3) in the previous verse (98).].
The clause «من الأعراب من ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause الأعراب أشدّ.. «2»
The clause «يتّخذ ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).
The clause «ينفق ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «يتربص ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يتّخذ.
The clause «عليهم دائرة ...» has no grammatical position, parenthetical, as an imprecation.
The clause «اللَّه سميع ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.

* Morphology:
(مغرما): a mīm-maṣdar from غرم يغرم of the pattern of fariḥa; its wazn is مفعل with fatḥa on the mīm and the ʿayn, because its ʿayn in the imperfect has fatḥa. (الدوائر): plural of الدائرة.. see verse (52) of Sūrat al-Māʾida.
(السوء): corruption, or a maṣdar meaning "harm"; its wazn is فعل with fatḥa on the fāʾ.

safi-cedvel:99-99.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction; (من الأعراب من يؤمن) like its counterpart «3»; (باللَّه) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يؤمن); (الواو) conjunction; (اليوم) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the Divine Name, genitive (majrūr); (الآخر) naʿt (adjective) of اليوم, genitive; (ويتّخذ ... قربات) like its counterpart «1», and the sign of accusative of قربات is the kasra; (عند) adverb, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (يتّخذ) [Note: Or attached to قربات ... or it is a naʿt of قربات.]; (اللَّه) the Divine Name, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive; (الواو) conjunction; (صلوات) conjoined to قربات, accusative, its sign of accusative being like it [Note: It may be conjoined to (ما ينفق), i.e. "and he takes the prayers of the Messenger as a means of nearness".]; (الرسول) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (ألا) a particle of alerting (tanbīh); (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) — and (ها) a pronoun in the position of accusative as the subject (ism) of inna; (قربة) khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ); (اللام) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to a naʿt of قربة; (السين) a particle of the future; (يدخل) imperfect verb, nominative; (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (اللَّه) the Divine Name, fāʿil (agent), nominative; (في رحمة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يدخل), and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi; (إنّ) like the first; (اللَّه) the Divine Name, the subject of inna, accusative; (غفور) khabar of inna, nominative; (رحيم) second khabar, nominative.
The clause «من الأعراب من يؤمن» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause من الأعراب من «4».
The clause «يؤمن ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).
The clause «يتّخذ ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يؤمن..
The clause «ينفق ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «إنّها قربة ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «سيدخلهم اللَّه ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «سيدخلهم اللَّه ...» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) or causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «أنّ اللَّه غفور ...» has no grammatical position, causal.

* Morphology:
(قربات): plural of قربة, a noun for that by which one draws near to Allah the Exalted; its wazn is فعلة with ḍamma then sukūn, or with two ḍammas; and the wazn of قربات is فعلات with two ḍammas only.

* Benefits:
(عند) and its states. In this verse comes His saying, Exalted is He, وَيَتَّخِذُ ما يُنْفِقُ قُرُباتٍ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ, and (عند) in this verse is an adverb of place attached to an omitted adjective of (قربات), its implied form being (قربات كائنة عند اللَّه). We shall clarify below some new points which often escape the student; Ibn Hishām set them out in al-Mughnī, saying:
1- It is a noun for physical presence, as in His saying, Exalted is He, فَلَمَّا رَآهُ مُسْتَقِرًّا عِنْدَهُ, and for abstract presence, as in His saying, Exalted is He: قالَ الَّذِي عِنْدَهُ عِلْمٌ مِنَ الْكِتابِ; and it conveys nearness, as in His saying, Exalted is He, عِنْدَ سِدْرَةِ الْمُنْتَهى عِنْدَها جَنَّةُ الْمَأْوى.
2- It occurs only as an adverb or genitive by من; the common people's saying ذهبت إلى عنده is a solecism (laḥn, i.e. an error). It comes as an adverb of place, as in the noble verse, and it comes for time, such as (الصبر عند الصدمة الأولى) and (جئت عند طلوع الفجر).
3- There are two words that come with the meaning of (عند), namely:
a- لدى: absolutely, as in His saying, Exalted is He, إِذِ الْقُلُوبُ لَدَى الْحَناجِرِ، وَأَلْفَيا سَيِّدَها لَدَى الْبابِ، وَما كُنْتَ لَدَيْهِمْ إِذْ يَخْتَصِمُونَ.
b- لدن: it comes when the place is the beginning of an extent, such as جئت من لدنه. عند and لدن come together in His saying, Exalted is He: آتَيْناهُ رَحْمَةً مِنْ عِنْدِنا وَعَلَّمْناهُ مِنْ لَدُنَّا عِلْماً. عند and لدن can be made genitive, whereas (لدى) cannot be made genitive.

safi-cedvel:100-100.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (السابقون) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ), its sign of nominative being the waw; (الأولون) naʿt (adjective) of the mubtadaʾ, nominative, its sign of nominative being the waw [Note: Or it is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, i.e. "the forerunners are the first of the people of the religion", and the clause رضي اللَّه is a resumption.]; (من المهاجرين) a preposition and its genitive noun, ḥāl (circumstantial) from the mubtadaʾ [Note: Or it is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ.], its sign of genitive being the yāʾ; (الواو) conjunction; (الأنصار) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to المهاجرين, genitive (majrūr); (الواو) conjunction; (الذين) relative, in the position of genitive, conjoined to المهاجرين; (اتّبعوا) past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma.. and the waw is the fāʿil (agent), and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), referring back to the Muhājirūn and the Anṣār; (بإحسان) a preposition and its genitive noun, ḥāl from the fāʿil of اتّبعوهم; (رضي) past verb; (اللَّه) the Divine Name, fāʿil, nominative; (عن) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (رضي); (الواو) conjunction; (رضوا) like اتّبعوا; (عنه) like عنهم, attached to (رضوا); (الواو) conjunction; (أعدّ) like رضي, and the fāʿil is "huwa"; (لهم) like عنهم, attached to (أعدّ); (جنّات) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb), its sign of accusative being the kasra; (تجري) imperfect verb, nominative, its sign of nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ; (تحت) adverb of place, accusative, attached to (تجري), and (ها) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الأنهار) fāʿil of تجري, nominative; (خالدين ... الفوز العظيم) its i'rab has been given [Note: in verse (89) of this sūra.].
The clause «السابقون الأولون ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive [Note: Or conjoined by the waw to an earlier resumptive clause.].
The clause «اتّبعوهم ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «رضي اللَّه عنهم» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (السابقون).
The clause «رضوا عنه» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause رضي اللَّه.
The clause «أعدّ ...» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause رضي اللَّه.
[Translator's note: The source reads «لا محلّ رفع», evidently a slip for «في محلّ رفع» ("in the position of nominative").]
The clause «تجري ... الأنهار» is in the position of accusative as a naʿt of جنّات.
The clause «ذلك الفوز ...» has no grammatical position, being in effect causal.

* Morphology:
(السابقون): plural of السابق, active participle of the three-letter verb سبق; its wazn is فاعل.
(المهاجرين): plural of المهاجر, active participle of the four-letter verb هاجر; its wazn is مفاعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.

* Benefits:
السَّابِقُونَ الْأَوَّلُونَ: The scholars differed about "the first forerunners". Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, Qatāda, Ibn Sīrīn and a group said: they are those who prayed toward the القلبتين. ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ said: they are the people of Badr. Al-Shaʿbī said: they are the people of the Pledge of Riḍwān at al-Ḥudaybiya. Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Quraẓī said: they are all the Companions, because precedence was attained by them through companionship with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant him peace.
[Translator's note: «القلبتين» is evidently a typographical error for «القبلتين», "the two qiblas".]
The scholars differed about the first person to embrace Islam, after agreeing that Khadīja was the first of creation to embrace Islam and the first to pray with the Messenger, may Allah bless him and his family and grant him peace. Some scholars said: The first to believe after Khadīja was ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib; this is the view of Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh. It was said that he embraced Islam at ten years old, and it was said less than that. Some of them said: The first to embrace Islam after Khadīja was Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, may Allah be pleased with him; this is narrated from ʿAlī, and it is the view of Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Nakhaʿī and al-Shaʿbī. Al-Zuhrī and ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr said:
The first to embrace Islam after Khadīja was Zayd ibn Ḥāritha, the freedman of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant him peace. Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm al-Ḥanẓalī used to reconcile these narrations, saying: The first to embrace Islam among men was Abū Bakr, among women Khadīja, among boys ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, and among slaves Zayd ibn Ḥāritha, may Allah the Exalted be pleased with them.

safi-cedvel:101-102.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction; (من) a preposition; (من) relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a fronted khabar (predicate); (حول) adverb of place, accusative (manṣūb), attached to the omitted ṣila (relative clause) of من, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (من الأعراب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the relative; (منافقون) delayed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ), its sign of nominative being the waw; (الواو) conjunction; (من أهل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to what ممّن is attached to, so it is a khabar conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the first [Note: Or it is a fronted khabar of a delayed mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "a people who persisted".]; (المدينة) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (مردوا) past verb, indeclinable on ḍamma.. and the waw is the fāʿil (agent); (على النفاق) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (مردوا); (لا) negative; (تعلم) imperfect verb, nominative, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "anta"; (نحن) a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ; (نعلمهم) like تعلمهم, and the fāʿil is "naḥnu", and the second object is implied, i.e. "We know them to be hypocrites"; (السين) a particle of the future; (نعذّبهم) like تعلمهم, and the fāʿil is "naḥnu"; (مرّتين) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, accusative, its sign of accusative being the yāʾ; (ثمّ) a conjunction; (يردّون) imperfect verb, passive, nominative.. and the waw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (إلى عذاب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يردّون); (عظيم) naʿt (adjective) of عذاب, genitive.
The clause «ممّن ... منافقون» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause in the previous verse.
The clause «مردوا ...» has no grammatical position, a resumption confirming the content of what preceded [Note: It may be in the position of nominative as a naʿt of (منافقون).. or it is a naʿt of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "a people", and the khabar is the preposition and its genitive noun before it (من أهل المدينة); the conjoining then becomes a conjoining of clauses.].
The clause «لا تعلمهم» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the fāʿil of مردوا [Note: Or in the position of nominative as a second naʿt of (منافقون).].
The clause «نحن نعلمهم» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «نعلمهم» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of نحن.
The clause «سنعذّبهم ...» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption.
The clause «يردّون ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause سنعذّبهم.
(الواو) conjunction; (آخرون) conjoined to (منافقون), nominative [Note: in the previous verse (101).. and it may be a mubtadaʾ qualified by the clause (اعترفوا), its khabar being the clause خلطوا.], its sign of nominative being the waw; (اعترفوا) like مردوا; (بذنوب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (اعترفوا), and (هم) muḍāf ilayhi; (خلطوا) like مردوا; (عملا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (صالحا) naʿt, accusative; (الواو) conjunction; (آخر) conjoined to (عملا), accusative, barred from tanwīn because it is an adjective on the wazn أفعل; (سيّئا) naʿt of آخر, accusative; (عسى) a frozen (jāmid), defective past verb — an abrogator (nāsikh); (الله) the Divine Name, the subject (ism) of ʿasā, nominative; (أن) a maṣdar-forming particle; (يتوب) imperfect verb, accusative by أن, and the fāʿil is "huwa"; (على) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (يتوب).
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن يتوب) is in the position of accusative as the khabar of ʿasā.
(إنّ) a particle resembling the verb — an abrogator; (الله) the Divine Name, the subject of inna, accusative; (غفور) khabar of inna, nominative; (رحيم) second khabar, nominative.
The clause «اعترفوا ...» is in the position of nominative as a naʿt of (آخرون).
The clause «خلطوا ...» is in the position of nominative as a second naʿt of (آخرون) [Note: Or it is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ آخرون.].
The clause «عسى الله ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يتوب ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the particle relative.
The clause «إنّ الله غفور» has no grammatical position, causal (taʿlīliyya).

* Morphology:
(سيّئا): a derived adjective from ساء يسوء; its wazn is فيعل, and it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by conversion. Its origin is سيوئ, with sukūn on the yāʾ and the waw vowelled with kasra; when the yāʾ and the waw came together, the first being quiescent, the waw was changed to yāʾ and assimilated into the first, so it became سيّئا.

safi-cedvel:103-103.t:
* I'rab:
